Enzo Maresca has said it is “normal” that Elliot Anderson described Manchester City as the “kings of Manchester” in a swipe at Manchester United.

The midfielder was a Manchester United target before joining City for £116m in the summer and marked his arrival by saying his new club were the monarchs of Manchester.

Manager Maresca cited City’s success in the last decade-and-a-half, when they have won eight Premier League titles, to support why Anderson, 23, would think that.

Maresca, 46, admitted United were the superior force in the city before that but said: “Probably the reason Elliot said that is that he grew up in the last 15 years when Manchester City was unbelievable [with] what they achieved. So it is normal when Elliot said that then if you go back it is a different picture, but for me the reason Elliot said that was when he grew up Manchester City was dominant.”

Maresca will lead City in a Manchester derby for the first time at Old Trafford on Sunday when Nico O’Reilly will be fit to return for his side, though Jeremy Doku is again absent with injury.

City, who beat Porto 2-0 on Tuesday, have had two more days to prepare than United, who played on Thursday as they defeated Sabah 4-0 in the Champions League.

United head coach Michael Carrick said the situation was “not ideal” but Maresca harked back to last season, when City faced Napoli on a Thursday in their opening Champions League game and then travelled to Arsenal to play on the subsequent Sunday.

Maresca said: “It happened exactly the same last year when the club played Napoli and then after two days played Arsenal. Sometimes it happens in football. I don't have any doubt that Man United are going to be ready for that. I think that happens and you need to adapt. It happened last year with us, this season with them, next season it will happen with a different team.”

News.title: ‘Just in case I die, IPP killed me’: The harrowing warning of prisoner trapped on indefinite jail term
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Inside a cell at on a wing for vulnerable inmates in Lancashire, Wayne Gregory left a message smeared in blood on the wall for the prison officers who found him: “Just in case I die, IPP killed me.”

He had also hidden a note written in biro on his upper thigh for those who examined him at the morgue, begging the coroner to investigate his detention on an Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence.

Although he survived, the disturbing incident was just one of a series of horrifying acts of self-harm which have marked the latter half of his 19 years trapped on an indefinite jail term with no release date in sight.

His face and body, now irrevocably scarred by serious injuries which he regularly reopens, are evidence of the devastating toll the uncertain punishment has taken on him.

He is one of almost 2,300 IPP prisoners still languishing on the open-ended jail terms, which were scrapped in 2012 and have been which has been described as “psychological torture” by the United Nations.

Hundreds like Gregory have unravelled during the punishment, including Carl Lamb, who cut off his own ear, and Thomas White, who set himself alight in desperation. At least 96 prisoners have taken their own lives in despair.

open image in gallery Wayne Gregory, who was sentenced to less than three years but has served almost 20, has repeatedly injured his own face in prison ( Supplied )

Last month, the prime minister announced he would finally end the injustice of the IPP sentence before the end of this parliament, bringing hope to thousands of such prisoners for the first time in two decades.

However, details of how the scandal will be addressed, including how complex inmates will be supported towards release, have not yet been decided.

Gregory, currently held at medium security HMP Garth, said he was “happy” at the news and the “end is in sight”, but revealed he was still struggling after years of self-harming.

When he was jailed in 2007, Gregory was told he must serve a minimum of two years and 275 days for a violent and serious attack he carried out with his brother, who was also handed an IPP sentence with the same tariff.

But while his brother was freed eight years ago and has rebuilt his life in the community, Gregory – whose anxiety means he struggles to complete the rehabilitative prison courses needed to secure his release by the parole board – has been left to languish.

His feelings of despair and frustration have spiralled into a devastating cycle of self-harm and destructive behaviour, which have prevented him from passing the parole board’s release test.

Now aged 42, he is battling to earn a place at a secure hospital where he hopes to start recovering, but, shockingly, he has been told he cannot be transferred to the medium secure unit until he stops self-harming.

“My brother has been released… and fitted back into society with no issues and started a family, whereas I’m covered in scars, frustrated, angry, institutionalised and suffering from crippling anxiety of groups of people developed over this sentence,” he told The Independent.

He said he turned to increasingly extreme self-harm as a “direct result” of the jail term.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has pledged to end the injustice of IPP sentences ( PA )

Gregory grew up in multiple care homes and foster placements before getting into trouble with the law as a teenager, receiving his first conviction at 15, before he was eventually handed an IPP sentence for wounding with intent in a joint attack on an extended family member when he was 23.

Both he and his brother were refused parole at their first hearing in 2011, but two years later his brother progressed to a Category D open prison while he was told to do more courses.

“I couldn’t understand why I couldn’t progress when my brother had, even though I was trying my hardest to complete anything asked of me,” he explained.

He first mutilated his own face in 2015, in what he describes as a “major cry for help”, which saw him inflict a serious wound to the right side of his mouth and cheek.

He warned staff at the prison he was going to start “chopping myself to bits” before he inflicted the wound, telling them: “It feels like I'm never ever gonna get out of this. So why do I give a s*** what I look like now? Nobody's gonna see me anyway.”

“I honestly felt at this point that I was in an endless pit of despair and I was telling everyone this,” he added.

Around a year later, he caused a similar injury to the left side of his face, having failed to complete a three-year course due to his struggles with group therapy.

open image in gallery Almost 2,300 IPP prisoners are in jail without a release date, long after the sentence was abolished ( PA Archive )

He believes his anxiety during group courses has seriously hampered his ability to progress in prison, adding that although officials know he needs one-to-one support, he has been told there are no resources to provide this.

Although he was briefly transferred to an open prison at HMP Leyhill in 2023, he was returned to a closed prison within a matter of weeks after he self-harmed again.

In 2024, he was considered for a placement in a 15-bed registered care home for men with complex needs, including substance misuse issues and mental health challenges.

However, this offer was withdrawn shortly before his parole hearing after Gregory started speaking out about his IPP sentence and first made contact with The Independent. According to documents in his parole dossier, the option of placement at the site operated by the Langley Trust was withdrawn because of the risk of negative publicity.

A spokesperson for the Langley Trust said: “We are unable to confirm or deny any connection with any named individuals, as we are required by law to protect our clients' information.”

Gregory is now hoping to join a major habeas corpus legal challenge brought against the government after the United Nations found a number of over-tariff IPP prisoners are being arbitrarily detained under international human rights law.

Gregory pleaded “when will it end”, adding: “I just cannot live like this.”

open image in gallery Carl Lamb, pictured as a child, has never been released from his IPP jail term ( Supplied )

Other prisoners have resorted to extremes, including Carl Lamb, who cut off his own ear with a razor blade in front of a prison officer in protest at his IPP sentence.

He was jailed with a tariff of one year, seven months and 25 days in 2006 for grievous bodily harm with intent following a road rage incident when he was 26. Now 46, he has never been released.

His brother Danny Eggar, 38, said he had watched his mental health severely deteriorate over the last decade, including some shocking acts of self harm and inflicting the injury to his ear in 2020.

“For me, it’s not the physical scars, it’s what it’s done to him mentally,” he told The Independent. “My brother is not the same person that I knew 10 years ago. He had his life taken away from him.”

He described the uncertainty of not having a release date as “mental torture”, adding: “It’s an absolutely inhumane prison sentence.”

Lamb, currently held at HMP Woodhill in Milton Keynes, said he feels hopeful for the first time in “many years” after hearing the prime minister’s pledge to finally end the injustice.

He told The Independent: “A lot of people suffered deeply because of this sentence. I've been around seen many prisoners in dark places – the suffering really can’t go on. What a joy it would be if the sentence was ended for people.”

open image in gallery IPP prisoner Thomas White with his son Kayden, aged just ten months ( Margaret White )

The Independent previously revealed how Thomas White, who has served more than 14 years for stealing a mobile phone, set himself alight and later smashed his face on the floor in desperation.

His family spent six years campaigning for his transfer to a hospital after his mental health deteriorated on the jail term. However, he has now been returned to Category B HMP Gartree, without a release date, after just ten months of care.

His devastated sister, pastor Clara White, called for a clear timeline for how the government will end the injustice for IPP prisoners.

"My brother has served more than seven times the punishment that the court originally considered appropriate,” she said. “He is a severely unwell man who needs treatment, stability and hope. Instead, he is being sent back to prison with no release date and no certainty about what his future holds.

“Andy Burnham’s pledge to resolve the IPP injustice is a welcome first step but we now need a clear timeline and plan from the government."

Justice secretary Alex Norris said the government will table legislation to end the IPP sentence “once and for all” by the end of this parliament.

“These are complex cases, and some of these offenders have committed serious crimes,”he told the commons last week.

“Public safety will always be my top priority, and we must balance that with fairness. It will take time to get this right, but work will begin immediately, and on a cross-party basis.”

A cross-party oversight group will help to guide this, including the architect of the flawed sentence, Lord David Blunkett, and former justice secretary Robert Buckland, who have both called for IPP reform.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), email jo@samaritans.org, or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

Oasis have confirmed the date of an upcoming tour announcement by using a drone light show in Manchester.

Taking place over the Joie Stadium, home to Manchester City Women at the Etihad Campus on Thursday night, the display lit up the band’s logo before replacing it with the date 14/09/26 and the time 4pm BST.

The band, who reformed for the successful Live ’25 tour last year following their split in 2009, have recently been dropping hints about potential tour venues across social media channels.

Liam and Noel Gallagher discussed their reunion in the new documentary Oasis: Don’t Look Back In Anger, which was released on Wednesday.

Written by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight, the project is part concert film and part documentary, following the band on their reunion tour that began in Cardiff in July last year.

It also features the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years following their 2009 split.

open image in gallery A drone light show over the Joie Stadium football ground at the Etihad Campus in Manchester, revealing the time and date of the forthcoming Oasis tour announcement ( PA )

Other possible locations the band have hinted at include the Etihad Stadium, Celtic Park and Knebworth – where they played to 250,000 people in 1996 during their Britpop heyday.

Rumours of a follow-up to the Manchester rockers’ 2025 reunion tour have been rife in recent weeks, but no dates or venues had been formally announced prior to Thursday’s display.

Even before the 2025 tour concluded, fans predicted that Oasis would be keen to get back out on the road again, given the run of shows were a defining cultural event – as well as a very lucrative one.

Oasis Live ‘25 was estimated by Forbes to have generated over $400m (£293m) in revenue, with Noel and Liam each pocketing between $50m-$100m. As a result, the pair cracked the Sunday Times Rich List this year with a combined net worth of $375m.

Contrary to tabloid media reports, sources told The Independent that the mood backstage during Oasis’s 2025 reunion was jubilant, with both Noel and Liam in great spirits as their famous friends – from football stars to pop singers, including Manchester City star Jack Grealish and the Happy Mondays’ Shaun Ryder – rubbed elbows.

open image in gallery Oasis made history when brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher put an end to their years-long feud and reunited onstage for the first time in almost 16 years to play a record-breaking world tour ( Getty )

“It’s been a proper love-in backstage,” one source said. “There’s a friends and family bar which is basically free booze – Guinness on draft (of course) (sic), beer, wine and champagne. It’s like going to a wedding every night.”

Sources have also said that Noel has been writing new music – it remains to be seen if this will emerge in the shape of the first Oasis album since 2008’s Dig Out Your Soul, with Liam on vocal duties.

The band have had eight UK number one singles and eight UK number one albums, with “Wonderwall”, “Don’t Look Back In Anger” and “Roll With It” among their best-known hits.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has failed to respond to a request to appear before the United States House Judiciary Committee or supply documents sought by one of its members more than a month after the deadline passed, the Press Association understands.

Democrat Jamie Raskin, the committee's ranking minority member, wrote to Infantino on 26 July announcing an investigation into "a sustained campaign" by Fifa to curry favour with US president Donald Trump.

The letter stated that attempts to gain favours extended to dropping high-profile corruption cases, while also accusing Fifa of "gouging" American consumers with "exorbitant" ticket prices for the World Cup this summer.

The Swiss official was asked to reply by 9 August, produce the requested files, and contact the committee to arrange an interview. However, it is understood that no response whatsoever had been received by Thursday.

As no subpoena was issued, Infantino faces no criminal penalties for ignoring Raskin’s request.

open image in gallery Infantino is yet to respond to Raskin’s requests ( Reuters )

Nevertheless, Fifa is facing a growing backlog of demands for answers on multiple fronts.

Two days after Raskin sent his letter, The Times and the Financial Times detailed Infantino’s plan to seek private investment for a new company, Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), created to manage commercial and operational arms of the World Cup and other Fifa tournaments.

The scheme was promptly rejected by three continental confederations, leading Infantino to withdraw it on 1 August. However, his management of the proposal has intensified pressure on his position, with Uefa declaring it had "lost confidence" in him as president. Infantino has promised a review into how the FFE project was handled, though Fifa has not revealed who will conduct it.

Uefa has called for an independent, external review into the FFE initiative and is seeking document disclosure through the US legal system, with a view to potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland.

Meanwhile, the Belgian football association (RBFA) is understood to be continuing legal action regarding the suspension of a one-match ban for US forward Folarin Balogun, which enabled him to play against Belgium in a World Cup last-16 fixture in July.

Infantino remains intent on seeking re-election for a further four-year term next March. He is presently the sole candidate, although Uefa stated on 27 August that it would work to offer a credible alternative contender.

Candidacies must be submitted by the deadline of November 18.

The presidents of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which represents nations across North and Central America and the Caribbean, joined Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin in denouncing Infantino’s "deception" over the FFE plan in an open letter on August 10.

Even so, Infantino continues to retain support within Asia. On Thursday, he met with the presidents of the Kuwaiti and Iraqi football associations, adding to backing already pledged by other Middle Eastern nations including Lebanon, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

open image in gallery Jamie Raskin has launched an investigation into Fifa's relationship with Trump ( Getty )

Within Concacaf, Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have also broken ranks to support him.

Separately, Fifa is expected to receive an analysis on Friday assessing the feasibility of expanding the World Cup to 64 teams.

A research document seen on 30 July set a 14 August deadline to appoint an agency to conduct the study, with the final analysis requested by 11 September.

Fifa has not commented on the document, but a proposal to consider expanding the 2030 finals has the backing of South American confederation Conmebol.

Under current plans, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will host one game each at the start of the centenary tournament, before the remainder of the competition is co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

Eddie Hearn insists Dana White is “out of the picture” concerning Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury after being accused of sabotaging the fight as talks shift towards Cardiff as a potential venue.

The promoters and fighters have hit a wall in negotiations over a number of issues in recent weeks with broadcasting partner Netflix eager for the fight to take place in the United States to better capture the American market.

But with the original signed contract stating the location would be in the United Kingdom, Hearn and Joshua have pushed back on the proposed change of plan, seeking an addendum to better compensate themselves and avoid losses.

But UFC and Zuffa Boxing supremo White took another swipe in his ongoing feud with Hearn on Thursday night ahead of Ryan Garcia v Conor Benn, claiming that he has “never seen somebody do more damage to a fight.”

White also warned that talks could collapse to end the prospect of the two biggest names in British boxing this century, adding that partners could “walk away” and accept a stalemate in negotiations.

“We're literally right f***ing there [at the point of ending talks and the prospect of the fight taking place],” White told IFL TV. “It gets to the point where it's silly now. Let's f***ing fight, right?”

And a bullish White continues to insist, “it’ll be me,” when asked who is the promoter of the highly-anticipated fight, but Hearn is adamant he is not part of the event at all.

open image in gallery Dana White speaks during a press conference for Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn ( AP )

Hearn told The Independent: “Unfortunately for Dana he has now realised two things. 1. He has nothing to do with the fight, 2. Joshua signed a contract to fight in the U.K. and that’s where he wants the fight to happen.

“Now that Dana is out of the picture we are moving forward with Netflix and SELA to find a suitable date in the U.K. We have a signed legally binding contract to fight Tyson Fury in the U.K. and we have not backed down from that position.

“Still some work to do, but hopefully some incredible news coming for British fight fans soon... keep your fingers crossed.”

With Hearn adamant the fight should not take place at Madison Square Garden in New York, The Times reported that Cardiff and the Principality Stadium has been floated as an alternative, with its roof able to assist with the colder conditions of a British winter in November or December.

But despite the prospect of lifting a curfew that could block the fight taking place at Wembley at a peak US time, the prospect of the fight taking place in the early hours of 21 November could be complicated by the Welsh rugby team’s planned test match with Australia just hours later with a 8:10pm GMT kick-off.

News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. News.title: West Nile virus hits Europe as temperatures climb
News.content:
“The future looks rosy for West Nile virus and other mosquito-borne viruses that follow it to the New World,” wrote the science writer Carl Zimmer in his 2011 book ‘Planet of Viruses’.

“That’s because the future is going to be warm and wet.”

More than a decade on, and after a record-setting hot summer, Mr Zimmer’s prediction has come to pass: the mosquito-borne disease, once confined mostly to the warmest parts of Africa, has become firmly entrenched in Europe, experts have warned.

At least 1,086 locally acquired cases of West Nile virus have been recorded across the continent over the last three months, as mosquitoes continue their slow march northwards.

The insects – which are cold-blooded – need warm weather to accelerate their life cycles and survive long enough to spread disease.

Across July and August, countries including Italy, Spain and France recorded West Nile cases in previously unaffected regions and cities, while others, including the Netherlands, recorded their first deaths from the virus this summer.

“I don’t think there are any more ‘tropical viruses’... the geographic barrier of these viruses no longer exists because of climate change,” said Dr Krishanthi Subramaniam, a microbiology lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

News.title: Britain pioneers new dried blood products for the modern battlefield
News.content:
A powdered blood product that can be mixed with water and used in minutes could help solve the challenges of treating severely wounded soldiers on hard-to-reach battlefields.

Britain is rethinking how to get blood to soldiers on the frontline, in the latest sign that the war in Ukraine has forced Western militaries to reconsider assumptions about modern combat medicine that had held since Iraq and Afghanistan.

The product, known as “spray-dried plasma”, is made by turning liquid plasma – the clotting-rich component of blood – into a stable powder that can be stored at room temperature for years before being rehydrated with water when needed.

“Plasma is vital for saving soldiers in war zones,” said Dr Ian Nesbitt, a former military anaesthetist and Faculty Lead for Anaesthesia at the David Nott Foundation, which trains doctors working in conflict zones.

“It helps blood clot when someone is injured. But in war zones, getting plasma to soldiers is incredibly complicated. It’s actually the logistics of it that are a real problem in maintaining a reliable supply of fresh frozen plasma for acutely injured patients.”

The NHS and the UK Ministry of Defence signed a strategic partnership this summer to jointly develop new blood products for frontline soldiers, focusing on dried plasma.

The agreement formalises work under way with a biotechnology company called Velico Medical. If successful, it will be used in future battlefields like the one in Ukraine.

“The war in Ukraine has woken up all countries, not just the UK,” Professor Renata Gomes, Chief Scientific Officer at NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT), told The Telegraph.

News.title: Mosquitoes are evolving to evade bed nets – but there may be a solution
News.content:
In Papua’s low-lying mangrove swamps and dense tropical rainforests, mosquitoes have always got to work early.

Here, the disease-ridden insects begin feeding in the early evening as people socialise and children play. It’s a characteristic that’s hampered malaria control efforts, because it has rendered bed nets less effective. People are bitten before they climb under the netting to sleep.

It’s also part of the reason that Indonesian Papua remains one of Asia’s most persistent malaria hotspots. Last year, cases across the country jumped by 30 per cent, to 706,000 new infections. The vast majority, roughly 90 per cent, were reported in Papua’s six provinces.

The same pattern is now emerging in parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where mosquitoes used to bite mostly at night and where the rollout of insecticide-treated bed nets is estimated to have averted 450 million malaria cases between 2000 and 2015, according to modelling in Nature journal.

A number of studies suggest mosquitoes in Africa are evolving in response to the mass rollout of bed nets, biting earlier in the evening, or later in the morning. In some cases, species which already did this have become more dominant, while others are adapting their habits.

“We’re battling evolution. And right now, we’re losing,” said Prof Neil Lobo, a research professor in the Eck Institute for Global Health at the University of Notre Dame.

“Mosquitoes are adapting. They’re biting outdoors, they’re biting earlier in the evening when people aren’t under their nets, and they’re becoming resistant to the insecticides we use. So we’re reaching the limits of what bed nets alone can do,” he told The Telegraph.

But there may be a solution.

NEWCASTLE “were always clear” with Manchester United that Lewis Hall’s “future was with us”.

Though Toon legend Alan Shearer claims the 22-year-old’s new long-term deal will not matter if decides to leave.



The Mags stressed keeping Hall from United’s clutches was just as important as appointing Eddie Howe’s successor after confirming his extension.

Despite a huge summer of change with boss Howe leaving alongside star names Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon, Newcastle told United in July there was no chance of Hall going too.



The England international is “absolutely delighted” to end speculation over his future by penning a five-year contract, making him one of the top earners at St. James’.

Sporting director Ross Wilson, who has also tied-down Lewis Miley and Sven Botman to extensions, said: “We were always clear that his future was with us, and in the context of our business this summer, retaining him and extending his contract was right up there in terms of importance.”

But United still view Hall as Luke Shaw’s successor and are set to return with another attempt to sign him next summer.

And Newcastle’s record goalscorer Shearer says the star’s contract will mean nothing if his heart is set on Old Trafford.

The former striker, who famously rejected moves to United TWICE in the 90s, told Betfair: “It’s great news for Newcastle that Lewis Hall has signed a new long-term deal.

“There is always going to be interest in top players and he’s a top left back. There’s not many good ones around and Newcastle have got a really good one, so I understand why other clubs were sniffing around him in the transfer window.

Sports.title: Manchester United might have already made their Benjamin Sesko decision
Sports.content:
WITH 12 goals in 20 appearances this calendar year, Benjamin Sesko is gradually developing into a dependable goalscorer for Manchester United.

Sesko marked his first start since May 3 with a second goal in as many games in United’s Champions League opener against Sabah, providing coach Michael Carrick with a conundrum.



Thirteen of Carrick’s 21 games in charge of United have been without Sesko in the starting line-up and the record is favourable. United won eight and drew three last term.

But Sesko sprung off the bench to score winners in two and an equaliser before his fourth ‘super sub’ goal at Everton last week. United missed Sesko at Hull and Everton in their first away games this term.



As a £73million signing, ‘super sub’ is not a nickname Sesko entertains. But he may be back on the bench against Manchester City on Sunday.

Carrick agreed: “He definitely offers a different kind of threat. I think that’s kind of the beauty of it, really, that we know what Ben gives us.



“And there’s not many around that kind of give you what Ben does in terms of his physique, his physicality, playing on the last line, his speed to run in behind. He’s a real threat.

“It’s great to have him back at this level after working to get back fitness. So, a couple of goals and good performances, good minutes in him.

“So really pleased with the way he’s gone.”

Sesko, 22, missed the entirety of United’s six-game pre-season schedule as he recovered from a shin injury he aggravated when pushed off the Old Trafford pitch by Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That accounted for Sesko’s managed-minutes against Hull and Ipswich before his impact at Everton, where he lashed in the winner last season.

With roughly 68 hours between kick-off against Sabah on Thursday evening and the derby on Sunday afternoon, Carrick possibly decided on his weekend side before the Champions League anthem blared around Old Trafford.

Particularly given the competition. Bruno Fernandes slotted in his fourth of the campaign against Sabah while Matheus Cunha also got off the mark.

Bryan Mbeumo is already on two goals and Marcus Rashford impressed in his starts against Ipswich Town and Everton.

Rashford was unused against Sabah, having come off at Everton with an unspecified issue. His rest would signpost a recall at the weekend.



After Carrick decided on Shea Lacey and Harry Amass as United’s final substitutes on Thursday night, he offered Rashford some fleeting words of reassurance at the end of his warm-up.

It was possibly, “I’ll need you Sunday”, or words to that effect.

The 28-year-old scored on his last derby appearance at the Etihad in March 2024, before his dramatic demotion at the same stadium nine months later.



For Rashford, starting against City would be a chance to exorcise the demons. His absence from Ruben Amorim’s squad in December 2024 seemed to signal the end of his United career.

Sports.title: Arteta: I sabotaged our travel plans so players get used to problems
Sports.content:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says he deliberately sabotaged the club's travel plans during pre-season - to get his players used to difficulties on the road.

Those sabotages include deliberately making his team late for matches by changing their route or meal times - as well as making the changing room hotter and reducing the number of massage beds.

The Premier League champions had travel concerns during their trip to face Napoli in the Champions League during midweek, caused by the Air Traffic Control crisis on Tuesday.

Arsenal were due to fly out of Luton Airport at around 3pm UK time on Tuesday, but delays meant they arrived in the Italian city around three hours behind schedule.

When asked if his players were affected by that, Arteta revealed he prepared his players by creating difficult scenarios during pre-season games.

"I love those challenges. I tried to create them in pre-season!" said Arteta. "So when they happen, we know how to experience them and we already know.

Image: Arteta has made his Arsenal team late for pre-season matches so they can prepare for games

"Get to the stadium very late, change the routine so the players have to do something else. When it happens, and it can: the flight can be cancelled, or the train is delayed, there is so much traffic, I don't want the players and staff panicking.

"When that happens, adapt to it. We have two or three hours on the plane - can we use it? Play together, spend some time together, sleep.

"But don't complain or use it as an excuse because it's not helpful at all."

Asked what he has done, Arteta replied: "Just delaying the meals, delaying the transport, taking a different route. We've done many things.

"Make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kinds of things because we're going to have to adapt to different contexts. And we will try to anticipate this and adapt to difficult conditions.

"When there's no element of surprise or stress on a matchday, I think it's important."

Pickpockets, lightbulbs - what else has Arteta done to Arsenal players?

Image: Arteta has done several quirky tactics on the Arsenal training ground before

Arteta gained similar headlines last year when it was revealed he tasked his former head of sports science and performance Tom Allen to hire a pickpocket to steal from his own players during an evening meal.

The pickpocket was disguised as a waiter during the meal - and after the dinner, Arteta held a pre-match team meeting where at the end, he presented his players' stolen items at the front of the room.

That ploy was in preparation for a match against a team who tried every possible tactic to gain an edge - and Arteta wanted to adopt a 'pickpocket mentality', to always be aware of people trying to steal advantages from them.

The Amazon Prime documentary All or Nothing also unveiled some more quirky Arteta tactics. Arsenal were due to play Liverpool at Anfield for the first time with fans back in the ground, so Arteta blasted out 'You'll Never Walk Alone' on loudspeakers during training, so his players could get used to the surroundings.

For another game, this time at home, Arteta also did a pre-match team talk involving a lightbulb - as he wanted his players to shine and emit energy and light to one another.

Sports.title: Hall signs new deal at Newcastle after Man Utd interest
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall has signed a new long-term contract at Newcastle United.

The England international has committed to a new deal at St James' Park despite Manchester United showing an interest in him during the summer transfer window following the departure of several other key players from the club.

The 22-year-old left-back joined the Magpies from Chelsea in August 2023 and since made 107 appearances for the club, including playing in every round of their successful 2024/25 Carabao Cup campaign - their first domestic trophy in 70 years - only to miss the final with injury.

Hall says the new deal comes as a proud moment.

He told the club's website: "I'm absolutely delighted. It's a really proud moment. It's an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters. I know how much it means to them.

"The fanbase and the support we get here, whether it's at St. James' Park or away, it's the best in the league in my opinion. To be able to bring joy to their faces, it's a big thing for me.

"I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all. One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United.

Image: Lewis Hall joined the Magpies from Chelsea in Sept 2023

"It's a really good place to be. It's really pleasing with how we've started the season, especially with the new gaffer and coaching staff coming in, and I think we can go on to achieve really big things."

Hall has played every single minute this season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle, including three Premier League games and both wins in the Carabao Cup.

Jaissle said: "I have been impressed with Lewis since I arrived. He is a very important player for us and for what we are building here, so this is exciting news.

"The combination of his ability and his profile make him an ideal fit for our squad, and his mentality is exactly what you want in a young player. He wants to learn every day and he wants to be better in every match.

"Lewis covers ground in a way that few players can. He defends with maturity and intelligence, and his technical level means he can support the team higher up the pitch.

"What excites me most is that I believe the best is still to come from Lewis. He has a lot of room to develop, and I am looking forward to working with him as he grows with us."

Sports.title: Merson: Spurs, Man City and Man Utd have defining games this weekend
Sports.content:
In his latest Sky Sports column, Paul Merson says Tottenham, Manchester City and Manchester United all have defining matches this weekend, even though it is early in the season.

Spurs are still without a win or a goal in the Premier League after three games and will play against an unbeaten Everton team on Saturday Night Football, live on Sky Sports, in front of their expectant fans.

Meanwhile on Sunday, the Manchester derby takes place as Michael Carrick's inconsistent United team take on a City side facing their first big test in the post-Pep Guardiola era.

Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts on two massive fixtures...

'Everton is a cup final for Spurs'

Spurs have to beat Everton this weekend. It's a cup final for them - I'd go as far as to say this is their season on the line.

If they lose to Everton, then you starting thinking: this is going to be another grind of a season. Here we go again. You would start really, really worrying as a Tottenham fan.

Tottenham Hotspur

Everton Saturday 12th September 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

But if they go and beat Everton, you start going two games without a defeat, they'll be on four points. Then all of a sudden you can build from there.

It's not as big as the Spurs vs Everton game on the final day of last season. If they lost that game, they were going to Lincoln.

But, at the moment, I just don't see this team putting five or six wins on the trot together. So this is a big football match.

The start Spurs have had is Brentford away, Newcastle at home and Nottingham Forest away. If they lose to Everton and have one point from four games, you start to worry.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Nottingham Forest's match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League

If they beat Everton, then they've got every chance of beating Aston Villa at home next week. If they don't beat Everton, they're not beating Villa. That's how it works. It's a snowball effect.

When you win football matches, you expect to win the one after. But if you don't, the confidence goes.

'I still don't see Man Utd in my top five'

Man Utd have got the Manchester derby - and their season is in the balance too. If you beat Man City, you're flying. If you get beat by Man City, here we go again.

It would be one point from two games including the Everton game. And other teams are winning around you.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville questioned Manchester United's defensive issues after they conceded twice away at Everton to draw 2-2 in the Premier League

I've said all along: I don't think Man Utd have bought very well. The squad isn't big enough. It's nowhere near enough.

Defensively they're nowhere near good enough. They let in two goals against Everton - and they were two good goals, but one of them was from the edge of the box. Everybody's behind the ball.

When you're winning, put another forward on. Don't take a forward off and put a defender on. Don't give that team the opportunity.

Instead, if you put a forward on for a midfielder or a forward, it changes the game completely. If you're the other manager, you think: 'Oh no, what am I going to do?'.

Manchester United

Manchester City Sunday 13th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Instead, Man Utd just invited pressure on. Just don't do that, especially if you're a big team.

If you're Coventry and you go in front at Everton, you of course put a defender on 100 per cent. But when you're Man Utd, I don't see the need to do that.

If you're dictating the game, Everton don't get that chance for Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

So I am worried - and this is why I didn't put Manchester United in my top five at the start of the season. Nothing's changed for me since then. When you draw games, it hurts you.

'Time to find out how good Man City are'

I don't think Man City have been great. But sometimes I look at teams when they keep winning and they haven't played well as a real worry for the other sides.

Sometimes wins can cover cracks - but City have got Erling Haaland scoring goals. And they kept a clean sheet against Coventry last time out, that's a positive for them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester City's match against Coventry in the Premier League

City have got some big games coming up against Man Utd and Liverpool. That's the test to know where City are under Enzo Maresca.

If City win those two games and the match against Sunderland in between, they're not going to be far off the top come the end of the season.

If they don't get at least two points out of those two games, then Arsenal could run away with the league title a bit. I have Chelsea down for third in the league and they're already miles off Arsenal.

Sports.title: Rogers and Palmer helping each other thrive
Sports.content:
Welcome to The Radar, a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺 Palmer-Rogers double act analysed

🔺 Scott starring for Bournemouth

🔺 Crystal Palace's tough-tackler

Palmer and Rogers thriving

Morgan Rogers was bemused when he found out Cole Palmer was man of the match in Chelsea's win over Leeds. "I got four assists," he pleaded. "I'll say you should have had it," replied a smiling Palmer. "Don't mention me. I'm just a bystander," added Rogers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the hilarious moment Morgan Rogers discovers Cole Palmer was man of the match

The exchange, captured by the Sky Sports cameras before their post-match interview, showed the chemistry between the pair. It can be seen on the pitch too. Do they feel like they've been playing together forever? "We pretty much have," answered Rogers.

Close friends and former team-mates in England and Manchester City's youth teams, Rogers and Palmer have picked up where they left off at Chelsea, wreaking havoc either side of Joao Pedro and providing a combined 11 goals and assists in five games so far.

Their half-time introductions inspired Chelsea's comeback on Wednesday. After Rogers had ingeniously flicked the ball off his backside to set up Palmer's equaliser, the pair could be seen combining in the lead-up to Chelsea's third and sixth goals too.

In the 4-3 win over Brighton, they took it in turns to tee each other up, only to be denied by last-ditch blocks. In their opener against Fulham, Rogers created three shooting chances for Palmer but he couldn't capitalise.

In total, they have created nine chances for each other, which is more than twice as many as any other two players in the Premier League, ahead of five pairings, among them Palmer and Joao Pedro and Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland, on four.

Although most expected Palmer to be the provider for Rogers, it has more commonly been the other way around so far. Palmer finished last season with a run of one goal in 13 games but has four in five this term, his threat increased thanks in part to his new team-mate.

Rogers explained how they intended to help each other after his arrival. "We have different qualities, different ways of playing and affecting games," he said. "Ultimately, it's about scoring and creating and linking the game. We can do that in our own ways."

The differences can be seen in how they feed each other. Rogers typically aims to find Palmer in space between the opponent's defensive and midfield lines, as in the examples below.

Rogers is similarly adept at finding space between the lines. But he also offers a threat in behind, something Palmer has attempted to exploit with passes targeting his forward runs.

It helps that in Xabi Alonso's system, the width is provided by the wing-backs. This gives Rogers and Palmer freedom to come inside, putting them in close proximity to each other and giving them more opportunities to combine in central areas.

With Rogers and Palmer playing off each other centrally, Chelsea have directed a higher percentage of attacks through the middle third of the pitch than any other Premier League side.

Hull, visitors to Stamford Bridge on Saturday, are the next side tasked with stopping them. Recent evidence suggests their run of three straight clean sheets may be at risk.

Scott excelling

While Chelsea were able to strengthen their attack with the signing of Rogers, their efforts to bolster their midfield were less successful. One of the players who got away from them in the summer continues to go from strength to strength at Bournemouth.

Alex Scott was valued highly by Andoni Iraola and the same is true for Marco Rose. "I love him," he said after their 2-2 draw with Newcastle last weekend. It was the third game in a row in which they have lost a lead late on and it felt particularly harsh on Scott.

The 23-year-old, scorer of Bournemouth's opener in their previous game against Everton, was the best player on the pitch at St James' Park. In addition to having a hand in both Bournemouth goals, he had more touches, made more final-third passes and contested more duels than any of his team-mates.

It was a continuation of a strong start to the season. Scott has showcased his blend of physical and technical qualities, working tirelessly and eating up ground as he shuttles between both boxes. There is a sense that he is taking more responsibility too.

It all bodes well for his future. Carry on like this and the clubs who coveted him during the summer will likely return in January. But for now Bournemouth will just hope for more of the same from him when they face Brentford at the Vitality Stadium on Saturday.

Tough-tackling Khalaili

Anan Khalaili has big shoes to fill at Crystal Palace having replaced Daniel Munoz in the right wing-back position. He provided evidence of his attacking threat with the driving run to set up Ben Chilwell's winning goal against Fulham last weekend.

But it's at the other end that he's been busiest. Khalaili has had some awkward moments defensively but he clearly relishes his one-vs-one battles and he has come out on top more often than not.

In fact, in addition to winning the second-most duels in the division so far, the 21-year-old, a summer signing from Union Saint-Gilloise, ranks top for tackles. His total of 17 puts him five clear of any other player. It's some going given he has only started twice.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Igor Thiago faces Bournemouth on Saturday aiming to get off the mark this season. The Brentford striker has registered 2.30 expected goals without scoring in the opening three games, the highest total of any player yet to find the net. Time for his luck to change?

"Honestly, I don't really know if there was much I could do today."

Sports.title: No wins and no goals - how concerned should Spurs be over PL start?
Sports.content:
It has been a winless and goalless start to the new Premier League season for big-spending Tottenham.

Last weekend's 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest saw Spurs fail to have a shot on target for the first time in a league game in over four years as they battled to their first point of the season.

Roberto De Zerbi's new-look side are yet to click after a £332m summer outlay which saw 10 new players arrive.

Having made their worst start to a league season since 2008, Spurs go in search of their first victory on Saturday as they host Everton, live on Sky Sports​​​​​​.

Here, Sky Sports News' Tottenham reporter Michael Bridge answers your questions, while we also look at the stats behind their start and hear your thoughts on their opening three league games...

Tottenham Hotspur

Everton Saturday 12th September 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

Spurs94: How concerned are you about the start to the season?

"I'm not concerned. It's only three games, and Spurs would've taken a draw at Nottingham Forest. It's a hard place to go under a very good manager in Oliver Glasner.

"I was at the Brentford game where Spurs were well beaten. I can fully appreciate that Tottenham being under-prepared is unacceptable, so I'll flip it round and say Brentford gave Spurs a good hiding and they fully deserved their win.

"Newcastle could have gone either way, but Spurs weren't clinical enough. But the reason why I'm not concerned is that it's still so early in the season.

"The last three games have shown me a little bit of a realisation that you can't expect it all to click so quickly when there have been so many incomings and departures."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge shares the latest from Tottenham ahead of their match against Everton

Tony H: Is De Zerbi losing control after coming out and complaining about his medical team after the Forest draw?

Dave Perryman: Do you think it's wrong for De Zerbi to publicly criticise his players and medical staff?

"De Zerbi absolutely did not have any complaints about the medical team. He's working closely with the medical team.

"Let's not forget that in the last couple of seasons Spurs have suffered an injury crisis, with key players missing an entire season.

"Tottenham Hotspur have worked hard over the last few months to ensure that this doesn't happen again, including an investigation which looked into whether the pitch had a bearing on such serious injuries.

"To clarify, De Zerbi doesn't want to take players off at certain minutes, but he's instructed to do so by his medical staff.

"He's not challenging them or being divisive. He's working alongside them. They are ensuring that De Zerbi has these players for the long term to hopefully prevent situations like Mohammed Kudus and James Maddison from occurring again."

Spurs4Life: Why are the Spurs fans getting on De Zerbi's back? Do they not remember the rocky start Mauricio Pochettino had?

Rich: How much pressure must there be on De Zerbi to get it right?

"If it wasn't for De Zerbi, there'd have been a very high chance Tottenham would be in the Championship right now.

"Spurs have given De Zerbi the keys to mould the squad how he sees fit. I'm of the opinion that he has earned the right to have those keys.

"He has made tough decisions, including allowing Luka Vuskovic to go to Brighton and to bring in Jan Paul van Hecke for a big fee despite him having a year to go on his contract.

"I must reiterate, it's three games in. For me, the start of the season for Spurs can be seen as post-transfer window.

"I think we won't see the real Spurs until maybe even November because there have been so many changes: new captain, new forward line, new midfield, new defence. It takes time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi says all of his side's new arrivals are 'bomba' signings

Brad Taylor: What are Spurs actually aiming for this season? Top four to six? Top half? Survival?

Dan: Based upon a much slower start to our campaign, would a mid-table finish be more realistic?

"With the outlay, you have to expect that they must finish in European places.

"It won't be made public, but the aim must be to get back into Europe.

"Now, of course, when I say Europe, ideally it's the Champions League. But even if it was Europa League football, people are now more aware than ever that additional home fixtures generate revenue.

"Brad, in my personal view, mid-table is the very least they should be aiming for."

The stats behind Spurs' winless start

Spurs are aiming to avoid unwanted history on Saturday - if Everton keep a clean sheet, then it will be the first time Tottenham have failed to score in their first four league games of a season.

Their struggles in front of goal are a result of a lack of quality chances created.

Despite ranking mid-table for shots attempted in the Premier League this season, Spurs are bottom for expected goals (xG) per shot, as you can see below.

Since the start of last season, the average xG per game by a Premier League side is 1.41, but Spurs are yet to reach that average return for xG in any game under De Zerbi.

One of the Italian's issues has been a lack of consistency in his attacking selections. De Zerbi has started with three different attacking combinations in all three league games this season and has used 10 different starters across his front three in his 10 league games in charge.

And it is not just the front line where De Zerbi has faced selection issues. Tottenham have made eight changes to their starting XI in the Premier League this season, the most of any side and their joint-most in the first three games of a campaign in the competition.

Spurs' running stats are another alarming area of concern this season.

Tottenham were only outrun once in De Zerbi's seven games in charge last season as they dramatically escaped relegation on the final day. This season, however, Spurs have been outrun in every game.

In fact, they rank second-bottom for distance run and 16th for sprinting distance in the Premier League this season, having been in the top five under De Zerbi last season.

Higher physical output, improved threat and better attacking quality are all needed to kickstart their season.

Sports.title: Caballo De Mar faces Queenstown in Doncaster Cup
Sports.content:
Caballo De Mar locks horns with Queenstown in the Doncaster Cup - live on Sky Sports Racing.

3.00 Doncaster - Caballo De Mar and Queenstown lock horns

A captivating renewal of the feature Group 2 Betfred Howard Wright Doncaster Cup Stakes sees Caballo De Mer and Queenstown lock horns.

George Scott saddles Caballo De Mer, who carries a Group 1 penalty after his Prix Vicomtesse Vigier success in May but sets a lofty target for his rivals to catch. Not at his best when beaten favourite at York, his trainer reaches for the blinkers as he looks to regain the winning thread under Oisin Murphy.

Aidan O'Brien's Queenstown is a solid stayer who returned to the winners' enclosure when claiming Group 3 honours at the Curragh and deserves a crack at this stronger grade.

Three-year-old Windlay is a fascinating contender for Emmet Mullins, with William Buick in the plate. He has plenty of excellent form over hurdles and broke his maiden in a Ffos Las heat last month. This is a huge step up in class, but he remains unexposed in this sphere and over these Cup distances.

Berkshire Sundance ran a creditable race in the Chester Cup from a difficult draw and has since applied himself to a decent standards in competitive races at Royal Ascot and Glorious Goodwood. He has plenty to find stepping into Group company for the first time, but is not without a chance for Andrew Balding.

2.25 Doncaster - Flann Sunna, Sale Shark and Pershaada contest deep renewal

A quality field 12 of has gathered for the Group 2 Carlsberg Danish Pilsner Flying Childers Stakes where Pershaada is likely to head the betting.

The Richard Hannon-trained filly has been busy this season winning two of her six starts with the highlight being her impressive Molecomb victory. Down the field in the Nunthorpe, she will appreciate dropping back to her own age group and should be in the mix under Sean Levey.

Image: Pershaada takes his chance at Doncaster today

Sale Shark saw off Adonius to land the Listed Roses Stakes at York last month, reversing Goodwood form in the process. He has been a progressive sort and looks ready for a crack at this level.

Flann Sunna lost his unbeaten record at Goodwood, but given the manner of his first two wins, it would be foolish to rule him out. Donning the Wathnan colours, Final Objective will be looking to build on a promising effort when second to Arapaho Gold in the Gimcrack. James Doyle takes the ride on this son of Sioux Nation, who drops down to the minimum distance for the first time.

1.15 Doncaster - Godolphin pair Rock Montreal and Nabati clash

Godolphin pair Rock Montreal and Nabati clash in a competitive edition of this opening Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes.

Nabati showed an excellent attitude when landing skinny odds at Newmarket last month, taking his record to two wins from three runs. He heads up in class and might be suited by this extra furlong under William Buick.

Rock Montreal is a live player for the Roger Varian team. A 1m guineas yearling, he burst onto the scene with a dominant success at Yarmouth and will be expected to build on that for a yard that took this prize last season.

Of the others, easy Salisbury debut winner Forbidden Fire makes most appeal, with the Karl Burke-trained Varzi also on the improve having tasted success at Pontefract the last day.

Best of the rest

Friday's Doncaster card also features the 1.50pm Betfred Leger Legends Classified Stakes, with some former weighing room favourites returning to the saddle. Derby winner Adam Kirby rides Caragio for himself, whilst Tom Scudamore gets aboard Bella Bisbee.

Staying on Town Moor, the British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap (3.35pm) sees Silver Lake and Salamanca City face off before York winner Henley On Thames takes on Tumishi in the 4.45pm Tanbry Construction Nursery Handicap.

At Chester, Hugo Palmer fields course specialist Roman Dragon alongside stablemate Tricky Tel in the feature Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap. On the continent at Saint-Cloud, The Odyssey and Regal Chime aim for Listed honours in the Prix Turenne.

Sports.title: Lewis Hall agrees long-term Newcastle deal, Chelsea buy-out close: football news – live
Sports.content:
13m ago 05.37 EDT Spanish World Cup-winner Juan Mata has confirmed he will be departing Australian side Melbourne Victory, but stopped short of calling time on his career. The former Manchester United and Chelsea ace has enjoyed a late-career resurgence and was voted the domestic A-League player of the year in 2025-26. But the 38-year-old has decided not to play on at the club as he mulls “the next steps in his career”. He will remain involved with the Australian side after taking an ownership stake. “I loved every minute and so greatly enjoyed everything that we achieved last season, falling back in love with football at such a special place, in an amazing city that it was a privilege to call home,” Mata said. “Now I am excited about our next chapters, believing together in the future of Australian football and inspiring the next generation of Melbourne Victory players and supporters.” AFP Share

16m ago 05.33 EDT Gianni Infantino has not responded to a request to appear before the US House judiciary committee or sent documents requested by one of its members more than a month past the deadline. The Democrat Jamie Raskin, the ranking minority member of the committee, wrote to the Fifa president on 26 July informing the Swiss he was launching an investigation into “a sustained campaign” by Fifa to curry favour with the US president, Donald Trump. His letter said seeking of favours extended to the dismissal of high-profile corruption cases, while also accusing Fifa of “gouging” American consumers with “exorbitant” World Cup ticket prices this summer. The Swiss was asked to respond to the letter by 9 August with the requested documents and to make contact with the committee to schedule an interview, but it is understood no response at all had been received as of Thursday. Because no subpoena was issued, there are no criminal consequences for ignoring Raskin’s request. Press Association Share Updated at 05.34 EDT

23m ago 05.27 EDT In totally normal Turkish football news… the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job. Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks. Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added. Full story: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay Read more Share

47m ago 05.02 EDT View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino was accused by the French federation’s president of behaving in a ‘unilateral and opaque fashion’. Photograph: Jarek Praszkiewicz/EPA The French football federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election. The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash. French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support Read more Share Updated at 05.35 EDT

1h ago 04.46 EDT United were the only Premier League club in Champions League action last night but Englishman Harry Kane scored for the eighth game in a row in the competition as Bayern Munich beat Bodø/Glimt 5-0 at the Allianz Arena. Starting their Champions League journey were Cesc Fabregas’s Como, who beat RB Leipzig 4-1 Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, while Lens scored twice in added time to reverse a 2-1 deficit and secure a 3-2 win. Our roundup of all of Thursday night’s European action is here. Share

1h ago 04.37 EDT David Hytner United clinical on Champions League return to dismiss Sabah View image in fullscreen Benjamin Sesko celebrates after scoring Manchester United’s third goal before half-time. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire. Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City. Read David Hytner’s full report from Old Trafford: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return Read more Share

1h ago 04.22 EDT Hall agrees contract extension Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall has signed a new long-term contract with the club. Reports suggest the left-back, 22, has agreed a two-year extension to his original deal that would take his contract up to 2031. Hall has been the subject of interest from Manchester United, among others, but has now committed his immediate future to Newcastle. “It’s an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters,” he said. “I know how much it means to them. “To be able to bring joy to their faces, it’s a big thing for me. I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all. “One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United.” Allow Instagram content?
