Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Ton up for hard-working McBurnie

With 10 top-flight goal contributions between them across three games already this season, the Chelsea trio of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the early pace-setters for the Premier League’s most prolific, fluid and high-octane attacking unit. But on the occasion of his 100th Premier League appearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and, given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion. Barry Glendenning

Chelsea v Hull, Saturday 3pm (all times BST)

2 Arbeloa must trust process as Iraola once did

This might be an opportune moment for Álvaro Arbeloa to meet Andoni Iraola, though perhaps not his Liverpool team. With three defeats and seven goals conceded from his first three Premier League games as Fulham head coach, questions are already being asked over the former Liverpool defender’s ambitious approach. Just as they were when Iraola failed to win any of his first nine league games in charge of Bournemouth. Trust yourself and the process, might be the Liverpool head coach’s advice if asked. Fulham have been creative under Arbeloa but are easily exposed defensively. Liverpool, starting to click in attack under their new head coach, have the assets to exploit Fulham’s weaknesses and subject Arbeloa to an uncomfortable Anfield return. Iraola’s wide options could be reduced, however, with Bradley Barcola suffering cramp on Wednesday – his first start since France’s World Cup semi-final loss – and Cody Gakpo nursing a minor injury. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Fulham, Saturday 3pm

3 Doucouré eagerly waiting Palace return

Cheick Doucouré has had a rotten run of luck with injuries. Just when the Mali midfielder looked as if he was ready to make a first Crystal Palace appearance since January 2025 in Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Middlesbrough, he was taken ill. Pierre Sage revealed last week that Doucouré looked as if he had “given him one million dollars” when he was informed he would be part of the matchday squad at Fulham, where Palace got off the mark with a 3-2 victory. Sage has confirmed that the 26-year-old, who has been sidelined with two serious knee injuries but was once a transfer target for Liverpool, could be involved against Ipswich at Selhurst Park on Saturday. Whenever he does return it is sure to be a heartwarming moment. Ed Aarons

Crystal Palace v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Cheick Doucouré returned to the Crystal Palace squad for last weekend’s trip to Fulham. Photograph: James Fearn/Getty Images

4 Cherries must end late lapses

The midfield battle between Brentford and Bournemouth will be crucial on Saturday, with Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangaré setting the tempo for Keith Andrews’ physical side. Brentford top the Premier League for aerial duels won (22.3 per 90 mins), interceptions (11.3 per 90), and fouls committed (16.3 per 90). “They defend well as a team, their high pressing is good,” said Bournemouth’s Marco Rose, who is hoping to guide his side to a first Premier League victory of the season. “Their transition, they have fast players. They have quality everywhere on the pitch, and every situation.” Rose’s answer for Brentford’s aggressiveness should be Alex Scott, who leads his team for interceptions and has drawn nine fouls so far this campaign – the fourth-highest tally in the league. Late drama could also be the deciding factor at the Vitality Stadium. Despite leading in all three of their opening league fixtures, Bournemouth have picked up just two points and four of their five goals conceded have arrived from the 84th minute onwards. History favours their opponents too, as the Cherries have failed to win any of their eight top-flight meetings with the Bees. Yara El-Shaboury

Bournemouth v Brentford, Saturday 3pm

5 Jackson ready to fill Watkins’ Villa boots

A summer of change at Aston Villa inevitably prompted plenty of noise but most of their new signings were long-standing targets, none more so than Nicolas Jackson. Unai Emery kickstarted Jackson’s career at Villarreal and, after reuniting at Villa, the Senegal striker scored his first goal at Club Brugge on Tuesday after his initial £47.5m move. Jackson has replaced Ollie Watkins, who proved a reliable source of goals across six straight top-flight seasons, and the early evidence has been encouraging. “I had a couple of fights with him when he was at Chelsea so when he first came in I thought: ‘What’s he going to be like?’ but he’s a brilliant guy,” said the Villa captain, John McGinn. “There’s a lot of expectation with the transfer fee but he’s going to be a huge player for us.” Ben Fisher

Aston Villa v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

6 Signs of early-season panic at Spurs

Only the most pessimistic home fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will be gripped by anything resembling the kind of dread, anxiety and outright terror that accompanied Everton’s visit on the final day of last season, but the return of David Moyes’ side so early in the current campaign will still make for nervous viewing. With no goals and just one point on the board after three league games, fan faith in Roberto De Zerbi – and the hundreds of millions of pounds lavished upon new signings – has created a prevailing presumption that Tottenham will soon start firing on at least some, if not all, cylinders. In Everton, Spurs welcome a team whose record in this corner of north London is worse than any other top-flight side’s. Should they fail to beat a team who have taken just seven points from the past 51 available to them away at Tottenham, the sounds of early but outright mutiny are likely to be audible from the stands. BG

Tottenham v Everton, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Stadium of Light to give Guimarães hot reception

Old acquaintance will be renewed at the Stadium of Light on Saturday evening. While Sunderland’s captain and midfield anchor, Granit Xhaka, needs no introduction to his former north London public, the home centre-half Dan Ballard is a former Arsenal youth captain who joined the Gunners’ academy at the age of eight. Then there is Bruno Guimarães. Newcastle’s former captain can expect a hot reception as his new side aim to extend their season-opening run of five straight wins (including the Community Shield). “Arsenal are flying, they’re one of the best teams in Europe,” says Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager. “It will be challenging but I’m very excited to experience this situation again.” Thanks to goals from Ballard and Brian Brobbey, Le Bris choreographed a 2-2 Premier League draw against Mikel Arteta’s side on Wearside last November. “When you face a strong opponent you can become a bit shy but the most important thing is to be ourselves,” says Le Bris. “Arsenal are so adaptive they will find solutions, so we must be flexible.” Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Arsenal, Saturday 8pm

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães returns to the northeast as Arsenal visit Sunderland on Saturday night. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

8 Coventry adding points to performances?

One of three teams, along with Aston Villa and Tottenham, yet to score a top-flight goal this season, Coventry were extremely unfortunate not to break their duck at Manchester City last weekend. Their having narrowly avoided handing Frank Lampard’s side an early opener, it took a string of excellent saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma to ensure City took three points at the death. “They played really well against Manchester City and created a lot of chances,” said Fabian Hürzeler, who takes his Brighton team to the CBS Arena on Sunday afternoon. Having been scathing in his criticism of his own side’s lack of energy and intensity in their woeful first-half performance against Leeds, the German will be aware that a similarly lethargic performance from his team is unlikely to go unpunished. Particularly away from home against a promoted team that may be firing blanks, but visibly grew in confidence with each passing minute of their defeat by one of the league’s best teams. BG

Coventry v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

9 Contrasting Manchester teams face off in derby

Manchester derby No 199 features a fascinating showdown between two young managers operating in the sport’s rarefied air: Michael Carrick, 45, who seeks to guide Manchester United to an 82nd victory in the fixture, and Enzo Maresca, 46, who aims for Manchester City’s 63rd. As the great Pep Guardiola’s successor, the visiting Italian can be delighted at his team’s perfect record from their four games under him since the Community Shield defeat. Carrick, though, should be disappointed at the return from an opening three matches as United’s permanent manager: a defeat at Hull and draw at Everton, with the 5-2 home win over Ipswich sandwiched between. United fans will protest beforehand about the club’s approach to eradicating ticket touting, and the occasion should be particularly spicy and vibrant. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Manchester City, Sunday 4.30pm

View image in fullscreen Manchester United supporters protested about the club’s ticket policies at Hull and will do so again before the Manchester derby. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

10 Battle of the goalkeepers at Elland Road

Two teams unbeaten in the Premier League this season, two German managers in the dugouts and a Monday night goalkeeping beauty contest at Elland Road. While Daniel Farke welcomes his compatriot Matthias Jaissle to West Yorkshire for the first time, James Trafford – the £40m England keeper Newcastle tried to sign on three separate occasions – will be in goal for Leeds. The visitors eventually turned their attentions to the £26m Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who arrived on Tyneside from Braga in July. So far at least, Jaissle is delighted by the 24-year-old’s performances. “Lukas is an amazing signing,” said Jaissle. “Coming to the Premier League and dealing with the pressure is not easy and, as a keeper, that pressure is something else. I like Lukas a lot. He’s so calm but so mature as well. There’s not even a hint of nervousness. He gives the whole team confidence. That helps a lot.” LT

Sports.title: Pochettino’s ‘different’ vow to the US invites unwelcome speculation
Sports.content:
I hope, in this lifetime, you find someone who loves you the way Mauricio Pochettino loves Tottenham Hotspur. The grip Spurs have on his heart seems the stuff of a literary classic: his imperfect partner who called things off at the first sign of trouble must merely check in on him occasionally to rekindle hopes of a reunion.

Perhaps a bit extreme, but this week’s revelation – that he’d return to Tottenham even if they were relegated and chalking his absence up to imperfect timing, not the part about handing the club a decade-old title – has implicity laid out the terms of his return as United States manager. Others may always have interest in his services, and a certain North London suitor will never get the door slammed in their face outright.

“Now it’s a four-year contract, it’s different,” Pochettino said this week. “We can next season lose the Copa América or the Gold Cup, they’re not happy with us and they can sack us. Or we can say: ‘OK. It’s not in the way that we think.’ Four years is different. Maybe now if someone calls in the future, it’s a different, different type [of thing]. We are excited, we are thinking to spend four years to the next World Cup. But now it’s a long period.”

If you’re a Spurs fan, it warms the heart to revisit last decade’s glory days. If you’re a US fan, you’re quite sick of hearing so much about a team besides the one he’s managing. If you’ve been cursed to support both, this must be a very confusing time. And if you’re US Soccer, you know that you no longer have an ace in the hole to outflank any outside interest.

One can’t undersell the appeal of coaching a World Cup host team, with a direct path to Pot One and raucous support for every match. Already a familiar face to Americans who follow the sport, Pochettino became a genuine sensation in the broader sports landscape. Millions of Americans had parallel thoughts that he, clad handsomely in a $500 safari shirt, resembled Russell Crowe – perhaps tacitly revealing that millions of Americans have long undersold the appeal of Russell Crowe.

Compared to his previous post at Chelsea, the US job offered relative reprieve. Never before has Pochettino been such a prolific fixture on hours-long podcasts. The stop/start cadence of international management is appealing for the football men who have grown weary of the meticulous corporatization of the club game. In that sense, Pochettino is among esteemed company.

Two years after Jürgen Klopp left Liverpool citing mental exhaustion, he has refreshed his tracksuit collection with fresh duds from Die Mannschaft. In his opening press conference, he read aloud to the press his terms of service – and was celebrated for it. Carlo Ancelotti was in no rush to abandon Brazil after a middling tournament, despite real questions about the pool’s depth and quality in midfield. Even Pep Guardiola held talks with Italy immediately after his decade in Manchester.

What’s different about Pochettino from, say, Klopp is his perceived eagerness to return to the club grind. Even atop the Red Bull Football conglomerate, Klopp was quick to brush aside any insinuations about returning to management. Pochettino, by contrast, held talks with Milan about their coaching vacancy immediately before the 2026 World Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There may be a simple answer. Each of Ancelotti, Guardiola, and Klopp – company with which Pochettino is regularly associated – has been the champion of England and Europe. Pochettino, at this stage, has not reached those summits.

Is aiming for a Copa América semi-final more enticing than restoring Tottenham to previous heights? What about reaching a World Cup quarter-final an ocean away from the tens of thousands who soundtracked the previous one? What can US Soccer offer that his caliber of clubs – Tottenham and beyond – can’t exceed?

While Pochettino and his charges have something resembling an excuse for their lack of execution against Belgium, the fact remains that the USMNT were once again eliminated in the last-16. Just like they were under Bob Bradley in 2010. And Jürgen Klinsmann in 2014. And Gregg Berhalter in 2022.

In theory, Pochettino will enter his second cycle in a position of strength having undertaken a thorough examination of the player pool. The fresh faces are no longer MLS journeymen or players in Europe’s lesser divisions. Instead, they’re promising prospects: 16-year-old wonderkid Cavan Sullivan, new Crystal Palace showman Zavier Gozo, highly anticipated La Masia netminder Diego Kochen.

If anything, working the up-and-comers into the established core and identifying sturdier central defenders to partner with Chris Richards should be an incredibly exciting project. The core is in great shape, with this summer’s headliners – Folarin Balogun, Alex Freeman, Richards, and Malik Tillman – all aged 30 or younger in the summer of 2030. There’s plenty of reason to think that the program is better positioned for a deep run at the next World Cup than the 2026.

Actualizing that potential will require a clear vision and a dedicated effort to raise this team’s standard throughout every window of the next four years. Batting eyelashes at past employers hardly projects that level of dedication. And so, for the next four years just like the past one, the biggest question surrounding the USMNT won’t be how far they can go in 2030. It’ll be whether Pochettino will still be the man leading them there.

Sports.title: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return
Sports.content:
It was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points off the top. The job that their manager, Valdas Dambrauskas, has done since taking over in the summer of last year is extraordinary.

It was also a night for cold, hard reality. Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.

Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.

United had wanted to put their best foot forward when they heard the Champions League aria after the chaos and embarrassment of their previous involvement in the competition. Erik ten Hag was the manager in 2023-24 and his team finished bottom of their group with four points, starting and ending with losses to Bayern Munich. It was what happened in between times against Galatasaray and Copenhagen that still causes a few shudders. It was a period when United panicked uncontrollably when they had a lead. When the defensive gifts from them came in crazy clusters.

Carrick took no chances with his starting XI. There was minimal rotation in the midfield and front line, save for a first start of the season for Sesko in the No 9 position. It was easy to think that the manager wanted to groove Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield before the City game.

United looked to Fernandes to get them going. As always. There were intelligent runs from him; incision about his passes, that wonderful disguise on some of them. The breakthrough goal stemmed from him chasing a high ball over the top that looked like a lost cause only for him to keep it in play. It was what happened next that quickened United pulses. When Sabah gave the ball away cheaply to Bryan Mbeumo, United moved quickly over to the left. Patrick Dorgu crossed and Cunha’s finish was clean.

Quick Guide Gabriel, 15, stars with hat-trick for United in Youth League debut Show Manchester United's JJ Gabriel (pictured) marked his Uefa Youth League debut with a hat-trick against Sabah aged just 15. The attacker is tipped as a future star and made his first appearance for the first team off the bench in last month’s friendly against Atlético Madrid. Gabriel has yet to make Michael Carrick’s squad for a competitive match but the teenager, who turns 16 next month, continues to knock on the door. He sparkled for the Under-19s in Thursday’s 5-0 win against Sabah in the Youth League in front of director of football Jason Wilcox, director of recruitment Christopher Vivell and first-team coach Travis Binnion. Amir Ibragimov and Jacob Watson scored early goals in Leigh, where Gabriel added another in a dominant first half. Gabriel scored two more late in the second half to claim the match ball against the Azerbaijani visitors, who did not manage a shot on a day that United mustered 44 attempts. PA Photograph: Zohaib Alam/Manchester United Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Sabah lined up in a 4-3-3 formation; no bus parking. They wanted to ask questions of a United defence that had a makeshift feel about it. There was assurance on the ball from them, the desire to carry it forward. And a huge chance in the 35th minute when Kaheem Parris crossed to the back post. Joy-Lance Mickels was clear of Noussair Mazraoui only to put the header wide. The angle was not favourable. It did not entirely excuse him.

View image in fullscreen Matheus Cunha opens the scoring with a smart finish in the first half. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Sabah were harshly treated by the half-time scoreline, even though United played on the front foot and created openings. It was the one-two punch in the closing stages of the first period that changed everything. Fernandes – who else? – made a sidefoot finish look easy after Tielemans had burst on a Cunha pass inside, spun and teed him up. The third followed a first time pass by Fernandes into Mbeumo, who got Sesko clean though. The Sabah backline was high. Sesko went around the goalkeeper to score. He never looked like missing.

There was a lovely scene 90 ­minutes before kick-off when some of the Sabah players wandered around the pitch, the stadium virtually empty, phones out to capture the quiet before the storm, the sheer scale of Old Trafford. They wore wide smiles. They were determined not to be overawed when it got started. The performance of the strolling central midfielder, Ivan Lepinjica, was certainly impressive. They were just too loose at the back.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United played some slick stuff at times, Mainoo and ­Fernandes ever involved. When Carrick’s ­pass-and-move game clicks, it is easy to feel the ­possibility. ­Imposing it against the higher-­profile teams is the name of the game. ­Starting against City.

Mason Mount was introduced at half-time for his first football of the season – “It was great to get Mason back on the pitch,” Carrick later said – with Tielemans coming off, his work done. The Belgian could be pleased with his impact. Carrick was always going to withdraw other likely starters against City, such as Mainoo. Sesko came off with him on 64 minutes and was warmly applauded. After his goal at Everton on Sunday, has he done enough to make the XI for the derby?

Carrick added: “We always push for more. Results-wise it hasn’t been the start we wanted, but performance-wise there are a lot of things we were looking for. The clean sheet was important tonight. Collectively as a team we have done a lot of good things and that is why we are excited what this season can bring.”

His side controlled the second half. The jeopardy was long gone. The fourth goal summed up Sabah’s travails in their defensive third. It was a scooped free-kick by Fernandes for Joshua Zirkzee, on as a substitute, and when his backheel hit Aden ­McCarthy, the Sabah goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, lost his bearings, the ball caught under his feet. It was a tap-in for Martínez. The substitute, Orphé Mbina, headed high for Sabah at the very end. There was to be no fairytale goal.

Sports.title: Champions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past Leipzig
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich opened their Champions League campaign with a 5-0 thrashing of Norway’s Bodø/Glimt.

The six-times winners were frustrated before half-time by Bodø/Glimt but cruised once Jamal Musiala smashed in the opener two minutes into the second period and the floodgates opened.

Harry Kane headed the second on the hour – his 34th goal in 39 Champions League appearances for Bayern – and Alphonso Davies made it 3-0 with a powerful half-volley. With Vincent Kompany’s side in full flow, Michael ‌Olise completed the scoring with a superb late double.

Cesc Fàbregas’s Como impressed on their debut in Europe’s premier club competition, crushing RB Lepzig 4-1.

Goals from Croatia midfielder Martin Baturina, Greece forward Tasos Douvikas and Senegal’s Assane Diao put Como in control. Serbia midfielder Andrija Maksimović pulled a goal back for Leipzig, before Maximo Perrone sealed a 4-1 victory late on in a dream night in northern Italy.

View image in fullscreen Cesc Fàbregas gives a post-game, on-pitch team talk to his players after Como’s opening Champions League win. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Uefa/Getty Images

Ten-man Slavia Prague suffered ​heartbreak at home to Lens ‌as they conceded twice in ​stoppage time to lose 3-2.

Mikulas ​Konecny was sent off for the hosts just after half-time after a tackle was reviewed by VAR, but minutes later Danijel Sturm put the hosts ahead. Abdallah Sima broke Slavia’s resistance with an equaliser only for Sturm to send the home crowd into raptures with his second in the 88th minute.

Florian Thauvin struck in the 91st minute and there was still time for Lens to snatch victory with a pinpoint strike by Ruben Aguilar.

PSV came from a goal down to draw 1-1 at home to Shakhtar Donetsk and end a woeful record in their opening matches of Champions League campaigns. The Dutch club had lost their opening fixtures in their last five Champions League appearances and trailed at half-time before Sergiño Dest ensured a point.

Right near the end of a cagey first half, Shakhtar stunned the hosts when Gleiker Mendoza cut in from wide and ‌sent a stunning low ‌shot beyond the dive of Matej Kovar. PSV responded immediately after the break as the ‌ball was fed across the area to Dest who calmly found the bottom corner with an inch-perfect shot.

Roma drew 1-1 with Fenerbahce in Istanbul, with Bryan Cristante’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Archie Brown’s goal three minutes into the second half. Confusion reigned after the match as the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation – only for the club president to insist he will stay.

Sports.title: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay
Sports.content:
The Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job.

Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks.

Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added.

“I just spoke to Ismail Kartal. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure,” he said. Asked whether the manager had told him he would stay, Yildirim said: “There’s no need for him ‌to say that he’d continue. I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s ​it. We are a family.”

Kartal, who spent a decade at Fenerbahce as a player, coached the club in 2014-15, then on an interim basis in 2021-22 before returning for a full ⁠campaign in 2023-24. He was the assistant manager at Fenerbahce the ​past two ​times the club won ​the Turkish title, and returned for a fourth ​managerial spell in ‌June.

View image in fullscreen Archie Brown celebrates his equaliser for Fenerbahce. The English full-back was left dumbfounded when learning of his coach’s resignation after the final whistle. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Fenerbahce have ​finished second ​in the Turkish Super Lig in each of the past five seasons, and reached the Champions League’s league phase this season for the first time in 18 years. The team sit ninth in the Turkish top-flight, having lost twice in their opening four games, including Saturday’s 2-1 home defeat to Besiktas.

Roma took the lead in the 39th minute when Donyell Malen rolled a pass to ​Bryan Cristante, who beat Fenerbahce keeper Ederson with a bouncing finish. The hosts levelled before half-time when Mason Greenwood slipped a ​pass through to Archie ​Brown, who clipped a finish over ​Mile Svilar.

Roma were awarded a penalty in the 68th minute when ​Kerem Akturkoglu was ‌penalised for a ​foul on Paulo ​Dybala, but a VAR check ruled that the challenge had taken place outside the area. Fenerbahce came closest to grabbing a winner late on when Nathan Aké headed against the Roma crossbar.

Fenerbahce will travel to Aston Villa and host Liverpool in two of their remaining league phase games – whether Kartal will be in charge or not remains to be seen.

Sports.title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support
Sports.content:
The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election.

The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash.

During the World Cup the suspension of the US forward Folarin Balogun was overturned by Fifa after lobbying from Donald Trump. The US president said he called Infantino to recommend that Balogun be allowed to play. Fifa has said the decision taken by its disciplinary committee was “a balanced measure” and “based on an explicit provision of the applicable regulations”.

Diallo outlined the reasons for the loss in confidence: “From July onwards, the conditions which led to us to support his candidacy had been disrupted. Does the withdrawal of the [sell-off] project solve the issue? I don’t think so. His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”

Diallo said of the initial decision to support Infantino: “It would be wrong to say that certain developments in football were not made under his mandate.” But he added: “When you are making changes to the game itself, in a unilateral and opaque fashion to sell our shared asset, that changes our appreciation.

“France is one of the founding members of Fifa, and as such we have a historical legitimacy to intervene when we feel that Fifa and its president are deviating from our vision of how world football should be run. We also have sporting legitimacy, as one of the top three teams in the world rankings over the last 10 years. We wanted to make it clear that we refuse to go in a direction which does not correspond to the general interest of our sport.”

When reports of the sell-off project came to light, the FFF expressed “doubts and deep concerns”. Uefa threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions and several European countries, including Wales and England, withdrew their support for Infantino but the FFF had not until Thursday publicly disavowed him.

Diallo indicated France would play an active part in Uefa’s search for an alternative candidate for the Fifa presidency before the 18 November deadline. The election will take place in March during Fifa’s next congress.

Before then, Diallo said, the FFF would reach out to figures it considers experts in “transparency and good governance” in football and beyond as part of France’s “contribution to the debate”, as it pushes for “far-reaching reform” of Fifa.

He cited Kevin Lamour, the former Fifa chief operating officer who was dismissed after criticising the sell-off plan, as one of the people the FFF would look to consult.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Declan Rice shrugs off Arsenal concerns and says 60 games a season is sustainable
Sports.content:
Declan Rice has insisted his body can sustain more than 60 appearances again this season, despite Arsenal’s concerns after he played through pain at the World Cup.

Rice racked up 69 appearances last season for Arsenal and England but revealed during the World Cup he had been managing neural back and hamstring pain, for which he is understood to have received a pain-killing injection, after a hamstring injury in December. It is understood Arsenal are monitoring the 27-year-old’s workload closely after he had only three weeks off before returning to training a week before the Community Shield last month.

Rice came off the bench to replace Bruno Guimarães in the victory over Manchester City in Cardiff and has since started all Arsenal’s matches, with Guimarães’ return from an injury being managed. A major reason why Arsenal bought the Brazil midfielder for £75m from Newcastle was to take some strain off from Rice, although it was noticeable that Rice played all of Wednesday’s Champions League victory at Napoli, with Mikel Merino coming off for Guimarães.

“I think for the last six seasons, even since my West Ham days when they were in Europe, I’ve played 60-plus every season,” Rice said. “So I think it is sustainable because I’ve shown that I can do it.

“It’s just about maintaining it, maintaining the level and the consistency of the performances. For me, that’s the main thing, showing up every week, giving a good account of myself and helping the team win. I’ve been lucky enough to be able to do that. So I’m really hungry to be able to do that again this season.”

It is understood Arsenal offered Rice more time off after the World Cup exploits but that he was keen to return for the start of the season. He is expected to be part of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia when it is announced next Friday, although whether he features in all four matches remains to be seen, with Arsenal likely to request that he and Bukayo Saka are given another opportunity to rest. Rice said he had found things “tough” during the World Cup but is adamant he is feeling “refreshed”.

“I feel really good at the minute, in really good form, so we’ll make it continue,” he said. “I think everyone knew I had an issue with a neural hamstring. But also on the top of the Premier League season, which was so demanding, the Champions League, to then play a World Cup in that heat really does take its toll. I’m a player that goes on the pitch, wants to be fresh and give 100% every time I put on an England shirt. Yes, there were stages where I felt really, really good and stages where I didn’t feel so good. There were a few things that frustrated me, just with myself, just not feeling 100%. It’s one of those things I just had to manage.”

Rice is one of three England players nominated for the Ballon d’Or this week, with Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane. The ceremony, traditionally in Paris, will take place in London on 26 October as a tribute to Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the inaugural award in 1956, and Rice has backed Kane to become the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001. “I would Iove to see Harry win it,” he said. “So I’m wishing him all the best in that.”

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley breaks silence on West Ham saga and insists this isn’t over yet
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley breaks silence on West Ham saga and insists this isn’t over yet

Amanda Staveley has expressed her ‘disappointment’ at PCP Capital Partners’ failed attempt to invest in West Ham United.

The British business executive, alongside husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, was keen on a return to football having spearheaded the Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund takeover of Newcastle United in October 2021.



4 Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi saw their efforts to invest in West Ham foiled Credit: Getty

West Ham have seen substantial change in recent years with Daniel Kretinsky playing a more influential role in the boardroom since his investment in 2021.

In a statement released on Friday, Staveley revealed that PCP’s original offer ‘was for both David Sullivan’s 38.8 per cent stake and Vanessa Gold’s 25 per cent stake’ in the Championship club.

But the pre-emption process that provided Kretinsky the opportunity to match PCP’s offer has now been accepted.



Therefore, Kretinsky and Sullivan will retain majority control of West Ham.

And while Staveley, who co-owned Newcastle between 2021 and 2024, openly revealed her disappointment at the outcome, her ambitions for the club remain open.



What did Amanda Staveley say about PCP’s failed takeover of West Ham?

"We are obviously disappointed not to have been successful in our bid to acquire the 25% shareholding in West Ham United," Staveley said in a statement.

"For transparency our original offer was for both David Sullivan's 38.8% stake and Vanessa Gold's 25.1% stake in the club.



"There was always the potential that the other shareholders would take up their rights under the shareholders agreement which is what they have elected to do.

"From the outset we and our global investment partners approached this opportunity with enormous respect for West Ham, its history, identity and most importantly loyal and committed supporters.

"We saw real potential to make a positive difference, rejuvenate the club and help West Ham compete consistently at the highest level of English football.

4 Czech businesman Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the majority owner at West Ham Credit: Getty



4 Kretinsky and David Sullivan will retain majority control of the Championship club Credit: Getty

"Mehrdad and I along with our partners retain the greatest respect for the West Ham community who supported us both in the stands and online in recent weeks.

"We will continue to follow this process closely. Our ambitions for the club remain and we would be open to the opportunity to work constructively with the existing shareholders in the future subject to use not taking up other opportunities that have been present to our consortium in the week of events over the past week."

The outcome may come as a huge disappointment to sections of the club’s fanbase who have grown disillusioned with the ongoing ownership saga.



There were also promises of significant investment in the squad this summer that failed to materialise.

But the much-needed conclusion to the tale has been welcomed by the Hammers’ Fan Advisory Board who hope the decision will create stability at the club.

“The West Ham United Fan Advisory Board welcomes the announcement confirming the significant change in the Club’s shareholding and Daniel Kretinsky becoming West Ham United’s largest individual shareholder,” its statement read.

4 West Ham's Fan Advisory Board have called for stability at the club Credit: Getty



“After a prolonged period of uncertainty, we hope this represents an important moment of stability and the beginning of a new chapter for our Club.

“We particularly welcome Daniel Křetínský’s acknowledgement of the responsibility that comes with his position and his commitment to communicate further with supporters once the transactions are complete.

“Change of control must now mean change of direction. We also look forward to clarity around the role David Sullivan may or may not play outside of being a shareholder.

"He resigned from the board and we would hope that position remains the same going forward.



“West Ham United supporters have demonstrated extraordinary loyalty to this Club, including more than 50,000 committing to season tickets following relegation. They now deserve to hear a clear, ambitious and credible vision for the future.

“That vision must explain how West Ham intends to return to the Premier League and establish itself there sustainably; the strategy for football, recruitment and the Academy; the future of the London Stadium and matchday experience; and how supporters will be genuinely placed at the heart of the Club.

“The FAB has consistently called for West Ham United to be run as a modern, professional and ambitious football club, with experienced executives empowered to manage its day-to-day operations and clear strategic leadership from the Board. We now have an opportunity to continue to make that a reality.

“The FAB welcomes this new chapter and wishes Daniel Křetínský and the Club’s leadership every success.



“The uncertainty must now give way to stability. The change in ownership must be followed by clear leadership. And very soon, supporters must be shown the vision for the West Ham United we are all trying to build.”

Sports.title: Why there is no 12:30pm Premier League kick-off this Saturday with Arsenal clash moved
Sports.content:
Why there is no 12:30pm Premier League kick-off this Saturday with Arsenal clash moved

For the first time this season, there will be no early kick-off in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.

Fans have been treated to three brilliant 12:30pm matches so far this term, but they're going to have to wait for their football this weekend.

2 Arsenal's clash with Sunderland was moved, meaning there is no early kick-off Credit: Getty

In the opening Saturday of the campaign, Hull City shocked Manchester United, with the newly-promoted side winning 2-0.

And goals galore followed, with Liverpool and Nottingham Forest drawing 2-2 before Newcastle and Bournemouth did the same last weekend.

However, there is no early game to look forward to this weekend, meaning fans have to patiently wait for the action...

Why is there no early kick-off this Saturday?

The Premier League have shuffled the schedule on Saturday due to the European football being played in midweek.

Sunderland vs Arsenal is taking place at 8pm, exclusively live on talkSPORT, after the match was confirmed to be rescheduled in July.

The match at the Stadium of Light was moved two months ago as the league pre-empted that the Gunners would be playing in the Champions League in the days prior.

Mikel Arteta's side beat Napoli 1-0 in Italy on Wednesday evening.

Sunderland vs Arsenal was also selected for TV coverage on TNT Sports, with the broadcaster only able to use the 12:30pm and 8pm slots.

Typically, if a game can't be played early on a Saturday due to a team playing in Europe on a Wednesday or Thursday, they will instead broadcast the fixture in their late slot.

In this case, Sunderland vs Arsenal was switched to the 8pm slot, which has left the early kick-off empty this weekend.

Premier League schedule this weekend Saturday, September 12 Liverpool vs Fulham - 3pm

Crystal Palace vs Ipswich - 3pm

Bournemouth vs Brentford - 3pm

Aston Villa vs Nottingham Forest - 3pm

Chelsea vs Hull - 3pm

Tottenham vs Everton - 5:30pm

Sunderland vs Arsenal - 8pm - live on talkSPORT Sunday, September 13 Coventry vs Brighton - 1pm

Manchester United vs Manchester City - 4:30pm Monday, September 14 Leeds vs Newcastle - 8pm - live on talkSPORT

Arsenal's busy schedule

Arsenal will appreciate some extra recovery time following their clash with Napoli as they begin a chaotic few days.

The Gunners are set to play three games in six days, starting with the Champions League match on Wednesday night.

After that, they take on Sunderland on Saturday, before then coming up against Ipswich in the Carabao Cup third round.

That cup fixture will take place on Tuesday, September 15, with commentary from the Emirates live on talkSPORT.

Meanwhile, Sunderland are also having to play three games in seven days, as the schedule starts to get busy in England.

But their toughest clash comes this weekend...

Sports.title: ‘Amazing story’ – How Loris Karius bounced back from night that almost ended his career
Sports.content:
‘Amazing story’ – How Loris Karius bounced back from night that almost ended his career

Loris Karius' nightmare 2018 Champions League final could have spelt the end of his top-level career.

The then-Liverpool goalkeeper – who it later transpired had been concussed earlier in the game – was at fault for two of the goals the Reds conceded in a 3-1 defeat to Real Madrid in Kyiv, receiving death threats after the game.

2 Karius is now first choice between the sticks for Miron Muslic's Schalke Credit: Getty

Karius never played for Liverpool again, but the 33-year-old has gone on to revive his career and is currently impressing for Schalke in his native Germany, helping them win promotion back to the Bundesliga as second-tier champions last season.

'An amazing story'

And it's 'amazing' to see him back at the highest level, says European football expert Andy Brassell. He told talkSPORT: "What happened in Kyiv in 2018 is something that would have finished most players – and it almost did finish him.

"It blew his career off course for ages. A load of his peak disappeared while he was flitting between clubs and out of teams.

"You look at: running aground at Besiktas because they weren't paying him, then you had being a reserve at [Hertha] Berlin, being an emergency third choice at Newcastle, and then ending up in the second tier at Schalke. It's an amazing story for him to get back to where he is, really."

Karius keeps Kane out (again)

Karius produced a sensational save to deny Ballon d'Or frontrunner Harry Kane late on as Schalke held reigning German champions Bayern Munich to a 0-0 draw last time out.

In doing so, he became the first 'keeper to keep a Bundesliga clean sheet against Bayern for almost 18 months.

Matej Kovar of Bayer Leverkusen was the last do so towards the end of the 2024/25 campaign.

In that point-securing moment, it felt like Karius' career had come full circle, with Brassell alluding to a penalty he saved from Kane while playing for Liverpool a few months before the 2018 Champions League final.

"When he saved that penalty from Kane, I guess people thought he could still develop into one of the better players in the Premier League," Brassell continued.

"He'd already had that little spell at Manchester City with the [Under] 18s and 21s, which is how he knew [current Bayern boss and former Man City captain] Vincent Kompany. Kompany congratulated him personally at the end of this game [for Schalke against Bayern].

2 Karius made five saves to deny Bayern on Saturday Credit: Getty

"At that point when he was at Liverpool, you thought he was going to develop into one of the key goalkeepers in the Premier League. Then Kyiv and everything else happened."

Karius on 'great' day

Eight years later, Karius looks to be in a good place, cementing his spot as Schalke's No.1 in the top flight, with Brassell noting: "[He's] got past setbacks that would definitely end the careers or top-level careers of most players.

"For him to arrive back at this point at 33 and be able to do this is amazing."

Speaking after his heroic display at the weekend, Karius said: "It was great for me. I only had to shout to keep going, move up, drop back.

"Real credit to the guys for what they did. They kept so much away and made things so incredibly hard for Bayern. The guys really worked hard until they couldn't go anymore. Everyone today can be proud of their performance."

He also drew praise from his opposite number, goalkeeping legend and Schalke academy graduate Manuel Neuer, who said: "Loris Karius was very good and definitely the right choice for man of the match.

"We had three big chances that he kept out. That was definitely key to us not winning this game."

Sports.title: Darren Fletcher seen confronting abusive Man United fan immediately after Champions League win
Sports.content:
Darren Fletcher was applauded by Man United fans for putting an abusive supporter in their place on Thursday night.

The Red Devils returned to the Champions League with a 4-0 win over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah.

2 Fletcher is a hugely popular figure at United from his playing days and his time as interim manager Credit: Getty

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko and Lisandro Martinez saw Michael Carrick's side cruise to a comfortable victory.

However, there were some unsavoury scenes after the match as players made their way home from Old Trafford.

Fletcher, who is currently head coach of United's Under-18s, was seen verbally confronting a supporter near the first-team coach.

"Listen, it doesn't matter, you can't speak like that," an angry Fletcher said.

"Show some respect. You're the reason people don't sign."

It appears the argument began after Man United players decided not to stop and sign autographs.

While the fan continued to protest, it was not clear exactly what was said to spark the row.

Other supporters in the video cheered ex-United midfielder Fletcher for backing the players and chanted his name.

Manchester City next

On the pitch, Carrick watched Sesko score for the second consecutive game after his return from injury.

However, the United boss did not reveal whether the Slovenian striker would get his first Premier League start when the Red Devils host Manchester City in the derby on Sunday.

2 The return of Sesko has been a huge boost for Carrick Credit: Getty

Cunha has started up front in the top-flight so far this season, with Marcus Rashford and Patrick Dorgu utilised on the left side of attack.

"It's not an easy decision, of course it's not," Carrick said.

"But it's definitely one I'd prefer: to have goals in the team and for the boys to be playing well.

"The understanding they all have is that sometimes it's going to be a start, sometimes it's going to be finishing the game.

"We need that within the group, from game to game over the season, to be able to call upon slightly different kind of things at different times.

"It's fantastic they're all in good form and started so well."

Sports.title: England U21’s new Arjen Robben warned against Chelsea transfer from sister club
Sports.content:
Those of a Chelsea persuasion will have fond memories of Arjen Robben - the skilful, electric, tantalising former Dutch winger.

A master at beating defenders and causing danger with his left foot after drifting in from the right, Robben was a problem for defences - and England could have their own version in Sam Amo-Ameyaw.



5 Robben is renowned as one of the best wingers in football history, and English football appear to have a like-for-like player on the rise Credit: Getty

Strasbourg have turned into a hotspot for young talent and share the same owners, BlueCo, as Premier League giants Chelsea, with the club now working towards a return to the top of French football.

The Ligue 1 side operate in the transfer market with a model that prioritises the signings of promising players in their teens or early 20s over established or more experienced names.

Chelsea mostly worked in the same way up until the recent summer window, but Strasbourg haven't strayed - the average age of their 18 recent arrivals is 20.4.



Hermann Malonga, who was eyed by Manchester City, is one of those to have made the switch as he joined from Paris Saint-Germain, with Jacobo Ortega arriving after his spell at Real Madrid.

However, with the 2026/27 season now in full flow, Strasbourg have made a strong start thanks to Amo-Ameyaw, who was one of their 'class of summer 2025' signings.



A former academy talent at Tottenham Hotspur, he completed his move to Strasbourg from Southampton initially on loan before the obligation to buy, worth a reported €7million (£6m), was activated.

On Sunday, the England U21 winger came off the bench to score two goals in a 6-2 Ligue 1 win at Troyes - both saw him burst in from the right and fire past the goalkeeper, just like Robben did in his prime.



Strasbourg to Chelsea the wrong thing

Continued success at Strasbourg would spark the potential for a big-money move to their affiliates Chelsea like Mamadou Sarr and Emmanuel Emegha have done of late, as well as Valentin Barco, who scored in the thrilling 6-3 win over Leeds United on Wednesday night.

Deivid Washington - transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg *Samuels-Smith joined Strasbourg in July 2025, but transfer was reversed in September 2025

5 Amo-Ameyaw is on his way to holding down a key role for Strasbourg, and this could tee up a future move to Chelsea Credit: AFP

5 High praise has seen him be touted as the new Robben, who got amongst the goals for Chelsea, Madrid, Bayern and the Netherlands by cutting onto his left with ease Credit: Getty

But when European football journalist Andy Brassell reflected on his display against Troyes, he argued that, despite the glitz and glamour of the Premier League, Amo-Ameyaw should stay put.



Brassell compared the 20-year-old to the Chelsea hero and Dutch legend Robben, who also starred for European giants such as Real Madrid and Bayern Munich.

Robben scored 246 goals and recorded 200 assists for FC Groningen, PSV Eindhoven, Chelsea, Madrid, Bayern and the Netherlands with his unique and effective skill set - the fact that Amo-Ameyaw has been likened to him is nothing but encouraging.

"Sam Amo-Ameyaw coming on and finishing the game, really, against Troyes, the 'multi-club derby' between Troyes and Strasbourg," he told talkSPORT.com.

"Strasbourg had a bit of a rough start in the first half; they went a goal down and were under pressure for a little bit, but they recovered from it really well.



"When they came back into the game, Amo-Ameyaw was great when he came on. He went from them having an advantage in the game to then completely killing it.

"He contributed nicely on many occasions last season, but you know when you can see a player has really taken a step up? He came on in this game, scored two goals on his left foot coming in from the right-hand side that Arjen Robben would have been proud of.

"Two brilliant goals, the talent is absolutely clear. It's just, with Strasbourg, you don't know if it's going to be kept in the place where it should develop for long enough.

5 Amo-Ameyaw made 12 appearances for Southampton, and two of those were in the Premier League Credit: Getty



"If there was some sort of Chelsea swoop for him in five months, or four months, or 12 months, it wouldn't surprise me, but it would probably be the wrong thing at this point in time.

"He's a really interesting player, I wouldn't want him to become just another commodity, I really enjoy watching him."

Brassell then assessed Amo-Ameyaw's chances of playing at senior level for England if he sustains an upward trajectory at Strasbourg.

He has already earned 46 total appearances across Three Lions youth sides, two of which have come at the second-highest level with the U21s.



"I guess if we're looking at it from an eventual England perspective, it is quite hard to see where you go," Brassell explained.

"We've got Bukayo Saka, Cole Palmer, we've talked about Nwaneri who, if he has a good season at (Borussia Dortmund, on loan from Arsenal), might be in the mix too.

"So, Amo-Ameyaw just needs to concentrate on having a really, really good season at club level and then take it from there.

"But, given that they lost Gary O'Neil as their coach and they lost some big players, it is an opportunity for him and for them. I think they've looked really quite decent over these last couple of weeks."

Sports.title: Stunned Fenerbahce player has to double take during interview after learning manager resigned
Sports.content:
Stunned Fenerbahce player has to double take during interview after learning manager resigned

Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown couldn't believe what he heard when told his manager had instantly quit post-match.

Ismail Kartal announced that he would be resigning from his post straight after a draw with Roma in the Champions League.



4 Brown was completely baffled by the news that his manager had quit

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Kartal shockingly confirmed that he would be stepping down.

It caught everyone off guard - even his own players - with Brown being left completely baffled during his own interview.

As he stood in front of journalist, he was told by a translator from the Fenerbahce staff that Kartal had left.



And as soon as he heard, Brown quickly swung his head around with a confused expression, asking: "What do you mean he resigned?"

The Birmingham-born defender then looked around as he took the news in, with it being confirmed that Kartal announced he had quit during his press conference.



Brown then asked again, to make sure nothing had been lost in translation. "He quit as coach?

"What do you mean by resigned... he's not coach anymore?"

Clarifying it had happened in his press conference around the same time as he was speaking, he added: "I didn't know about this."



Kartal's resignation marked a disappointing end to a productive night for Brown, who had scored in Fenerbahce's draw.

In fact, the left-back won the Player of the Match award following the 1-1- draw with Serie A side Roma in Istanbul.

His strike just after half time helped his side claim a point in their league phase opener.

4 Kartal quit his job when speaking to the media post-match on Thursday Credit: Getty



Why did Ismail Kartal resign?

Fenerbahce manager Kartal left his job minutes after the full-time whistle and vowed never to return to the club.

This was his fourth stint in charge of the Turkish giants.

“I am resigning from my position while there is still time," he said. "I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return.

“I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players… our president and managers tried to help us in every way. Those were wonderful days.

"As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position.



“Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today.

4 Birmingham born Brown has never played in England but that has not stopped him competing at the highest level of club football in the Champions League Credit: Getty

4 Brown scored as his club returned to the Champions League and he will come up against Aston Villa next Credit: Getty

“I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.”



Where is Archie Brown from?

The 24-year-old has never played professionally in England having come through West Brom and Derby academies.

He left England at the age of 18 in 2021 to join Swiss side Lausanne-Sport.

He then moved to Belgium to play for Gent where he was called up to the England U20 squad before joining Turkish side Fenerbahce in 2025 where there a number of familiar faces to Premier League fans are playing.

He has cited former Arsenal and Chelsea defender Ashley Cole as the standard bearer for left-backs and even got to train with him as Cole was winding down his career at Derby.



"What stood out to me the most was his approach to the game," he told Sky Sports.

"I saw his ability to laugh and joke in the changing room, but when he stepped on the training pitch or a game, it's like a switch flicks and he's able to get into that zone."

He has previously spoken of his desire to play in the Champions League, which he is now doing as well as competing for titles whether that is in the Premier League or on the continent.

Sports.title: Gary Neville names Man United's 'best XI' for the derby against Man City - and includes one of three players 'they were banking on selling' this summer
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has offered Michael Carrick selection advice ahead of Manchester United's derby clash with Manchester City, naming the Red Devils' 'best XI' for the Old Trafford contest. United host their arch rivals on Sunday at 4.30pm, with Carrick looking to get one over their neighbours again having masterminded a 2-0 win over Pep Guardiola's side in January this year. Enzo Maresca is now in the dugout for the visitors who boast a perfect record after three Premier League matches, sitting top of the table alongside reigning champions Arsenal. United meanwhile. have endured a bumpy start to the league campaign - dropping points against newly-promoted Hull City as well as Everton thus far. And club legend Neville has given his view on how Carrick should line up for the mouthwatering contest this weekend, including Marcus Rashford in his starting team - a player he insists the club were 'banking on selling' this summer. 'Senne Lammens, Diogo Dalot, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martínez, Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo, and then the front four of Marcus Rashford, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes. To me, that is Manchester United's best eleven,' he said on Big Game Preview, sponsored by Sky Bet. Gary Neville has offered selection advice to Man United boss Michael Carrick

'Manchester United banked on sales that never materialised in the transfer market. It is a big point on the selling side, because they wouldn't have expected Marcus Rashford to be back, and Manuel Ugarte got injured. 'They would have expected Joshua Zirkzee to leave for maybe 10, 15 or 20 million pounds, so they were banking on bringing in that 50, 60 million [pounds], and they didn't bring any of that money in.' Neville also singled out a key personnel decision Carrick will face when new £70million signing Carlos Baleba returns to fitness. 'The only thing I can see happening eventually is that we'll have to drop one of that front four and play three in midfield,' he said. 'Maybe Youri Tielemans, Carlos Beleba and Kobbie Mainoo, adding an extra midfield player. That means sometimes Bruno has to go to the side, which isn't ideal because I think he's better in that number ten spot. 'But how do we [Manchester United], without changing shape, become more solid so we don't concede every single game? Because if we carry on conceding like this, we won't be in the Champions League. We have to stop conceding goals.'

Sports.title: West Ham footballer Edson Alvarez forced to deny bombshell claims linking him to a KIDNAPPING plot
Sports.content:
West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez says he 'categorically rejects' allegations linking him to an alleged kidnapping plot. Mexican film-maker Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez had publicly made the allegations earlier this week in an interview with TVNotas. Ordonez claimed he was kidnapped in November 2024, with two people forcing their way into his car before blindfolding him and threatening him with weapons. He stated that his attackers had also inserted a syringe into his neck, with his kidnappers claiming they were acting under orders from Alvarez's then father-in-law Jonathan Toache Bedolla. Ordonez said bystanders had helped him to escape and that he reported the incident to the police. He claimed Alvarez was not directly involved in his kidnapping but was aware of the plot. West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez says he 'categorically rejects' allegations he was involved in an alleged kidnapping plot The film-maker alleged he is owed 3.5million pesos (£152,000) by Alvarez following working on a documentary about the Mexico captain, which was claimed to have been produced ahead of the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. Ordonez said he asked for payment in 2024 and alleged he was also involved in a dispute with Alvarez's father-in-law over a property he owned at the time. He claimed Alvarez's then father-in-law paid to have the investigation stopped. Alvarez has posted a lengthy response on social media to deny Ordonez's claims and has vowed to take legal action against the 'false allegations'. 'In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly,' Alvarez wrote. 'I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me. 'Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me. 'Until now, I had chosen not to respond. However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line. 'If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it. Alvarez released a statement on Instagram to deny claims made by Mexican filmmaker Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez in an interview this week 'Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritizes sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth. 'I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure. Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me. 'I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner's father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported. 'Throughout nearly ten years of my professional career, I have made every effort to stay away from media scandals and to have my name recognized for my work both on and off the pitch. I come from a hardworking and honorable family that taught me that a reputation is built over many years through hard work, discipline, and conduct. For that very reason, I will not allow mine to be irresponsibly used to involve me in matters that are entirely unrelated to me. 'My priority is, and will continue to be, where it has always been: my daughters, my family, and my professional career.' Alvarez, who has made 102 appearances for Mexico, captained his national team at this summer's World Cup. The 28-year-old was expected to leave West Ham in the transfer window but failed to seal a move. Alvarez has made 74 appearances for the Hammers since joining from Ajax in 2023.
