Sports.title: Darren Fletcher puts 'abusive' Man United autograph-hunters in their place: Coach shouts back after angry fans attacked players for not stopping when they wanted to meet their heroes
Sports.content:
Darren Fletcher puts 'abusive' Man United autograph-hunters in their place: Coach shouts back after angry fans attacked players for not stopping when they wanted to meet their heroes

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United coach Darren Fletcher hit back at an 'abusive' fan after players did not stop to sign autographs following their Champions League win over Sabah.

Footage shared on social media showed Fletcher walking over to a section of Man United supporters, who had been waiting close to the team buses after their 4-0 win at Old Trafford on Thursday night.

Fletcher, who is currently the head coach of Man United's Under-18 side, specifically picked out one supporter having taken exception to their language towards players.

The fan had allegedly been abusive towards players as they made their way home post-match, after Man United stars had refused to stop to sign autographs.

'Hey listen, it doesn't matter you can't speak like that,' Fletcher said, prompting cheers from other Man United supporters in attendance.

Fletcher then pointed at the fan and stated: 'You are the reason people don't sign, you are the reason people don't sign.'

Darren Fletcher took aim at an 'abusive' autograph hunter after Man United's victory over Sabah in the Champions League

The fan had reportedly been angered by Man United players refusing to sign autographs

Darren Fletcher put a fan in his place after the Sabah game. The fan was abusive towards players when they didnt stop.#mufc pic.twitter.com/F7xySUClpW — StrettyEnd (@_StrettyEnd) September 10, 2026

His intervention led to fans chanting 'legend, legend' in support of Fletcher as he walked away.

Fletcher, now 42, has been head coach of Man United's Under-18 side since July last year.

He briefly stepped up to have a two-game spell as interim manager last January after Ruben Amorim's sacking, before Michael Carrick took charge.

During his career, Fletcher had made 342 appearances and scored 24 goals for Man United.

He won five Premier League titles, the Champions League and FA Cup during his playing career at Old Trafford.

Fletcher's former team-mate Patrice Evra previously claimed Sir Alex Ferguson had once torn into his players after failing to sign autographs when on a pre-season tour.

While players have been criticised in recent years for refusing to stop to sign autographs, Daily Mail Sport has previously revealed that Man United have grown increasingly frustrated with professional autograph hunters.

Concerns have previously been raised that players have been harangued as part of ‘industrial-scale autograph harvesting’ at Old Trafford, with signed memorabilia then being sold.

Manchester United had earned a 4-0 win over Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday

Man United had recorded a comfortable 4-0 win on Thursday night on their return to the Champions League.

First half goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko had seen the Red Devils storm into a 3-0 lead against tournament newcomers Sabah.

Lisandro Martinez added a fourth in the second half against their opponents from Azerbaijan.

The Red Devils will now turn their attentions to Sunday's Manchester derby.

Sports.title: Darts star Michael van Gerwen credits his messy DIVORCE for four-and-a-half stone weight loss in remarkable body transformation - after a long-time friend 'pulled a trick' and got his wife pregnant while they were still married
Sports.content:
Michael van Gerwen believes the 'stress' of his messy divorce is behind his remarkable body transformation – with the darts star shedding four-and-a-half stone in the wake of his split.

Van Gerwen, 37, a three-time world champion, confirmed back in May last year that he and partner Daphne had separated after more than ten years of marriage.

Daphne announced in December that she had fallen pregnant with her new boyfriend, Robert, after their new relationship 'overlapped' with her marriage to van Gerwen.

Robert later admitted that he had 'pulled a trick' on his old friend, with van Gerwen saying 'I'm just human, you know. At some point, you want to think about nice things again, not just be preoccupied with the mess you're experiencing at that moment.

The pair, who began dating in 2008 and tied the knot in 2014, have two children together - Mike and Zoe - and the Dutchman spent a period of time away from the oche as he attempted to deal with his new reality.

The Dutchman has returned to the sport, showing off a slimmed-down new look. He told fans on a recent live stream that the divorce played a major role in his weight loss.

'How much weight did I lose? 28 kilos,' he said.

Michael van Gerwen has credited his dramatic weight loss to his divorce from his ex-wife

Michael van Gerwen with Spurs cult hero Heurelho Gomes after shedding weight

Van Gerwen and ex-wife Daphne (left) split after 10 years together

'I used to always eat after the darts when I went back. I used to eat badly all the time. I never do it anymore.

'And guys, to lose weight, very good, very good. I have some very good advice: just divorce. That's so much stress. Doesn't matter. Easy.'

He also revealed that he has never been a beer drinker, preferring wine.

He added: 'I don't mind a good glass of wine, guys. I never drink beer in my life. It's disgusting.

'But a good glass of wine, especially with a nice dinner when you're with friends and things like that, I think it's really nice.'

In an interview last year, Robert confirmed he and Daphne had known each other 'for a long time' and had 'always clicked' before the start of their relationship.

'That's when the spark ignited,' Robert told Shownieuws. 'It wasn't the intention but it happened.

'We didn't want to offend anyone, let me be clear about that. We didn't want to hurt anyone, not Michael, not anyone. It happened. It turned out a little differently than expected.'

Daphne added: 'But not everything that's been posted online is true.

'I just want to say that (Robert) had already broken up with his ex (when the pair started their relationship).'

Van Gerwen's ex-wife Daphne Govers and her boyfriend Robert broke their silence in an interview on Dutch television

Daphne did confirm that she believed that she was friends with her ex-husband, while Robert stressed that he has 'respect' for Van Gerwen, meeting the darts player often due to the custody arrangement for his two children Zoe and Mike.

'I find it difficult,' Robert added. 'Of course, I pulled that trick on him, and I'm not proud of it.

'But hey, I chose my own happiness, and he's welcome here.'

The interview also saw Daphne share details about the 'miracle' child she and her new boyfriend are set to welcome in January – eight months after her May separation.

'I didn't expect it. I was at the hospital with the other two, too,' Daphne said. 'I couldn't have gotten pregnant naturally. If it does happen, it'll be a miracle.

'My world was completely turned upside down. How am I going to handle this? But in the end, it all worked out. It's more than welcome.'

When asked about how van Gerwen feels about the pregnancy, she replied: 'I wouldn't dare say. I don't think very happy, but I really don't know.'

Sports.title: Why Man City are fired up to end their Old Trafford hoodoo: Squad unity, the star duo drumming standards into newcomers and the missing ingredient players say Enzo Maresca has added ahead of Man United clash
Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi has done his homework. He looks a little bit bookish, so that stands to reason.

Aside from naming no fewer than four Manchester City midfielders – Messrs Toure, De Bruyne, Gundogan and Rodri – when asked for a Premier League idol growing up, the 18-year-old born just north of Paris studiously learned his lines on this weekend’s derby.

‘The most important game of the year,’ Bouaddi said softly but deliberately. ‘It means a lot for the fans and for us. We will give everything for this game.’

Watching the togetherness of City’s squad in recent weeks, particularly in Porto’s white-hot cauldron of aggravation on Tuesday, it feels like a hop across town to Manchester United is exactly what they crave. To roll on to the next big event, riding a wave.

Erling Haaland and Gianluigi Donnarumma, two deputies of captain Ruben Dias, are said to be drumming in the standards of the club to the new signings in the hope they can integrate quickly. Haaland is becoming more vocal and has started this season boisterously.

And listening to Bouaddi, the recent recruits have clearly taken heed.

Erling Haaland celebrates his second goal in Man City's 2-0 win over Porto. The Norwegian has become noticeably more vocal this season

City's Ayyoub Bouaddi already knows the importance of Sunday's derby. 'It means a lot for the fans and for us,' he said. 'We will give everything for this game’

Sunday's derby probably comes a touch too soon in the reign of Enzo Maresca to draw any real conclusions on the ultimate direction of the team this season but it is an opportunity to lay down a marker that the status quo up here is not changing just because the messiah took his leave into the Catalonian sunset.

In fact, there is definitely something for the Italian to improve upon – and it is not often we will be able to say that when comparing to the Guardiola era. The record at Old Trafford is patchy at best.

Of the stadiums that City have visited more than once over the last seven campaigns, they’ve only fared worse at Tottenham. It’s an average of a point a game in north London – four defeats, two wins, one draw.

Only marginally better is the 1.14 points-per-game at United. Exactly the same number as Anfield, even though the fortunes of those two clubs have been worlds apart.

Two wins, two draws and three defeats since 2019 simply does not tally with City’s supremacy over their crosstown rivals. They haven’t scored a goal there since 2023, were wretched amid a defensive injury crisis in January – Michael Carrick’s first game in caretaker charge – and both sides were frankly horrible in a dour goalless draw the year before.

There has been acrimony over refereeing calls, not least the infamous Marcus Rashford non-offside that tipped the scales of a game in City's Treble-winning year. Haaland once kicked into gear in this fixture too. But the overriding feeling is that City rarely do themselves justice four miles away near Salford Quays.

When losing (in 2020, 2023 and 2026), City had all of the ball. Not a fair chunk, pretty much all of it. An average of 70 per cent – but they were eventually picked off by a team adept at counter-attacking rather than taking ownership of proceedings.

Bryan Mbeumo celebrates giving Manchester United the lead in the derby in January this year

Pep Guardiola's poor record at Old Trafford is one of the few things Enzo Maresca could feasibly improve upon

A mixture of doing little with possession, too pedestrian and risk averse, and then missing key defenders has generally done for them.

Remarkably, John Stones was injured for all three defeats. Ruben Dias missed the last two and in 2020, the absence of Aymeric Laporte was acutely felt.

That cocktail produces a sour taste and it is a strange quirk that the Emirates and Stamford Bridge are eminently happier hunting grounds for City.

The anaemic displays at Old Trafford almost mirror the diminishing lustre of this fixture and on Thursday, it was a decade to the day since Guardiola travelled to meet Jose Mourinho’s United for the very first time and Manchester took its place as the epicentre of the world game.

The anticipation ahead of that meeting has not been matched anywhere in the intervening years.

Maybe there is a responsibility on the current incumbents to bring back some vigour. Not off the pitch, not the media barbs, because neither appear interested in those, but in the style of the show, a blood-and-thunder that once was a prerequisite.

Carrick is unlikely to be able to engineer that this time, given United’s start to the season. Maresca, though, possesses a chance to continue the feeling of building a team in his image, to piggyback on the sense of achievement from Porto.

The little brawl in the tunnel will not have done them any harm at all in that respect. The way they defend will offer spaces for the likes of Bruno Fernandes to exploit but City are also creating heaps of chances.

‘Maresca has brought so much energy,’ says City's Matheus Nunes of his manager (pictured). ‘I feel like there is a new energy around. I think we needed that'

‘He (Maresca) has brought so much energy,’ said Matheus Nunes. ‘I feel like there is a new energy around. I think we needed that.

'He came with a lot of enthusiasm, he knows the standards of the club as he was here before and won everything. He’s got everything he needs to succeed, and I hope this season shows it.’

That has transmitted to the players. It is self-evident in the way they have talked and behaved over the first month. Most of them are looking for a first win at United and those sort of firsts can galvanise the older guard.

City go to their old foes with the fire to change the record.

Sports.title: How nepo-baby Ben Shelton became US tennis' new superstar: Big-hitting American downed Carlos Alcaraz, is dating NBA legend Dennis Rodman's daughter and is now on the cusp of a $10MILLION brand deal after New York exploits
Sports.content:
If you had told Ben Shelton he would play the second US Open semi-final of his career tonight in July, he might not have believed you. The 23-year-old had endured a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it first-round exit at Wimbledon and he was frustrated.

‘It's been a weird season for me this year,’ Shelton admitted. He had three titles under his belt, but a string of early exits where it mattered - the majors and Masters. There were so many things that disappointed him in his game.

But two months is a long time in tennis. Shelton started August by defending his Canadian Open title, before taking his form to New York and beating Carlos Alcaraz in a late-night instant classic.

His meeting on Friday evening with fellow American Frances Tiafoe is not the first time he’s been at this stage. In 2023, he was a gregarious upstart one year into his career, with the unvarnished gifts, and ego, of a champion-in-waiting. He had a controversial celebration: hanging up the phone on his opponents. He had hyped himself before the tournament saying he was looking to become players feared in the draw. And Shelton was, until Novak Djokovic hung up on him, winning in straight sets.

At 20 years old, Shelton had become box office. A tennis nepo-baby, Shelton is the son of former tour journeyman Bryan Shelton, but as a child, saw the family business as ‘boring’, preferring American football or basketball. It’s no stretch to imagine the left arm that provides his 146mph serve attached to an NFL quarterback. After he switched full focus to tennis at 13 however, Bryan now sits in his box as coach.

Add to family lore the draw of Shelton being one-half of one of American sportiest power couples. Since sliding into his Instagram DMs in early 2025, USWNT star Trinity Rodman - daughter of NBA legend Dennis - is a frequent fixture on tour, with Shelton pitchside for her Washington Spirit matches when the ATP’s gruelling schedule allows.

Ben Shelton's courageous showing in his US Open quarter-final against Alcaraz has given him a shot at the final

The 23-year-old has reached this stage before in 2023 (left) - before Novak Djokovic hung up on him to win his 24th Grand Slam

Shelton is now frequently accompanied by his girlfriend Trinity Rodman - a blockbuster USA athlete in her own right

All this has brought Shelton attention, celebrity and riches - after three years wearing Roger Federer’s ON brand, he is reportedly set to ink a $10million deal with New Balance - but results? That’s where things get more complicated.

Shelton has been dogged by inconsistencies, particularly at the Grand Slams. In Paris, he has never made it past the fourth round, and Wimbledon’s 2025 quarter-final is an outlier amid early exits. Never mind that he has titles on both of the natural surfaces. When asked to perform on the biggest stages, his standout attributes can turn into fatal flaws.

‘That’s the challenge, working with a guy like Ben, who is very aggressive,’ his father said in July. ‘There are times when he crosses that line and sabotages himself, and doesn’t make it to the second or third round of the tournament.’

But the win against Alcaraz showed the soaring height of his ceiling. The biggest weapon is his serve. Keeping himself in top condition to deploy it leaves him covered in cupping marks. Shelton is devoted to the traditional Chinese medicine technique for recovery and would sooner skip tending to his arm than Samson would book in for a buzzcut.

Shelton is also a superior athlete, and proved he was able to match Alcaraz’s lightning-quick movement with his own work-rate, chasing down shots which should have been impossible, and getting them back over the net with flair.

If Shelton can play like he did against the Spaniard twice more, he could end American’s 23-year wait for a home men’s Grand Slam winner. But to do that, he has to pass another psychological test by defeating his close friend Tiafoe. Tiafoe is a three-time finalist and a fellow showman who saves his very best for his home Slam.

Like Shelton, Tiafoe saw out his own five-set comeback epic to reach the semi-finals, and having met twice before, their head-to-head at the tournament sits tantalisingly at one win apiece.

He has met US Open semi-final rival - and fellow American - Frances Tiafoe twice before at their home Grand Slam (pictured in 2023)

After beating Alcaraz, Rodman prompted Shelton to bring back his once-iconic celebration - his confidence has hit new heights at just the right time

The final series of their trilogy has added potency, their clash guaranteeing a Black US Open men’s finalist for the first time on Arthur Ashe since, well, Arthur Ashe in 1972. History is on the line.

But Shelton’s form has been cresting, and he will come into their contest buoyed up by his meeting with Alcaraz with lethal confidence.

At 3.34am on Wednesday morning, Shelton looked up to his player’s box. There, Rodman cheekily picked up the phone, like it was 2023 again. Shelton has learned a lot in three years. But he still answered.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am in November: Welsh government set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am in November: Welsh government set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cardiff's Principality Stadium now looks set to be the unlikely winner of the venue war for boxing's biggest fight - by hosting Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury in the early hours of the morning.

The Welsh government could today approve lifting the stadium's 10.30pm curfew to host the fight - stepping in after rows over holding it at Wembley Stadium or Madison Square Garden in New York.

Cardiff has history of hosting late-night boxing. Joe Calzaghe fought Mikkel Kessler at the Principality in 2007 at 2am. Fury and Joshua could fight at a similar time to satisfy broadcaster Netflix's huge audience in the United States.

Netflix had wanted the fight in New York to suit their prime timezones, while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn pitched Wembley to host under the guise that Britain's biggest fight of the century should be hosted in the UK - and he has refused to budge unless contracts are rewritten with upgraded financial offerings.

Cardiff now appears to be the compromise. The Principality Stadium has an 80,000 capacity and a retractable roof - unlike Wembley - which could be useful in late November. A date of Saturday, November 28 has been mooted.

The Times report a press conference is tentatively scheduled for next week pending the Welsh government's approval.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could now be set to fight in Cardiff, Wales in November

Joshua and his camp wanted the fight in the UK - while broadcasters Netflix wanted a US host

Wembley looked an ideal venue for the fight but the strict 11pm curfew has been a sticking point, despite London mayor Sadiq Khan saying he wanted to ensure allowances were made to host the fight.

Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has been insistent on a start time of 2am.

Netflix have been running s for Fury-Joshua as recently as Thursday night, clearly confident an agreement will be struck.

The streaming giant has yet to sign off on Cardiff but American sportswriter Dan Rafael last night reported he had asked Netflix if they would approve, with a source telling him: 'I think they're OK.'

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union said: 'We'd be delighted to host this fight.

'We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.'

Joe Calzaghe trains at the Principality Stadium before his 2am fight there in 2007

Joshua has fought in Cardiff twice previously, beating Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker in the Welsh capital in 2017 and 2018.

While Joshua has left Hearn to do the talking on his side of the deal, Fury has been publicly speaking and threatening that the heavyweight contest will be called off.

This week he suggested he will no longer be fighting Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continued.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

Provided Cardiff hits no further stumbling blocks, the Welsh capital may now offer the solution to get the fight on at last.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Conor Benn hits out at 'spoiled brat' Ryan Garcia ahead of Las Vegas world title showdown - as Brit dismisses concerns over huge weight cut on eve of clash with 'insecure' rival
Sports.content:
Conor Benn hits out at 'spoiled brat' Ryan Garcia ahead of Las Vegas world title showdown - as Brit dismisses concerns over huge weight cut on eve of clash with 'insecure' rival

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Conor Benn knows there is a sizeable question hanging over him before he even gets into the ring with Ryan Garcia this weekend: can he still make 147lb?

Benn has not fought at welterweight for more than four years, having moved up through the divisions before competing at middleweight during his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Now, for the biggest fight of his career, taking on Garcia for the World Boxing Council (WBC) title under the bright lights in Las Vegas, he has to come all the way back down.

'I can't wait. It's going to be hard,' Benn told Daily Mail Sport during camp. 'I know it's going to be hard, but I believe I can do it.

'I think a lot of people are banking on the weight being an issue and me not having made 147 for four years. Ultimately, my discipline will prevail, and I'll continue to show why I can do what people say I can't do.'

Whether the weight cut affects Benn's strength and power on Saturday night will be one of the central questions of his WBC world title fight.

Conor Benn works out at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas ahead of his showdown with Garcia

Garcia has suggested Benn's move back down could leave him vulnerable, but Benn is dismissive of that concern.

'You think I've been up at middleweight, mixed it with someone who's competed at super middleweight? You think I'm worried about what a lightweight can do to me?' he said.

'You think I'm concerned in the slightest about this guy? I'm not concerned about one little thing he brings to the table… that silly left hook of his is useless. He can bring whatever he wants. It don't concern me.'

Benn's unusual route to this fight has been shaped by his rivalry with Eubank.

Their first meeting at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April 2025 was the culmination of years of animosity between the two families, with Benn and Eubank Jr inheriting a rivalry that began with their fathers in 1990.

The fight itself was fought at a catchweight above 160lb, with Benn stepping up significantly from his previous division. Eubank won a close decision, leaving Benn to reflect on a performance in which he felt the occasion and the emotion had affected him.

Benn and father Nigel at the Mandalay Bay in Vegas - this is Benn's second fight since he renewed the family feud with the Eubanks

Seven months later, the pair met again at the same venue. This time Benn won the decision, dropping Eubank twice in the final round in a dramatic conclusion to their second fight. It left them level at one victory apiece and appeared to finally close the door on one of British boxing's most talked-about rivalries.

Benn insisted the atmosphere this week is nothing like those two nights when asked whether his hatred for Garcia compared.

'This is nothing like the Eubank fight,' he said. 'The Eubank fight, there was nothing pleasant or friendly or fake about the Eubank fight. There was a lot more raw emotion in that fight and I let that get the better of me the first time. That won't happen here.'

Garcia has been happy to trade insults with his British opponent, but Benn clearly has little time for his opponent's personality.

'He just carries on like a spoiled brat, like a big child who throws his toys out of the pram,' Benn said. 'I'm not worried about him in the slightest. If anything, I'm gonna have a bit of fun with him. He's a little bit sensitive, highly emotional, and a little bit insecure.'

There is also an uncomfortable shared history between the two men when it comes to drugs testing.

Benn's original 2022 fight with Eubank was cancelled after he returned two adverse findings for clomifene, something he has consistently denied intentionally taking. Garcia subsequently returned an adverse finding for ostarine following his 2024 victory over Devin Haney, which he also denied intentionally taking.

Both men were asked at the fight's press conference whether they had concerns that the other could use performance-enhancing drugs ahead of Saturday's contest.

Neither appeared keen to make it a central issue, with the focus instead returning to the fight itself.

Ryan Garcia, Benn's opponent, has also had controversy in his career over positive drug tests

Garcia has also questioned whether Benn's career has prepared him for this level of opposition, arguing that the Briton is taking a step too far by challenging for the world title.

JEFF POWELL IN LAS VEGAS An advance guard of a couple of hundred UK fight fans arrived here in time to see Conor Benn stage a public work-out three days before he challenges Ryan Garcia for the world welterweight title in the intimidating T-Mobile Arena. They kicked up a din as Benn went through a few minutes of snappy pad work in a temporary ring pitched between a bar waiting to serve them and the MGM Grand Casino’s sports book. While admitting he can’t wait to wolf down fish and chips after all the dieting to make the 147lbs welter limit he assured them: ‘I feel great and I’ll give my all to give you all a night to remember.’ But he refrained from removing his top to give them a glimpse of his body. Both he and Garcia looked sharp and calm in their brief appearances. The Benn faithful will be heavily outnumbered on Saturday night by the Americans and Mexicans rooting for King Ry but they are in good voice.

Benn's response was typically blunt. 'How is this too far? He quit against Tank Davis. He got outclassed by Rolly [Romero], and then got a world title shot with Barrios,' he said.

'Then there is me. Stepping up to fight the contenders up at middleweight, fight of the year up at middleweight, avenging my loss. Two big stadium shows. Just come off beating a two-time former world champion and having to make 147, which again I ain't made in four years in six weeks.

'What's he talking about? Ultimately, who cares what he thinks? I don't listen to quitters anyway.'

For all the talk, though, the immediate challenge is the scales. Benn has to get himself back down to a weight he has not made since 2022, before attempting to deal with one of boxing's fastest and most dangerous punchers.

He accepts it will not be straightforward, but he remains convinced the doubts surrounding him will only add to his motivation.

'If I'd listened to everyone that didn't believe in me, I'd be nowhere,' he said. 'But I continue to believe in me. And that's all that matters… you believing in yourself. I believe in me to get me to where I am right now, to revenge that loss against Eubank, to put on Fight of the Year against Eubank, to then fight for the WBC world title.

'I don't need nobody else to believe in me. Continue to doubt me because doubt fuels the fire.'

Sports.title: Katie Taylor is crowned undisputed champion for a THIRD time with unanimous decision victory over Flora Pili - as Irish boxing icon, 40, enjoys fairytale end to her career in front of 82,000 fans at sold-out Croke Park
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

There will never be another night quite like this for Katie Taylor… or, for that matter, for boxing itself.

Under the lights at Croke Park, in front of 82,000 delirious fans, Ireland's greatest fighter walked into the ring for the final time and left it as a three-time undisputed world champion after defeating Flora Pili on points.

Taylor had dreamed of this moment for much of her life. She had spent more than a decade rewriting the history of women's boxing, collecting world titles, conquering America, avenging the only defeat of her professional career and becoming the undisputed champion not once, but twice.

But nothing could have prepared her for this.

The noise inside Croke Park was deafening as Taylor made her final walk to the ring, the 40-year-old receiving a hero's welcome before facing the undefeated Frenchwoman in the last fight of a career that has transformed boxing in Ireland and beyond.

And when the first bell rang, Taylor set about doing exactly what she had come to Croke Park to do.

Katie Taylor celebrated victory on her farewell fight to become a three-time undisputed champion

Taylor overcame the challenge of Flora Pili, who had been unbeaten in 12 fights as a professional

Taylor appeared in the ring with family and friends are wrapping up her career in style

From the opening round, she demonstrated her speed deploying a lightning-quick jab despite being 11 years older than her opponent.

It was in the second round Pili really felt Taylor's power after taking a strong right hand to the temple.

It got the fans excited but the Frenchwoman weathered the storm before receiving a slap across her face from her trainer in the corner as he urged her to 'wake up'.

Knowing she was down heavily on the scorecards Pili showed conviction in the seventh round but it was never going to be enough to topple the Irish champion.

As the tenth and final round rang in, both fighters touched gloves as a sign of respect. The crowd cheered their champion home as she drew the curtain on her career.

Taylor did everything she could to get the stoppage in the dying seconds of the fight but she had to settle for a points victory.

There was a moment after the final bell when Taylor simply stood and took it all in.

The noise, the tears, the Irish flags, the thousands of people on their feet inside Croke Park and the knowledge that this really was the end.

Taylor emerged to a stunning ovation at a sold-out Croke Park, with 82,000 in attendance

Taylor's husband Sean McCavanagh was among those watching on ringside at the venue

Westlife performed in the build-up to Taylor taking to the ring for the last time in her career

Michael Flatley was among the well-known faces in attendance on the historic night

She had wanted one final night. One final fight. One final chance to walk into the ring in front of her home crowd and remind the world exactly who she was.

She got all three.

Taylor leaves boxing as a three-time undisputed world champion, an Olympic gold medallist and one of the most important figures the sport has ever produced.

But her legacy cannot be measured in belts alone.

She changed women's boxing forever. She gave a generation of young girls a reason to believe that they belonged in a boxing gym. She carried Irish boxing on her shoulders for years and became a sporting icon far beyond the ring.

And perhaps most fittingly of all, she signed off where she had always wanted to be.

At Croke Park. In front of her people. With another world title wrapped around her waist.

The final chapter could not have been written any better.

Katie Taylor came home, became undisputed for the third time and walked away on top.

A champion to the very end.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua fight is OFF in another social media rant: Gypsy King accuses AJ of 's***ing his pants' in talks over Battle of Britain deal
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has suggested he will no longer be fighting Anthony Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continue.

The two British heavyweights had seemed set to finally face off later this year, but Fury had suggested his rival was stalling over the contractual agreements.

Joshua's promoter, Eddie Hearn, claimed last week that talks had 're-opened' – but things, if Fury is to be believed, seem to have again gone backwards.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

The bitter tug-of-war over their heavyweight superfight has largely centered on a debate around hosting it at London's Wembley Stadium or broadcaster Netflix's choice of Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

Tyson Fury (pictured) has claimed Anthony Joshua has bailed on their potential fight

Joshua (pictured) is still yet to sign the deal to fight Tyson Fury, Frank Warren has revealed, with a deadline for Sunday

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

In an address to camera, Fury accused Joshua of trying to derail their fight to avoid being embarrassed: 'If I agreed to tie both hands behind my back and wear solid cement boots, Anthony Joshua would never get in the ring with me because I'll annihilate him.

'And he's a piece of s*** bully, and that's his game—bullying people like he tried to do to Daniel Dubois, and he got knocked spark dead out.

'The latest news from them is, 'Tyson don't want to fight in England'. Why the f*** wouldn't I want to fight in England, you sausage? 'Tyson only wants to fight in America'. Are you joking or what?

'Tyson is not in charge of this fight. Tyson didn't put the money up for this fight. Tyson is not the paymaster. Netflix are and Turki Al-Sheikh. Lovely. If it's in England, even better. I'll knock the motherf***er out even quicker. Prime time England, 10 o'clock, Wembley Stadium, 100,000 people. Why the f*** wouldn't I want it in England? Doesn't make any sense, does it?

'Like I said, who do you think you are? You and your little pathetic puppet Eddie Hearn trying to save you. There's no escaping, you know. I'll come to Watford (Joshua's hometown) and I'll set about you. I'll batter you in your own front garden, you piece of s***.'

Joshua's 2020 Black Lives Matter speech was brought back up by his great boxing rival Fury

'There is no getting out of this one. There is no getting out of this one. Get ready for this fight. I've had enough of your sauce to last me 11 years. I'm battering the f*** out of you, you useless dosser, piece of s***. That's what you are. And you know it as well, and everybody else knows what you are: a coward.'

Roaring out his title of the 'Gypsy King,' Fury added: 'You's are going down, and the cash cow is getting knocked out. Because after this, he won't be able to show his face in public ever again.

'You're a useless dosser, a big bodybuilding piece of s***. Too many weights, not enough speed. When I crack a big right hook off it, you'll go over like spaghetti legs Deontay Wilder. But he's 10 times the man you'll ever be, because he's got a pair of b*****ks like King Kong, and you've got a pair of b*****ks like two f***ing garden peas, you piece of s***.'

On Sunday, Fury revealed he has turned his attention to trying to fight Oleksandr Usyk for a third time – on the back of two defeats.

'So this would only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk,' he said. 'Let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court, Oleksandr.'

He added: 'Do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits? Let me know, because I'm now looking for a new opponent.'

Fury's promoter Frank Warren, who suggested that in reality boxing's longest hatching deal had to be finalised by Sunday, told Daily Mail Sport last week: 'AJ hasn't signed yet.

'Tyson signed in January. He's training in Miami for the fight in early November and doesn't care where it takes place.'

There is debate around the contract and location of the fight, with Fury supposedly agreeing the match-up earlier this year

The original agreement stipulated England, putting Wembley Stadium on alert.

But Netflix, the mega-paymasters for the broadcast, have joined their Saudi partners in insisting on New York's fabled Madison Square Garden so as to maximise US revenue.

Joshua will need at least a two-month training camp for a fight of this magnitude and ideally nine to ten weeks.

It comes after Joshua was given ten days to agree a deal on August 26 with Warren previously warning: 'Unless AJ commits by the end of next week I'm afraid this will slip away like so many of those great fights which never happened.'

He added: 'At some point everyone has to say the most important thing is that it happens. Not this bulls*** about money.

'That everyone wants the fight. Does AJ really want it? I don't know. He's been through that tragedy of the car crash which killed two of his closest friends. Only he knows what he wants.'

Much of the discussions around Wembley centre on a willingness to allow a late start time – and late curfew – to suit the American TV market. Mayor Sadiq Khan this week stated that he is keen to host the fight and find a solution.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua's conqueror Andy Ruiz is PUMMELLED with punches and brutally beaten on his return to the ring after two years - but incredibly insists he WILL keep fighting
Sports.content:
Andy Ruiz, the man who condemned Anthony Joshua to his first ever professional defeat, suffered a horrific loss of his own on Friday night.

The 36-year-old Mexican was left bruised and bloodied as he lost to Poland's Damian Knyba on his return to the ring after two years out.

Knyba unleashed heavy punch after punch in the seventh round but Ruiz managed to ride it out, after being saved by the bell, to lose by a unanimous points decision.

Ruiz, who is now signed to British promoter Eddie Hearn, vowed to carry on despite losing his comeback fight to Knyba. The Pole now has a record of 18 wins and one defeat.

Rewind to June 2019, and Ruiz shocked the boxing world by upsetting the odds to knock Joshua out in the seventh round at Madison Square Garden.

Ruiz was a late stand-in for Jarrell Miller, who had failed a drugs test, and wasn't seen as a threat to Joshua's chances of remaining unbeaten and hanging on to his then IBF, WBO and WBA world heavyweight titles.

ANDY RUIZ IS SAVED BY THE BELL 🤯🤯🤯#TheFight | #RuizKnyba | Live NOW on DAZN and TNT ▪️ pic.twitter.com/JVQjG3KQM3 — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) September 5, 2026

Andy Ruiz kneels down in front of the referee after being on the receiving end of heavy blows

Ruiz feels the full force of Poland's Damian Knyba during Friday's fight in New Jersey

Ruiz famously defeated the then undefeated Anthony Joshua back in June 2019

Joshua exacted revenge six months later and Ruiz has gone on to have just four more fights since due to injury problems, beating Chris Arreola and Luis Ortiz before drawing with Miller and now suffering his third loss.

Ruiz said after Friday's defeat in New Jersey: 'It was just a long layoff, and it was a great opponent.

'I didn't want to take an easy fight, so that's why I took Damian. He's a big guy. But we've got to take risks. I've still got it in me, man. I've just got to stay active and I want to fight again.

'Every time I tried to come in, he'd hold me really tight, and I just couldn't let my combinations go.

'He played a good game plan, but I'd love to run it back and do things a lot different.'

The judges scored the fight 117-110, 114-113 and 114-113 in Knyba's favour.

It wasn't the night Hearn was hoping for after signing Ruiz this summer but much of his current focus is on trying to finalise Joshua's highly anticipated fight against British rival Tyson Fury.

The bout has been proposed to take place in November after years of negotiations but the location of the fight appears to be a major sticking point.

Hearn and Joshua are said to want the fight to take place at Wembley Stadium in London while the Fury camp are reportedly leaning towards Madison Square Garden in New York City.
