NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday paid tribute to the victims of 9/11 terror attacks in the United States on its 25th anniversary.Calling India as a "victim of cross-border terrorism", PM Modi said that the New Delhi will continue to fight terrorism in all its forms and manifestation."25 years on from the horrific 9/11 attacks, we remember and honour the victims and stand in solidarity with the families whose lives were forever changed. Terrorism has claimed countless lives around the world. As a victim of cross-border terrorism, India has been at the forefront of this fight for several decades," PM Modi said in a social media post."While the threat keeps evolving, our resolve and opposition to terrorism in all its forms and manifestations remain unwavering. We stand in solidarity with all efforts to combat this scourge," he addedHe also shared images from his visit to the 9/11 Memorial & Museum in 2014.On September 11, 2001, 19 al-Qaida terrorists hijacked four commercial passenger aircraft in a coordinated attack against the United States. Two planes crashed into the World Trade Centre's Twin Towers in New York, while a third struck the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia. The fourth aircraft crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers and crew attempted to regain control.The attacks killed 2,977 people, according to official US figures. The tragedy triggered sweeping changes in US counterterrorism policy, military operations and domestic security measures.At Ground Zero in New York, annual remembrance ceremonies continue to honour the victims, with their names read aloud by family members and loved ones. The attacks were orchestrated by al-Qaida leader Osama bin Laden.

World.title: Indonesia seeks to repatriate five baby orangutans found in Odisha; trafficking network suspected
World.content:
File photo: Five baby orangutans were discovered in a Balasore forest, baffling wildlife officials

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Indonesia is working to bring back five baby orangutans found in a forest in Odisha, as authorities investigate a suspected international wildlife trafficking network that may have brought the animals thousands of kilometres from their natural habitat.The five orangutans were found by forest department officials patrolling the Jaleswar range in Balasore district on September 8. They are believed to be between one and 1.5 years old and have since been moved to Nandankanan Zoological Park in Bhubaneswar, where they are being kept in quarantine.Indonesiaâs ministry of forestry said preliminary observations suggested the animals could be Sumatran orangutans, but stressed that their species and genetic origins would be confirmed through DNA testing.âBased on preliminary observations of their physical characteristics, the five animals are suspected to be Sumatran orangutans,â the ministryâs head of public relations and foreign cooperation, Ristianto Pribadi, said in statement quoted by Antara news agency.The ministry said it was coordinating with Indian authorities, including Indiaâs CITES Management Authority, as well as diplomatic missions in Jakarta and New Delhi, Indonesiaâs National Research and Innovation Agency and its agriculture ministry to expedite the animalsâ return.The presence of the orangutans in India has raised suspicions of transnational wildlife trafficking because the apes are native only to the islands of Sumatra and Borneo. Odishaâs environment minister Ram Singh Khuntia had earlier said investigators suspected an international racket could be involved.International commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited under CITES, the global agreement regulating trade in endangered wildlife.Indonesian conservation groups including the Leuser Ecosystem Foundation, Indonesian Wildlife Network, Center for Orangutan Protection and Indonesian Orangutan Forum have also offered to assist with the repatriation.Once returned to Indonesia, the orangutans are expected to undergo health checks, quarantine and behavioural assessments. If they are found fit, they could enter a rehabilitation programme aimed at eventually returning them to the wild.The case comes as orangutan populations face mounting pressure from habitat loss and other threats. The World Wildlife Fund estimates that about 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago.A third species, the Tapanuli orangutan, is classified as critically endangered, with fewer than 800 believed to survive in the wild. Its entire known population lives in the Batang Toru forest in North Sumatra, an ecosystem threatened by mining, palm oil plantations and a large hydropower project.The discovery of the five infants has now prompted authorities in India and Indonesia to investigate how the animals entered India and whether they were victims of a wider international trafficking operation.

World.title: Suvendu Adhikari eats fish bhog at Kalighat amid Bageshwar Baba row: What sparked the controversy
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday visited Kolkata's Kalighat Temple and partook of the traditional fish and pulao bhog, days after Dhirendra Krishna Shastri triggered a row by asking Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food during

.

The visit came as the controversy over Shastriâs remarks continued to grow, with leaders across parties, including the BJP, pushing back against alleged attempts to dictate Bengalâs food habits.

Speaking to reporters after offering prayers, Adhikari described Kaushiki Amavasya as a significant occasion in Sanatan culture and said that the festival was being observed with devotion at major temples across the state, including Kalighat and Tarapith.

"Today is Kaushiki Amavasya. Today is a very big day in our Sanatan culture, a major worship (Mahapuja). Whether it is Kalighat here or Tarapith there, it is happening simultaneously," Adhikari said.

"State-level worship is being held in Tarapith. Here in Kalighat, all our lighting has been set up; it is an atmosphere of celebration throughout," he added.

Adhikari said Kolkata holds a special spiritual significance, recalling its association with Maa Kali, Maa Durga, Ramakrishna Paramahansa, Maa Sarada Devi, Swami Vivekananda and Lord Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.





"This is a spiritual land. It is the land of Ma Kali, the land of Ma Durga, the land of Thakur Ramakrishna Dev, the land of Ma Sarada Devi, the land of Swami Vivekananda, and the land of Lord Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu," he said.

BJP Bengal also posted Adhikari's photo and said, "On the sacred occasion of Kaushiki Amavasya, chief minister Shri Suvendu Adhikari offered prayers to Maa Kali at Kalighat and, following the templeâs traditional customs, partook of the sacred bhog of pulao and fish."

This comes days after Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, during his visit to West Bengal for a three-day Hanumant Katha in Howrah's Liluah, appealed to Bengali Hindus to observe Navratri with devotion and sincerity.

What is the controversy

During his visit to Bengal, Shastri had appealed to Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food during the Durga Puja festivities and described those who eat meat on religious occasions as âhypocritesâ.

Fish and meat are closely associated with traditional cuisine in West Bengal, while religious practices vary across communities and regions.

Shastri's remarks also led to a rare display of unity between Congress and BJP as both parties rejected the godman's advice, saying personal views should not dictate what Bengali society should eat.

On Tuesday, Congress lodged a police complaint against Shastri, asserting that the call was âintended to create disharmonyâ.

In the complaint submitted to the officer-in-charge of Kolkataâs Bhawanipore police station, the South Kolkata District Congress Committee alleged that Shastri made âderogatoryâ comments during an event in Howrah on September 5.

âWe want to apprise you that immediate administrative action needs to be initiated, and an FIR needs to be registered with necessary arrests. His remarks could spark disharmony in society and were against the democratic spirit,â Congress leader Pradip Prasad said in the complaint, according to PTI.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Meanwhile, BJP West Bengal chief Samik Bhattacharya said that Bengalis would âcontinue to eat what they have been eatingâ.

âWe generally eat âluchiâ on Ashtami and goat meat on Navami. We will continue to do that. Nobody can tell the people of West Bengal what they should eat,â Bhattacharya said.

âLet me live the way I want to. Bengalis will eat what they have been eating. Can Bengalis not eat fish and meat?â he asked, quoting Swami Vivekananda.

World.title: Putin, Xi and a bigger Brics: India becomes the stage for high-stakes global diplomacy test
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi has been turned into a fortress. Roads are being secured, security has been stepped up and the capital is preparing for the arrival of some of the worldâs most powerful leaders.

Russian President Vladimir

, Chinese President

and other leaders are set to gather for the

Summit, turning New Delhi into the stage for a meeting of a bloc that now represents nearly half of the worldâs population.

But beyond the motorcades, bilateral meetings and summit optics lies a much bigger test. With 49.5% of the worldâs population, Brics is no longer simply a grouping of emerging economies. As India hosts the 18th Brics Summit on September 12-13, New Delhi now has to show what it can do with that growing weight.

India has spent its 2026 chairship pushing the grouping towards more practical cooperation: from food and energy security to critical supply chains, artificial intelligence and development finance. The challenge now is whether those efforts can translate into meaningful outcomes at a time when wars, tariff battles, supply-chain disruptions and geopolitical rivalries are reshaping the global economy.

A bigger Brics, a bigger global footprint

Brics began with Brazil, Russia, India and China, with South Africa joining in 2011.





The grouping expanded significantly in 2024 with the addition of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. Indonesia joined in 2025, taking the number of full members to 11.

The bloc also has 10 partner countries: Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.

The expansion has dramatically widened Bricsâ geographical reach across Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America.

It brings together major energy producers, manufacturing powers, large consumer markets, commodity exporters and rapidly developing economies.

Diversity is both an asset and a challenge. Brics has emerged as an important platform for major emerging economies to coordinate positions on global governance, development, trade, finance and technology. Its members also use the grouping to press for greater representation of developing countries in institutions such as the IMF, World Bank and UN.

Yet the same diversity makes consensus more difficult. Unlike a formal economic union, Brics has neither a single economic policy nor a common foreign policy. Its members have different political systems, economic structures and strategic interests, and in some cases, sharply divergent positions on major international issues.

The West Asia crisis is a particularly difficult test. Iran and the UAE are both members of Brics but have differing positions on the conflict.

Saudi Arabia is also part of the grouping, adding another layer of complexity to attempts to craft a common political response.

With Brics functioning on the principle of consensus, India faces the delicate task of finding language that can accommodate competing national positions while still producing a meaningful summit declaration.

What isâ BRICSâ

Indiaâs four priorities

Resilience

The resilience pillar focuses on strengthening the ability of BRICS economies to withstand disruptions in the global economy.

The agenda includes health, agriculture, food security, energy security, disaster risk reduction and critical supply chains.

The focus reflects lessons from the pandemic, geopolitical conflicts and disruptions to global trade and logistics. For emerging economies, disruptions in energy supplies, food markets, shipping routes or access to essential industrial inputs can quickly translate into inflation, shortages and slower growth.

India has therefore sought greater cooperation among BRICS countries to build more resilient and diversified supply chains, alongside stronger trade, investment and connectivity.

Innovation

The second pillar focuses on innovation and emerging technologies. India has highlighted digital public infrastructure, fintech, artificial intelligence and knowledge-sharing as tools that can help Brics economies improve public services and create new opportunities for growth.

For New Delhi, the emphasis is not simply on technological advancement but on using technology for inclusive development.

India is seeking to showcase its experience with digital public infrastructure while encouraging cooperation in areas where emerging technologies can support health, agriculture, financial inclusion, disaster management and public service delivery.

The larger objective is to make Brics cooperation more relevant to citizens rather than confining it to government-to-government discussions.

Cooperation

The third pillar seeks to deepen practical cooperation through policy coordination, development finance, trade facilitation, investment, connectivity and reform of global institutions.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar has said Brics must move from being a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery.

That approach is reflected in the range of meetings held during Indiaâs chairship, including ministerial engagements and discussions involving business, technology and other stakeholders.

India has also sought to strengthen people-to-people exchanges and broaden participation beyond political leaders and government officials.

Sustainability

The fourth pillar is sustainability, with a focus on climate action, green finance, energy transition and sustainable development. For Brics economies, the challenge is particularly complex: many are simultaneously dealing with rising energy demand, development needs and pressure to reduce emissions.

India has therefore placed emphasis on finding practical pathways that balance economic growth with climate objectives, while recognising the different development levels and energy requirements of member countries.

India will host the BRICS summit here on September 12-13, 2026.

Brics and Indiaâs Global South pitch

At its core, Brics has evolved into a platform for emerging economies seeking a greater say in the institutions that shape the global economic and political order. Its members argue that the distribution of influence in institutions such as the IMF and World Bank does not adequately reflect the economic weight of developing countries today.

India has consistently backed reforms to global governance institutions, including greater representation for developing countries. But New Delhiâs approach is not one of replacing the existing global economic system with a new bloc-based order.

India continues to maintain deep economic, technological and strategic relationships with Western economies while participating in groupings such as the Quad and G20.

For New Delhi, Brics is therefore a tool of strategic autonomy and multi-alignment a platform through which India can work with China, Russia, Gulf countries, Africa and Latin America while simultaneously expanding its engagement with the US, Europe and other partners.

It also strengthens Indiaâs credentials as a leading voice of the Global South.

The economic story

The economic weight of Brics is perhaps its most obvious strength.

According to figures cited by the Indian government, the 11-member grouping accounts for around 49.5% of the worldâs population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade.

Indiaâs total goods trade with Brics members more than doubled from $203.1 billion in FY21 to $417.5 billion in FY26, according to data cited by the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).

But the numbers also expose a major challenge for New Delhi: the rapid growth of imports has far outpaced exports.

Indiaâs exports to Brics increased 48.8%, from $64.3 billion in FY21 to $95.7 billion in FY26. Imports, meanwhile, jumped 131.8%, from $138.8 billion to $321.8 billion.

As a result, Indiaâs trade deficit with Brics more than tripled, rising from $74.5 billion to $226.1 billion. The BRICS share in Indiaâs exports fell marginally from 22% to 21.7%, while its share in Indiaâs imports rose sharply from 35.2% to 41.5%.

UAE is Indiaâs biggest Brics export market

Within the expanded grouping, the UAE emerged as Indiaâs largest export market in FY26. India exported goods worth $37.4 billion to the UAE, up 124% from FY21.

China was the second-largest destination at $19.5 billion, followed by Saudi Arabia at $10.3 billion. Brazil and South Africa accounted for around $7 billion each, while exports to Russia and Indonesia stood at around $4.5 billion each.

Indiaâs exports declined to Indonesia, Iran and Ethiopia.

On the import side, however, China remained Indiaâs largest Brics supplier. Indian imports from China doubled from $65.2 billion to $131.6 billion, accounting for about 41% of Indiaâs Brics imports.

The UAE supplied goods worth $63.9 billion, while imports from Russia increased more than tenfold, from $5.5 billion to $55.4 billion, primarily because of higher energy purchases.

China, the UAE and Russia together accounted for almost 84% of Indiaâs imports from Brics.

For India, the challenge is therefore not simply to increase trade with Brics but to make that trade more balanced.

GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava said the priority should be to correct the growing imbalance. âBrics is becoming an increasingly important source of machinery, industrial inputs, energy and commodities. However, it is not absorbing a comparable share of Indian exports,â said.

âIndia should seek better market access in China, Russia and Indonesia, address non-tariff barriers, promote higher-value exports and reduce excessive dependence on a few Brics suppliers.

Without stronger export growth, deeper intra-BRICS trade could further widen India's already large trade deficit,â he added.

The broader Brics trade numbers tell another story. GTRI estimates that Brics countries exported around $1.1 trillion worth of goods to one another, equivalent to 18.8% of their combined global exports.

Their imports from fellow Brics countries stood at around $1.4 trillion, representing 29.5% of their global imports.

This means BRICS economies remain more important to one another as sources of imports than as export destinations.

China is the dominant player. In 2025, Brics countries exported goods worth around $5.67 trillion, accounting for 21.6% of global exports. Their imports totalled approximately $4.58 trillion, or 17.3% of global imports.

China alone exported $550.8 billion to other Brics members and imported $464.9 billion from them.

Chinaâs manufacturing scale, export capacity and role in global supply chains make it the economic anchor of Brics. For commodity-producing members, China provides a major market. For countries such as India and Brazil, the bloc provides opportunities for diversification and greater collective bargaining power.

But it also means Brics integration cannot be understood simply as a partnership among equals.

For the grouping to become a genuinely integrated economic force, the next stage would require deeper business-to-business connections, greater investment flows and stronger institutional links.

The Trump factor

Indiaâs Brics presidency has another powerful observer: US President Donald Trump.

As Brics leaders gather in New Delhi against the backdrop of the Iran war, disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, trade tensions and a rapidly shifting global economy, Washington will be watching closely. Each of these issues intersects with US interests, from energy prices and shipping routes to tariffs, the dollar and the changing balance of global power.

Trump has repeatedly targeted Brics over its efforts to reduce dependence on the US dollar, portraying the grouping as a challenge to American economic dominance.

âYou have this little group called Brics. It's fading out fast, but BRICS is, they wanted to try and take over the dollar, the dominance of the dollar, and the standard of the dollar,â Trump told reporters at the White House last year in July.

He also warned: âAny Country aligning themselves with the Anti-American policies of Brics, will be charged an ADDITIONAL 10% Tariff. There will be no exceptions to this policy. Thank you for your attention to this matter!â

In October 2025, Trump described Bricsâ de-dollarisation efforts as an âattack on the dollarâ and again threatened tariffs against countries joining the grouping.

âI told anybody who wants to be in Brics, that's fine, but we're going to put tariffs on your nation,â he said in the Oval Office.

The Troika: India, Russia and China

The geopolitical backdrop has made the Brics summit even more consequential. At the recent Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin, Prime Minister Narendra

Modi

, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin projected an unusually warm display of strategic camaraderie.

PM Modi described Russia as a âspecial and privileged partnerâ, while Xi said âthe worldâs two most populous countries need to be friends.â Putin, meanwhile, referred to Modi as his âdear friendâ and travelled with him in his armoured Aurus limousine.

The optics came at a particularly sensitive moment for Washington. The Trump administration has sought to prevent Russia and China from developing an even closer strategic partnership.

Trump himself has said: âThe one thing you never want to happen isâ¦ Russia and China uniting. Iâm going to have to un-unite them, and I think I can do that.â

The logic echoes the strategy of former US president Richard Nixon, whose 1972 opening to China exploited the Sino-Soviet split and transformed the Cold War balance.

The emerging picture today, however, is markedly different. Rather than driving Russia away from China, Washingtonâs efforts have coincided with Moscow maintaining close ties with Beijing while simultaneously deepening its relationship with New Delhi.

Italian analyst Francesco Sisci described the dynamic as a âReverse Nixonâ.

âThe Nixon paradigm did work in reverse, but differently from what the US had thought; that is, Moscow played Washington this time,â he added.

The significance goes beyond symbolism. Russia has emerged as an important supplier of energy and defence equipment to India, while China remains Indiaâs largest trading partner and a major economic power within Brics.

The global guest list for Brics Summit.

Xiâs India visit adds another layer

Chinese President Xi Jinping will also visit India for the Brics summit, marking his first visit to the country in seven years. His participation is significant not only for Brics but also for the gradual improvement in India-China ties following the 2020 eastern Ladakh military standoff.

PM Modi and Xi have held several meetings since their 2024 interaction on the sidelines of the Brics summit in Kazan, which marked a further easing of tensions and the resolution of issues related to disengagement.

The two sides have also resumed high-level engagement on the boundary question.

For India, the Brics summit provides an opportunity to push for fair market access, reliable supply chains and greater balance in bilateral trade, while maintaining its position that peace and tranquillity along the border are essential for the broader development of ties.

For China, the summit is equally important because Beijing will take over the Brics chairship after India.

Iran, UAE and the test of consensus

If the economic agenda tests Bricsâ ability to deliver, the Middle East crisis is testing its ability to reach consensus. Iran is a full member of Brics. So are the UAE and Saudi Arabia, countries with their own strategic interests in the region.

India is seeking language that emphasises the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection.

The Strait of Hormuz adds particular urgency because any prolonged disruption could affect global energy markets, shipping costs and inflation.

The challenge is to ensure that disagreements over the conflict do not derail the broader economic agenda. If consensus on political language proves difficult, New Delhi may seek to insulate economic agreements from contentious geopolitical issues by acknowledging individual national positions.

The India challenge: Making a bigger Brics work

The rapid expansion of Brics has increased its global influence but also raised questions about governability.

Prof Srikanth Kondapalli of Jawaharlal Nehru University has described the transformation as significant, pointing to the growing geographical spread and increasing number of countries seeking closer association with the grouping.

He believes India is attempting to make Brics cooperation more decentralised and practical by taking the agenda beyond leaders and ministers to businesses, startups and civil society.

âThis is a new format that India is trying to pursue a decentralisation process compared to many centralised initiatives,â Kondapalli told ANI.

He pointed to cooperation in areas including agriculture, startups, climate finance and artificial intelligence, arguing that these could help developing economies cope with international shocks.

At the same time, he warned that further expansion could make consensus-building more difficult.

âThere is no organisation which is intercontinental other than the United Nations. Brics has over these two decades established itself as an intercontinental organisation,â he said.

The challenge for India is therefore to ensure that a larger Brics does not become a less effective Brics.

What India wants from the summit

Indiaâs priorities for the summit extend beyond the headline political issues. Among the areas expected to receive attention are trade, investment, development finance, resilient supply chains, cross-border payments, startups, technology, sustainability and global governance reform.

India also wants continued support for issues such as UN Security Council reform and counter-terrorism cooperation.

The proposed outcomes are aimed at giving the chairship a practical legacy. The summit is expected to culminate in the release of the New Delhi Declaration, although reaching consensus on the document remains one of the key diplomatic challenges.

According to the ministry of external affairs schedule, the summit will begin on Saturday afternoon with a closed-door session for Brics member countries on âInclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism.â

The leaders will subsequently visit the Bharat Innovates Exhibition, followed by a family photograph and joint tree-planting ceremony. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the leaders on Saturday evening.

On Sunday, the leaders will attend the open session titled âResilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.â The summit will conclude with the release of the New Delhi Declaration.

On Sunday, the leaders will attend the open session titled âResilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability."

Indiaâs multi-alignment in sharper focus

For India, the message is less about choosing and more about preserving strategic room to manoeuvre. Recent diplomatic activity has underscored that approach. PM Modi met Xi in China and held talks with Putin, while also maintaining engagement with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The Russia relationship remains particularly important because of energy. According to Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, Indiaâs energy imports from Russia have reached record levels.

âI donât want to give you any figures for understandable reasons, but every month we have a new record,â he said.

Peskov also said Russia remained committed to fulfilling its defence commitments to India, including deliveries of the S-400 Triumf air defence systems.

âRussia is capable of fulfilling its obligations, and they will be fulfilled. This issue is being mentioned during the conversations of our two leaders,â Peskov added.

Moscow is also exploring deeper cooperation with India in areas including rare earths and the potential sale of Su-57 fighter jets, according to Peskov.

On Ukraine, he suggested that Moscow sees considerable convergence with New Delhi. âWe know Indiaâs position on the Ukrainian conflict, and to a great extent... it corresponds with our own position, because we do want the resolution of the Ukrainian conflict by peaceful means, and Russia is open to this process,â Peskov said.

The tariff factor

The relationship with Washington, meanwhile, has become more complicated. Trumpâs tariff policy has added an economic dimension to what was already a difficult geopolitical balancing act.

For India, the concern is that pressure over trade could spill into wider strategic ties. At the same time, Indiaâs growing closeness to Moscow and renewed engagement with Beijing do not necessarily signal a break with Washington.

As Sreeram Sundar Chaulia of the Jindal School of International Affairs put it, India could still seek to maintain both relationships, âthe Russian cake and eating the American pieâ, but trust with Washington would be crucial.

Russia has rejected the suggestion that Brics is pursuing formal de-dollarisation. Peskov said the grouping was not considering such a move, while criticising the use of national currencies as instruments of political pressure and calling proposed US sanctions illegal and unacceptable.

Indiaâs position is broadly consistent with this distinction: greater financial diversification is not the same as replacing the dollar.

Why Brics matters to India

Despite its political differences and economic imbalances, Brics remains strategically important to India.

The grouping gives New Delhi a platform to work with China, Russia, Gulf countries, Africa and Latin America while continuing its engagement with the US, Europe, the Quad and other Western partners.

It also strengthens Indiaâs claim to a leadership role in the Global South. Working alongside major emerging economies, India can push for reforms of institutions such as the UN Security Council, IMF and World Bank, whose structures are widely seen as insufficiently representative of the developing world.

Support within Brics for reform of the UN system is significant, although it falls short of an explicit endorsement of Indiaâs bid for permanent membership of the Security Council, an issue complicated by Chinaâs position.

The China factor remains central. Stepping away from Brics would risk leaving greater space for Beijing to shape the economic and political agenda of the developing world. Indiaâs presence allows it to push for a more balanced approach and resist any attempt to turn Brics into an explicitly anti-Western platform.

Despite its political differences and economic imbalances, Brics remains strategically important to India.

Building alternatives without targeting dollar

Financial cooperation is another important pillar. Institutions such as the New Development Bank (NDB) and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) demonstrate Bricsâ ability to build mechanisms of its own.

India supports greater use of local currencies for legitimate trade and settlement, but has opposed the idea of a common Brics currency or a China-dominated alternative to the existing financial system.

The economic case is equally important. Brics provides India with access to large markets while creating opportunities for trade diversification, supply-chain resilience and de-risking.

Its membership also deepens Indiaâs economic ties with major energy suppliers such as Russia, agricultural and commodity producers such as Brazil, and Gulf and African economies.

From dialogue to delivery

Jaishankar, while announcing Indiaâs Brics summit, said the grouping must now move âfrom a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery.â

That objective is reflected in Indiaâs focus on concrete outcomes for the New Delhi summit, including a Brics declaration, a logistics and supply-chain cooperation framework, startup and incubator networks, development finance, cross-border payments, and continued support for priorities such as UN Security Council reform and counterterrorism.

India has some reason for confidence when it comes to navigating difficult multilateral negotiations.

At the 2023 G20 Summit in New Delhi, the inclusion of the African Union as a permanent member was a major diplomatic achievement. Equally significant was the last-minute consensus on Ukraine, where India helped broker compromise language that enabled leaders to adopt a joint declaration despite deep divisions over the war.

That experience could prove valuable as New Delhi prepares for another difficult summit involving an even more diverse set of political and economic interests.

Brics has travelled a long way from the acronym coined by Goldman Sachs to describe emerging economies with high growth potential.

A 20-year-old grouping at a turning point

Brics has travelled a long way from the acronym coined by Goldman Sachs to describe emerging economies with high growth potential.

UNCTAD estimates that Brics membersâ global merchandise exports rose from nearly $1 trillion in 2003 to around $6 trillion in 2024, while their share of global exports doubled from approximately 12% to 24%.

Yet economic size alone does not create an integrated bloc. The growth of intra-Brics trade has been substantial, but investment and deeper business links remain less developed than the blocâs headline economic numbers might suggest.

Brics has created political visibility, expanded South-South trade and established institutions such as the NDB. It has also strengthened calls for greater representation of emerging economies in global governance.

The next test is whether that weight can be converted into deeper cooperation and tangible results.

From a platform to a force

For India, the opportunity lies in using Brics to make the Global Southâs economic weight count more effectively without turning the grouping into an anti-Western alliance.

That requires navigating several contradictions at once. India must work with China without allowing Beijingâs economic dominance to dictate the agenda.

It must deepen ties with Russia while managing its increasingly important relationship with the US.

It must push for local-currency trade without turning the dollar debate into a confrontation. And it must build consensus among countries whose interests can diverge sharply, particularly on issues such as West Asia.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The economic challenge is equally clear. India needs Brics markets, but it also needs to ensure that greater integration does not deepen its trade deficit.

It needs access to Chinese and other Brics markets while reducing excessive dependence on a handful of suppliers.

At a time of wars, tariff battles, supply-chain disruptions and a rapidly changing global order, this is perhaps the biggest test yet for a bloc that began as an economic acronym and has grown into an important geopolitical platform. Brics has grown bigger. Indiaâs task is to make it more effective.

World.title: 'Plotting a super-tainted majority': Congress taunts Centre over delay in Parliament prorogation
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Friday mounted its attack against the centre over the delay in prorogation of Parliament after it adjourned sine die, accusing the government of plotting a "super tainted two-third majority" to get the Delimitation Bill passed in Lok Sabha.

In a social media post on X, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days.

"So today the Modi govt has set a new record, bettering its own set in 2015. The gap between the adjournment of Parliament sine die and its prorogation has reached 29 days. The gap for the 2015 Monsoon Session was 28 days. The gap for the 2026 Monsoon Session is increasing by the day with no clear prospect for its early prorogation.

Normally the gap is just three-four days," Jairam Ramesh said.

"It is abundantly clear that the Union home minister was severely wounded by the stunning defeat he had inflicted on himself and his govt with his staggering arrogance in the Lok Sabha on April 17, 2026. He is now plotting a comeback to secure a super-tainted two-thirds majority to get the Constitution Amendment Bill passed in the Lok Sabha. He has already engineered a split in three parties that had voted against the Bill on April 17, 2026, and is using threats, intimidation and incentives to get others (who had also voted against the Bill) to change their stance.





The Union home minister does not have the numbers but his bravado, bluff and bluster will not let him read the writing on the wall," he added.

The Congress leader said that the government is keeping the suspense going, thinking that the opposition will get rattled.

"By not proroguing the Monsoon Session, the self-styled Chanakya may think he is playing mind games and indulging in psy-ops. But this is silly since the govt can convene a session any time it wants to for any purpose.

He is just keeping the suspense going, thinking that the opposition will get rattled. He can continue to hallucinate," Jairam Ramesh said.

"Why is the Modi govt refusing to convene an All-Party meeting to discuss its proposals for delimitation so as to build the broadest possible consensus - which is what the country needs? This has been the consistent demand of all opposition Parties since mid-March 2026. Why this secrecy and mystery on a subject that is of profound importance to the very fundamentals of the Indian Republic?" he questioned.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

This comes as Congress has been questioning the delay in proroguing Parliament's Monsoon session, saying "something fishy" was going on and the government was trying to conjure up a "super-tainted" two-thirds majority, but it would not succeed in achieving that.

During the Budget session on April 17, the Modi government faced a setback as the Constitution amendment bill, involving delimitation, for the implementation of the women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies was defeated in the Lower House.

Of the 528 MPs who voted, 298 voted in support, while 230 opposed it. The bill required 352 votes for a two-thirds majority.

World.title: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh chief minister

on Thursday paid floral tribute to the state's first chief minister and freedom fighter Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary, recalling his contributions to India's freedom struggle, governance and social reforms.

Speaking at an event held to mark the birth anniversary, Yogi Adityanath described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence.

"On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the revered people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to the memories of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant ji on the occasion of his auspicious birth anniversary, and offer my humble tributes," Yogi said.

Recalling Pant's contribution to the Kakori case, the chief minister said that in 1925, Pant had strongly defended revolutionaries facing a case filed by the British government following the Kakori Train Action.

He said Pant actively participated in the freedom movement and resigned as the Premier of Uttar Pradesh after being elected to the post in 1937, choosing instead to join the struggle against British rule.





"Whether it was the Quit India Movement or other major agitations from time to time for the freedom struggle, he actively took part in them," Yogi said.

The Chief Minister highlighted Pant's role after Independence, saying he became the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, when present-day Uttarakhand was also part of the state.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"As the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh... he initiated efforts to present the governance of such a large state as a model of good governance, foster its economic development, and work for the welfare of every section of society," he said.

Yogi also recalled Pant's contribution to land reforms and described the model introduced during his tenure as exemplary.

Later, as Union Home minister from 1954, Pant worked to address linguistic conflicts and played an important role in establishing Hindi as the official language, Yogi said.

"On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to his memory and offer my humble tributes to him," the chief minister said.

World.title: BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami interact with youth in Haldwani
World.content:
HALDWANI: BJP national president

and Uttarakhand chief minister

took part in a youth interaction programme in Haldwani, where they discussed careers, employment, entrepreneurship, skill development, technology, sports and the future of Uttarakhand with young participants.

During the interaction, participants raised questions related to the development of the state and the country. They also shared their experiences of various government schemes and offered suggestions on employment, self-employment and access to better opportunities in Uttarakhand.

Nabin cites central schemes, emerging opportunities

Nabin said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs leadership, the potential of Indiaâs youth was being given a new direction while new opportunities were being created for them.

He said initiatives such as Digital India, Startup India, Skill India, Make in India and Khelo India had provided young people with platforms to advance according to their talent, capabilities and skills. He added that young people were not merely seeking employment but were also emerging as creators of jobs and new opportunities.

He said the role of youth was increasing amid a rapidly changing economy and advances in technology.





According to him, new avenues had opened up in areas such as artificial intelligence, startups, innovation, digital technology and entrepreneurship. He said Uttarakhandâs young people had immense talent and potential and that connecting their energy and capabilities with the stateâs development could help take Uttarakhand to new heights.

He said that in a mountainous state such as Uttarakhand, it was important to expand opportunities in local employment, self-employment, tourism, skill development and entrepreneurship.

He added that the ideas, suggestions and aspirations of young people could play an important role in determining the future direction of the state. He called on the youth to turn future challenges into opportunities and actively contribute to building a developed India.

He also described social media as a powerful medium and said young people should use it positively for the development of society and the country.

He said all 1.4 billion citizens would need to work together to realise the vision of a developed India. He also urged young people to enter politics and public life and contribute to nation-building. He stressed the importance of time management, saying effective use of time was essential for success.

Dhami highlights recruitment, self-employment

Dhami described young people as the countryâs greatest strength and said Indiaâs large youth population was providing the nation with new energy, fresh ideas and capabilities.

He said the growing use of technology and innovation was also opening up new opportunities for young people.

The chief minister said that after assuming office on July 4, 2021, his government began working with the resolve that âthe youth and water of the mountains should both serve Uttarakhand.â He said recruitment to vacant posts in government departments was accelerated and that around 34,000 young people had so far been appointed to government services.

He also referred to action against irregularities in recruitment examinations, saying members of cheating rackets had been sent to jail and that a crackdown had been launched against those attempting to jeopardize the future of young people.

He said the government was not limiting opportunities to government jobs and was also focusing on self-employment, startups and entrepreneurship. He cited the Chief Ministerâs Self-Employment Scheme, skill development programmes, homestays and the Chief Ministerâs Udyaman Khiladi Scheme as initiatives through which young people were being provided opportunities.

Sports infrastructure, technology and investment

The chief minister said Uttarakhand was establishing a new identity in sports and that sports infrastructure was being expanded across the state. He referred to work towards setting up a Sports University in Haldwani and a womenâs Sports College in Lohaghat. He also cited Uttarakhand athletes winning more than 100 medals at the National Games, describing it as evidence of the stateâs growing sporting talent and changing sports environment.

He said opportunities were being created for young people in tourism, local products, science, innovation, artificial intelligence, robotics and other emerging technologies. He also referred to the Investors Summit, saying it had been organized with the objective of generating new investment and employment opportunities, while efforts were under way to expand industrial activity in the mountainous regions of the state.

The chief minister said the government was also providing free coaching facilities to young people preparing for competitive examinations to help ensure equal opportunities. He added that the talent, hard work and potential of Uttarakhandâs youth were among the stateâs greatest strengths in its effort to build a developed Uttarakhand.

World.title: Yoon acquitted in case related to South Korean marine's drowning in rare legal reprieve
World.content:
Former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol was acquitted on Friday (September 11, 2026) in a case related to a marine's drowning death in a rare reprieve in one of the criminal cases brought against him following his ouster for imposing martial law.

The independent counsel's indictment had alleged Yoon deliberately appointed former Defence Minister Lee Jong-Sup as his ambassador to Australia to help him leave the country and evade a criminal investigation into the death of Cpl. Chae Su-geun, who drowned during a search-and-rescue operation for flood victims in 2023.

But the Seoul Central District Court ruled it was unclear whether Yoon's appointment was intended to disrupt the investigation. Yoon said he appointed Mr. Lee as ambassador to promote military cooperation with Canberra, and his lawyers welcomed the court's verdict while calling on prosecutors not to appeal.

Yoon's former Justice Minister and Presidential Security Director were among other defendants also acquitted of charges that they colluded with Yoon to help Mr. Lee sidestep the investigation. Prosecutors didn't immediately say whether they would appeal Friday's (September 11) verdict.

A separate indictment alleges Yoon and other officials tried to cover up and manipulate the investigation into Chae's death, which sparked a public uproar after it emerged that military commanders had ordered soldiers to conduct search operations without life vests and other safety equipment.

An early investigation by the marine corps held a division commander and seven other people responsible for Chae's death. But Yoon expressed fury over the commander's inclusion, prompting senior presidential and Defence Ministry officials to pressure the marine corps to revise the report to exclude the commander, according to prosecutors.

Prosecutors said the then-head of the marines' investigation team, Park Jung-hun, defied the pressure and sent the report to police and that Yoon subsequently ordered officials to retrieve the report from police and dismiss Mr. Park, who was investigated for insubordination.

Yoon was formally removed from office in April 2025 and has faced multiple criminal trials after President Lee Jae Myung approved special investigations into his martial law imposition and several other matters, including Chae's death.

He has appealed the conviction and life sentence for rebellion, which was the most serious charge stemming from his brief imposition of martial law in December 2024. Yoon's martial law decree lasted only hours, after a quorum of lawmakers managed to break through a blockade of heavily armed soldiers and voted to revoke the measure, forcing his Cabinet to lift it.

World.title: 'Talaq-E-Hassan' valid form of divorce, to be registered under new Act: Gauhati HC
World.content:
The Gauhati High Court has held that 'Talaq-E-Hassan' is a valid form of divorce not prohibited in the country, directing a petitioner to approach the Barpeta jurisdictional Marriage and Divorce Registrar for registration of his divorce under the Assam Compulsory Registration of Muslim Marriages and Divorce Act, 2024.

Justice Arun Dev Choudhury had passed the order on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) in a writ petition concerning registration of a divorce pronounced through Talaq-E-Hassan.

According to the petitioner, he got married in 2016, and following differences, his wife allegedly left the matrimonial home in 2018 while attempts at reconciliation did not succeed.

He subsequently pronounced Talaq-E-Hassan on three separate dates — March 22, April 26 and May 27, 2026. He then approached the concerned authority for registration of the divorce under the applicable law.

The petitioner argued that Talaq-E-Hassan was not prohibited and that the divorce had been pronounced according to its requirements.

The State, however, submitted that the earlier 1935 legislation had been repealed and the authority appointed under that law could no longer register the divorce.

Justice Choudhury observed that the Talaq-E-Hassan as pronounced by the petitioner is a valid form of Talaq and is not prohibited in the country as of today.

He, however, declined to direct the earlier Barpeta authority to register the Talaqnama because the 1935 law had been repealed and the post created under it had been abolished.

He directed the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional Marriage and Divorce Registrar under the 2024 Act.

The Registrar must examine whether the divorce was effected by the petitioner and verify his identity before deciding whether registration is required under Section 12 of the Act.

If registration is refused, the petitioner may pursue the remedy of appeal under Section 17 of the 2024 Act.

The Judge also observed that the wife, who was not present in court despite notices being served, remained free to challenge the Talaq-E-Hassan before an appropriate forum.

The court disposed of the writ petition.

World.title: Telangana Govt resolves to establish unified governance for CURE
World.content:
Telangana Government has resolved to establish a unified governance structure for the Core Urban Region Economy (CURE) region enabling constitution of multiple municipal corporations within it.

The Telangana Core Urban Region (Integrated Governance) Bill, 2026, passed in the State Assembly on Friday (September 11, 2026) is in this direction. The bill envisages to combine metropolitan level coordination with decentralised administration ensuring that governance is effective responsive and citizen centric.

Salient features of Bill

Accordingly, a CURE Apex Governing Council would be established for setting the vision and strategic priorities for the region besides ensuring coordination among corporations, urban authorities and departments discharging functions in CURE. One of the main features of the CURE would be shifting from an outdated model of taxation based on annual rental value system to the capital value system which would balance citizen interests with consideration of fiscal health of the local government. Simplification and consolidation of the licensing regime, introducing the concept of night economy, ensuring urban labour welfare and supporting economic participation of women and transgender persons would be among other salient features of the Bill.

The Bill, the government said, was necessitated as the GHMC Act contained upward of one hundred obsolete or redundant provisions. It had not kept pace with the increased geographical limits of the corporation area and did not provide a framework which was critical for effective coordination and citizen centric governance of an ever changing urban region.

“This has led to structural inconsistencies and gaps in areas of urban governance and service delivery. It is therefore considered necessary and expedient to repeal the GHMC Act and enact a new modern and comprehensive law for CURE,” as per the Bill. The core objectives of the new Bill would be integrated governance and seamless administration through mechanisms and channels for coordination among State Government, corporations and other urban authorities for effective discharge of urban governance functions. The government intended to develop CURE as economic driver of the State through provisions that promote ease of doing business and support economic growth. Improving fiscal health of the corporations to empower them to effectively discharge their functions and ensuring accessible and effective grievance redressal mechanisms constitute other major objectives of the new Bill.

Integrated, effective and citizen centric governance would require a context specific institutional framework that would enable coordination across authorities, clear accountability, meaningful citizen participation and quality of life, according to the Bill.

World.title: Bank strike hits branch operations in Hyderabad on September 11; operations expected to resume on September 15
World.content:
Customer facing branch banking services were impacted across Hyderabad on Friday (September 11, 2026) as thousands of employees and officers across public sector banks participated in the one-day nationwide strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU).

Most of the branches were shuttered while those that opened were manned by the incharge with illumination at the facility kept to the minimum even as customer footfalls were scarce. Ahead of the strike, the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) urged customers to make use of the digital channels.

Branch banking operations are expected to resume on Tuesday (September 15, 2026), with the strike followed by the weekend and the Ganesh Chaturthi holiday. Employees of some of the old generation private banks and regional rural banks were also part of the strike. Less than 5% of the staff in Telangana Grameena Bank were not part of the protest, a source in the RRB said. Private banks remained open.

The demands

As part of the strike, a large number of bank staff participated in a demonstration programme on Bank Street in Koti and raised slogans in support of their demand for implementation of the five-day week. The unions have been urging the government to implement what bank management and the workforce agreed several years ago — banks will remain closed on all Saturdays. At present, banks are closed, besides Sundays, on the second and fourth Saturdays. To compensate for the loss of working days, it has been agreed that branches will work for an additional 40 minutes every working day.

The strike on Friday (September 11, 2026) was also against implementation of a production linked incentive scheme. Earlier this week, the government said it has decided to keep in abeyance the implementation of the PLI scheme.

Citing reports from various States, All India Bank Employees Association (AIBEA) general secretary C.H. Venkatachalam said in a statement that the strike has been a total success with employees and officers enthusiastically joining the strike. Banking services were affected in a big way, including clearance of cheques.

Besides AIBEA, the UFBU consists of All India Bank Officers Confederation (AIBOC); National Confederation Of Bank Employees (NCBE); All India Bank Officers Association (AIBOA); Bank Employees Federation of India (BEFI); Indian National Bank Officers Congress (INBOC) and Indian National Bank Employees Federation (INBEF).

The National Organisation of Bank Workers (NOBW) and the National Organisation of Bank Officers (NOBO) previously used to be part of the UFBU.

Three-day bank strike proposed

The one-day strike is the beginning with UBFU planning a three-day bank strike from September 28-30 that will translate into no branch banking over five days from the preceding weekend (fourth Saturday and Sunday). It also plans to launch an indefinite strike from October 26, 2026.

World.title: Long incarceration, ailing mother prompt SC to grant interim bail to UAPA accused
World.content:
The Supreme Court has granted interim bail to a man held as an undertrial for nearly six years under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, allowing him to care for his ailing mother and hearing-impaired child.

A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and A.G. Masih, in a recent order, also took into consideration his prolonged period of incarceration while his trial remained pending. The period of bail is only for 10 days, from Friday (September 11, 2026) to September 21, after which he has to surrender.

Senior advocate Siddharth Dave and advocate Neha Rathi, for the petitioner, said their client had already been behind bars for 5 years and 11 months. So far, only 20 prosecution witnesses have been examined out of a total of 50. There was no likelihood of the trial concluding anytime in the near future, with a majority of witnesses yet to be examined.

The petitioner, who is accused of radicalising “gullible Muslim youth”, said there was no material to link him to any ‘terrorist act’ under the UAPA provisions. The appeal is part of a group of matters challenging a Karnataka High Court judgment of January 2026.

The National Investigation Agency vehemently opposed the grant of interim bail, submitting that the disability of the child was “long-standing”. It said the mother did not require any urgent medical treatment, and a brother, who was also said to need medical attention, was not living in the same household.

In its Wednesday (September 9, 2026) order, the top court, however, recorded that it was a fact that the child had to undergo bilateral cochlear implantation surgery. The petitioner’s brother too may undergo an eye surgery.

“In addition to that, we have taken note of the fact that the applicant/petitioner has been under incarceration for a period of five years and 11 months. Hence, in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are inclined to grant interim bail to the applicant/petitioner for a period of 10 days,” the court directed.

The legal issue of whether prolonged incarceration would dilute the stringency of bail provisions like Section 43D(5) has been a debated question of law.

In a 2021 judgment in the K.A. Najeeb case, the Supreme Court had held that constitutional courts can override statutory restrictions in anti-terror laws like UAPA to grant bail to accused persons who have already suffered prolonged incarceration with no sight of completion of their trial.

The Najeeb judgment, authored by Justice Surya Kant, had observed that constitutional courts cannot become mute spectators before the power of Section 43D(5). Courts had to necessarily intervene to protect the fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution. Prolonged incarceration and inordinate delay in trial were a violation of the right to speedy trial and access to justice which were both essential ingredients of the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution.

In May 2026, a Bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan, in a judgment in Syed Iftikhar Andrabi versus Union of India, confirmed the principle laid down in the 2021 Najeeb judgment while voicing “serious reservations” about a decision of another top court Bench to deny bail to former JNU student leader Umar Khalid and his co-accused Sharjeel Imam, charged under UAPA in the Delhi riots ‘larger conspiracy’ case.

The question whether delay in trial and resultant prolonged incarceration would necessarily lead to bail in UAPA cases has been referred to a larger Bench for an authoritative ruling.

World.title: Showers in Delhi: IMD issues red alert; wet spell to continue till September 13
World.content:
Heavy rain lashed parts of Delhi on Friday (September 11, 2026), accompanied by strong winds, with the weather office issuing a red alert until 5 p.m.

Clouds shrouded much of the national capital amid preparations for the BRICS Summit — to be held here on September 12 and 13 — with central and northern parts, including Parliament Street and Bharat Mandapam areas, receiving light to moderate rain.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an update shared at 1 p.m. that many areas are expected to receive light to moderate rain, with rainfall of up to 15 mm per hour, while heavy rain of more than 15 mm per hour is also likely in some areas in the next few hours.

In view of the forecast, the IMD's district-level nowcast has issued a red alert.

The rain comes after the national capital recorded above-normal maximum temperatures in recent days.

Meteorologists said the city could also experience light to moderate rain during the evening hours, with rainfall activity likely to continue over Delhi for the next two days.

World.title: CPI seeks TVK, VCK support for Thattanchavady bypoll in Puducherry
World.content:
The Communist Party of India (CP) has sought the support of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) for the Thattanchavady bypoll in Puducherry.

A delegation of CPI leaders led by the party’s Puducherry secretary A.M. Saleem on Thursday (September 10, 2026) met Tamil Nadu Minister for Water Resources and TVK general secretary N. Anand in Chennai to formally seek support for the October 6 bypoll. The delegation briefed the TVK leader on the CPI’s support base in the Thattanchavady constituency, Mr. Saleem said in a release.

The CPI delegation also called on VCK leader Thol. Thirumavalavan, seeking his party’s support for the bypoll in Puducherry.

World.title: BJP nominates Devasish Sharma for Assam’s Nagaon Lok Sabha byelection
World.content:
GUWAHATI

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has nominated former IAS officer Devasish Sharma as its candidate for the Nagaon Lok Sabha byelection on October 6, 2026.

Mr. Sharma had stoked controversy before opting for voluntary retirement as the Nagaon District Commissioner on September 3 and joining the BJP on Tuesday (September 8, 2026). The Nagaon parliamentary constituency covers Morigaon district and five of Nagaon district’s seven Assembly segments.

The Nagaon Lok Sabha seat fell vacant after Pradyut Bordoloi, who won in 2019 and 2024 as a Congress candidate, resigned ahead of the April 9, 2026, Assembly elections and joined the BJP. He now represents the BJP from the Dispur Assembly constituency.

On September 4, 2026, Congress leader and Dhubri MP Rakibul Hussain approached the Election Commission of India (ECI), seeking an inquiry into complaints of financial irregularities during his stint as the Nagaon District Commissioner.

Referring to his earlier complaints between August 28 and September 3, Mr. Hussain questioned Mr. Sharma’s alleged political neutrality and asked whether his role as Nagaon’s District Election Officer could be affected by joining a political party.

“If Devasish Sharma had already decided to contest as a BJP candidate, he should never have served as the (Nagaon) District Election Officer,” Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi said a few days ago, adding that the development was “nothing short of fraud”.

The BJP defended Mr. Sharma’s nomination, asserting that there was nothing wrong with a bureaucrat joining the party after the government okays his voluntary retirement. The government accepted his retirement request on September 3.

Guitar glamour

Mr. Sharma has been known to strum the guitar and belt out songs in public. As the Morigaon District Commissioner, he entertained polling teams that reached the strong room past midnight after the second phase of polling for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections ended.

According to his acquaintances, he was seen playing the guitar and singing frequently at public and private functions in Nagaon before opting for voluntary retirement.

The guitar-playing was reminiscent of another officer with the Nagaon connection who joined the BJP and became the party’s representative from the Buxar Assembly seat in Bihar.

Former IPS officer Anand Mishra served as the Nagaon Superintendent of Police until his transfer to Lakhimpur district in 2022. He resigned in January 2024 to eventually contest the 2025 Bihar Assembly election.

Mr. Mishra was active on social media, posting videos of his guitar sessions while serving as the police chief of Nagaon and Lakhimpur districts.

World.title: LHC suspends PMDC’s return orders for Afghan medical students
World.content:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday suspended the operation of the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council’s (PMDC) directives ordering Afghan medical students to return to the neighbouring country.

The decision came from Justice Khalid Ishaq, who was hearing a set of petitions filed by 13 Afghan students enrolled at different institutions in Lahore, including King Edward Medical University, Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences.

The pleas were filed after the PMDC issued a notification in September 1, directing Afghan medical students enrolled in Pakistani colleges “to return to Afghanistan”. The notification also barred medical and dental colleges from granting admission or placement to Afghan students for the current academic session.

In their pleas, the students referred to the Sept 1 notification, as well as a similar July 31 directive by the PMDC, and requested the LHC to declare them “illegal and unconstitutional”, without lawful authority and void from inception.

On Friday, Advocate Asad Jamal, who was representing the petitioners, contended that the students had been condemned unheard and their rights to education, life and dignity had been violated as the council had transgressed it’s jurisdiction under the PMDC Act.

He said the petitioners’ fundamental rights should be treated in accordance with law.

On the other hand, the council’s lawyer, Haris Azmat, argued against the suspension of the directives, saying that it was a matter of national security.

Justice Ishaq, however, rejected the argument and ordered that the operation of Sept 1 and July 31 directives by the PMDC should be suspended. He further directed that students be allowed to continue education, sit their examinations and return to hostels.

The judge also sought replies from the respondents, including the PMDC, the health ministry and the vice chancellors of the medical varsities and colleges in question, at the next hearing on September 18.

The pleas

The petitioners, comprising seven women and six men, filed the petitions through Advocate Jamal on Thursday. They said they had been removed from their colleges on the PMDC’s instructions, arguing that the council and the medical colleges lac­ked the legal authority to expel them.

They argued that the PMDC’s powers, as the top regulatory body under the PMDC Act 2023, must be exercised within the bounds of the Constitution and Pakistan’s international legal obligations.

They said neither the 2023 Act nor constitutional or international principles permitted the council to act arbitrarily, particularly against students who had already spent years pursuing their medical education in Lahore and other areas of Punjab.

Nilofar Nikzad, one of the petitioners, said she had completed two years of medical studies in Afghanistan before being forced to abandon her education because of Taliban restrictions on women’s access to education.

The petitioners said the sudden and disruptive process had led to their eviction from hostels by their respective colleges, leaving them without accommodation while their academic futures hung in the balance. They said the PMDC directives had caused significant distress among Afghan medical students studying across Pakistan, prompting them to seek recourse from the courts as a last resort.

The petitioners asked the LHC to declare two PMDC directives, issued on July 31 and Sept 1, “illegal and unconstitutional”.

Multiple petitioners who have approached the LHC hold scholarships under the Higher Education Commission (HEC)-sponsored Allama Iqbal Scholarship Programme.

In July 2025, the HEC held a reception to welcome around 350 Afghan students arriving in Pakistan to pursue their studies.

A health ministry official told Dawn earlier this week than an “in principle” decision had been made to send Afghan students enrolled in Pakistani medical universities back to their country, due to the ongoing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.

No decision by govt to return all Afghan students: FO

Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan on Thursday denied that the government had ordered all Afghan medical students to leave Pakistan, but stopped short of confirming whether those affected by the PMDC directive had valid visas and registrations.

“There is no such decision by the government to return all the Afghan students,” Khan told reporters at a weekly briefing in Islamabad. He said Afghan students could remain in Pakistan if they were enrolled in a valid degree programme and held valid visas.

“Of course, if a student is enrolled in Pakistan in a valid degree programme and holds a valid visa, he or she can stay here and complete their education,” Khan said.

However, when asked specifically about the status of students affected by the PMDC directive, the spokesman referred the matter to the medical regulator.

“Going back to your question, the PMDC has issued the letter. I would refer you to the PMDC,” he said, advising reporters to ask the council whether the students held valid registrations and visas.

“There is no blanket ban on Afghan students,” Khan said, reiterating that those holding valid visas and registered in recognised degree programmes would be allowed to complete their education in Pakistan.

Advocate Jamal earlier claimed in a post on X that there was “no distinction made between valid visa and invalid stay by PMDC in its directives”.

Meanwhile, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has condemned the PMDC decision, warning that the move could turn an education policy into a humanitarian crisis. It said around 100 Afghan medical and dental students in Lahore alone could be affected, including an estimated 20 to 40 women.

Deportation drive

Millions of Afghans have poured into Pakistan over the past several decades, fleeing successive wars, as well as hundreds of thousands who arrived after the return of the Tali­ban government in 2021.

A deportation drive first launched in 2023 was renewed in April last year when the government rescinded hun­dreds of thousands of residence permits for Afghans, warning them of arrests if they did not leave.

Last year alone, over a million Afghan nationals were deported by Pakistan, a Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and States and Frontier Regions (SAFRON) was informed.

Pakistan deported a total of 1,155,221 Afghan nationals in 2025, top officials of the Ministry of Interior and Chief Commissionerate for Afghan Refugees told the meeting.

The repatriated Afghans included 163,429 proof of registration card holders, 74,943 Afghan citizen card holders, 509,671 undocumented individuals and 407,178 voluntary returnees.

According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the repatriations appear to have picked up pace in the current year, with nearly 150,000 Afghans returning home from Pakistan and Iran by mid-February 2026. These returns added to the 5.4 million Afghans who have gone back to Afghanistan from the same two neighbouring countries since October 2023.

In June, the Ministry of Interior issued a directive to immediately arrest any Afghan national “found residing in Pakistan without a valid visa”.

World.title: KP advocate general questions maintainability of plea against PTI's Sept 27 protest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Advocate General Shah Faisal Utmankhel on Thursday questioned the maintainability of a petition filed in the Islamabad High Court (IHC) against the PTI’s planned protest in the federal capital on Sept 27.

The PTI has announced a nationwide protest on Sept 27 to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, has challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital. A larger bench, headed by IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar, is hearing the case.

Justice Muhammad Azam Khan and Justice Muhammad Asif are also a part of the bench.

During the hearing on Friday, KP Advocate General Utmankhel argued that an appropriate legal remedy was available to the petitioner before the Islamabad chief commissioner and that the extraordinary jurisdiction of the high court under Article 199 of the Constitution — under which a high court may take up a matter if it is satisfied that no other adequate remedy is provided by law — could not be invoked in the present circumstances.

He also pointed out that the petition was moved against a political party that had not been impleaded as a respondent. He questioned why the PTI had not been made a party to the petition if the proceedings concerned its planned protest, while CJ Dogar asked whether the PTI was actually planning to undertake the long march.

The chief justice further asked the advocate general if he agreed with statements made by KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi regarding the planned long march. The chief justice, however, did not specifically refer to any particular remarks by the KP CM.

Utmankhel replied that the office of the advocate general was not concerned with the chief minister’s political narrative but only with his official responsibilities.

On the court’s directive, he also read out the oath administered to the KP CM and argued that he had not violated his oath through any of his statements.

Referring to Article 5 of the Constitution, the chief justice asked whether the chief minister was constitutionally bound to remain loyal to the state.

“CM Afridi is very much loyal to the state,” AG Utmankhel replied.

He reiterated that political statements by the chief minister did not fall within the domain of the advocate general’s office, suggesting that the PTI and the chief minister should be impleaded as parties to the petition.

The KP chief secretary was then called to explain the provincial government’s position regarding the planned protest.

He adopted a stance similar to that of the advocate general, saying political statements were dealt with at the party level.

Responding to questions about any instructions having been issued by the chief minister to government officials in connection with the long march, the chief secretary assured the court that KP government officials would not be allowed to act beyond their constitutional limits.

CJ Dogar then recalled that the court had been told the planned march intended to strengthen the judiciary — seemingly a reference to the KP AG’s remarks from Thursday’s hearing — and pointed out that previously, the PTI had not complied with directions issued by the courts regarding its protest marches.

Justice Khan asked whether the chief minister could announce or support a long march and sit-in before formal approval had been granted for the protest.

At that, Utmankhel replied that such processions and marches were organised by political parties and citizens.

He referred to a statement by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, saying she was more concerned about developments in KP than in India. This was apparently a reference to Maryam’s statement from last week, when she said Punjab faced a greater security threat from “neighbouring provinces than from neighbouring countries”.

Utmankhel also cited a statement by Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, recalling that the PML-N had remarked that the court would rule against the long march.

At that, the chief justice wondered how Utmankhel had learnt of the statements aired on television when he had said during Thursday’s hearing that he did not watch television programmes.

The KP AG replied that, after the court had referred to statements reported by the media during the previous hearing, he watched television programmes throughout the night.

He further maintained that the PTI’s planned sit-in was aimed at promoting the rule of law, supremacy of the Constitution and strengthening of the judiciary.

To that, the chief justice replied: “We also want this, but you need not to come to Islamabad for this; it (protest) can be held in the provinces.”

But Utmankhel argued that Islamabad belonged to all the provinces and that the federal capital could “not be confined to its residents”. He said a peaceful long march should not be stopped.

He further questioned whether residents who joined the protest would also be expelled from the federal capital.
