Tamta Mikeladze: “The parliament’s work is therefore, on the one hand, directed against democratic institutions and rights, while on the other, it strengthens the executive branch’s discretionary powers and centralisation.

The theoretical frameworks of ‘autocratic legalism’ and ‘sham law’ are important for describing this process. In such a system, a law may formally meet the technical requirements of a legal act, but it loses its primary function: limiting state power and reducing arbitrariness. The law no longer acts as a mechanism for constraining power. Instead, it becomes a tool for maintaining and consolidating power.

In short, Georgia’s process of autocratisation, after years of oscillating between hybrid democracy and hybrid authoritarianism, is now aggressively and systematically affecting the legal sphere itself for the first time. It is fundamentally changing the law’s substance and nature.

We still have no adequate understanding of how difficult it will be to rehabilitate the state, political system, legal system and society after the crisis and the authoritarian period that Georgian Dream has inflicted on them.”

On legislation in Georgia

World.title: Georgian blogger says Interior Ministry wants to punish him for insulting Russian propagandists
World.content:
Civil rights activist and blogger Tornike Razmadze says Georgia’s Interior Ministry has summoned him to court to impose a fine or administrative detention because he insulted Kremlin propagandists Margarita Simonyan and Vladimir Solovyov in response to their insults against Georgian King Erekle II.

Georgia’s recently established Hate Speech Unit at the Interior Ministry has accused Razmadze of violating Article 166, Part 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences. The provision covers swearing in a public place and carries a fine of 500 to 3,000 lari ($185–1,110) or administrative detention for up to 20 days.

According to the activist, the case concerns a video he posted several weeks ago in which Russian propagandists discussed Erekle II, calling him a “king who crawled on his knees”. Margarita Simonyan, in particular, claimed that King Erekle had begged the Russians for help “on his knees” and that modern Georgians would likewise get down on their knees and ask Russia to take them under its protection.

Tornike Razmadze explains that this was why he used obscene language against Simonyan and Solovyov — more precisely, against their mothers.

According to the blogger, Simonyan and Solovyov effectively insulted the ruling Georgian Dream party as well. What angers him most is that, instead of taking offence at the Russian propagandists, the government wants to punish the person who insulted them. Razmadze sees this message from the authorities as the most important aspect of the whole case.

The activist also appealed to Georgia’s Public Defender (Ombudsman):

“I am not asking you for protection or support. I have one simple request: record your position on the case opened against me. I simply want to hear your position.”

However, the Interior Ministry’s Hate Speech Unit said the case had nothing to do with kings or propagandists. It said Tornike Razmadze was accused of insulting Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze.

“Insulting comments on social media by citizen Tornike Razmadze and Anna Bdeyan directed at Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze were identified. Administrative proceedings have been launched against them under Articles 166 and 173,” the Interior Ministry said.

The blogger’s lawyer, Mikheil Zakareishvili, in turn, says the Interior Ministry deliberately added Article 173, which concerns insulting a public official, to the charges. He says the original reports did not contain such wording. The lawyer is convinced that the case was opened specifically because of the insults directed at Simonyan and Solovyov.

The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA) considers the case against Razmadze another example of restrictions on freedom of expression. The association says prosecuting people over statements made on social media violates their fundamental constitutional rights and freedom of expression.

What is the Hate Speech Unit

The new Hate Speech Unit at Georgia’s Interior Ministry began operating on 1 June 2026. According to the ministry, its main task is to identify public statements that demean human dignity or are offensive and may constitute administrative offences.

Over the past three months, the unit has fined dozens of people. Vakhtang Sanaya, a journalist and presenter on Formula TV, became the first person to receive a two-week administrative detention sentence. Activist Giorgi Akhobadze also received a one-month detention sentence for a Facebook post.

Georgian blogger insults Simonyan

World.title: Russian Orthodox Church calls on pilgrims to ‘boycott’ New Athos Monastery in Abkhazia
World.content:
The Russian Orthodox Church (ROC) has called on pilgrims not to visit the New Athos Monastery in Abkhazia.

The ROC considers the monastery’s abbot, Father Dorotheus, a schismatic.

However, this did not stop Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy chief of staff of the Russian presidential administration and the Kremlin’s point man for Abkhazia, from visiting the monastery.

The Moscow Patriarchate’s chancellor, Metropolitan Grigory, has sent a circular letter to all bishops of the Russian Orthodox Church warning that Russian pilgrims must not attend services at the New Athos Monastery. The services there are led by defrocked hieromonk Dorotheus (Dbar).

“We are concerned about cases in which Orthodox pilgrims from dioceses of the Russian Orthodox Church visit the New Athos Monastery and take part in services held there. Pilgrims often go to confession and receive communion there without knowing that they should not.

I ask you to take measures to ensure that pilgrims travelling to holy sites in Abkhazia with your blessing are always informed that they must not engage in prayer or Eucharistic communion with the monk Dorotheus. They should also be informed that the sacraments performed in schism have no spiritual grace,” Metropolitan Grigory wrote.

Archimandrite Dorotheus

Archimandrite Dorotheus heads the Holy Metropolis of Abkhazia, one of two unrecognised Orthodox churches operating in the republic. A graduate of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki in Greece and a doctor of theology, he is highly popular in Abkhaz society and well known in church circles.

His “rival” is Father Vissarion, who heads the Abkhazian Orthodox Church (AOC). He is the only serving Abkhaz cleric ordained by the Georgian Orthodox Church during the Soviet era. Despite its unrecognised status, the AOC enjoys the active support of the Russian Orthodox Church.

The ROC, by contrast, has opposed Archimandrite Dorotheus and officially defrocked him in 2023 for refusing to submit to its authority.

The Holy Metropolis of Abkhazia and the AOC have been engaged in a long-running and bitter conflict.

Father Vissarion has also addressed not Russian but Abkhaz believers, saying they should not take part in services at New Athos.

Father Dorotheus himself believes that the Moscow Patriarchate’s letter was prompted by Archpriest Nikolai Balashov, an adviser to Patriarch Kirill of Moscow and All Russia. According to Dorotheus, Balashov has consistently worked in the interests of the Georgian Orthodox Church for decades.

“Similar circulars have appeared repeatedly. Yet their authors stubbornly refuse to acknowledge the main point: pilgrims who visit the New Athos Monastery are not there ‘out of ignorance’. The overwhelming majority of them knowingly take part in the services I conduct.

These people know the church bureaucracy well and can see that it contains no spiritual truth — only political and administrative manipulation,” Father Dorotheus wrote on his social media page.

Dorotheus believes another factor also prompted the AOC leadership to step up its activity. On 28 August 2026, Abkhaz President Badra Gunba and Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy chief of staff of the Russian presidential administration, made an unofficial visit to the New Athos Monastery.

According to Dorotheus, this was the first time since 2011 that such high-ranking officials had visited their monastery.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

Boycott of the New Athos Monastery

World.title: Georgian ‘delegation’ delivers gifts to Russian unit fighting against Ukraine
World.content:
According to Russia’s RIA Novosti news agency, Georgian volunteers on a “humanitarian mission” in the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic delivered an icon of St George the Victorious, motorcycles and prayer rooms to a Russian unit named after St Gabriel Urgebadze and the Nevsky Brigade, which are fighting against Ukraine. Besik Danelia, a Georgian “public figure” who leads the volunteers, told the agency about the initiative.

The Georgian Orthodox Church strongly opposes the use of Archimandrite Gabriel Urgebadze’s name to justify or support military action. Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Georgian Patriarchate’s press service, said it was particularly unacceptable that some Russian Orthodox Church clergy had supported the initiative.

Father Gabriel (Urgebadze) was a Georgian Orthodox monk and archimandrite whom the Georgian Orthodox Church canonised as a saint. One of the best-known episodes of his life took place in 1965, during the Soviet era. During a 1 May demonstration, he publicly burned a huge portrait of Lenin. Authorities beat him severely, arrested him and sent him to a psychiatric hospital. Later, despite pressure and persecution from the authorities, he continued his church service. His life became associated with strict asceticism, helping others and the idea of love.

What is known about the unit named after Father Gabriel and Besik Danelia

In an interview with RIA Novosti, Besik Danelia said he had travelled to Donetsk to visit “brothers” who, according to him, “are defending their homeland on the front line”, and had brought them humanitarian aid.

Andrei Kramar, a representative of the de facto authorities in occupied Donetsk, also said that a “Georgian delegation” that openly supports Russia’s war had visited the region.

“A Georgian delegation came to us and brought humanitarian aid. They are doing this openly. They are proud to support and have chosen a side in the special military operation,” Kramar said.

Reports about the existence of a “Orthodox” unit named after Father Gabriel Urgebadze and made up of ethnic Georgians first emerged in January 2026.

Besik Danelia (right) in Donetsk. Photo: press service of Andrei Kramar, deputy chairman of the so-called DPR’s People’s Council

Besik Danelia was previously a member of Nino Burjanadze’s pro-Russian Democratic Movement – United Georgia party. He has also appeared on the Georgia Wave media platform, which is linked to Putin supporter Mamuka Pipia, where he echoed the Georgian Dream ruling party’s calls for an apology to Georgia’s occupied regions.

Georgian “delegation” in Donetsk

What the Georgian Patriarchate says

The Georgian Patriarchate says that using the name of Archimandrite Gabriel Urgebadze for a military unit is particularly incompatible with his legacy.

Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze: “First of all, let us note that Orthodox people are dying on both sides of the Russia-Ukraine war. We watch this with deep pain in our hearts. We pray and ask the saints to intercede so that the Lord may grant peace to Ukraine, Russia and the whole world. And at such a time, without any consultation with the Georgian Orthodox Church or consideration of its position, we have unexpectedly encountered an unprecedented situation.

For us, it is categorically unacceptable to use the name of the Venerable Father Gabriel, an archimandrite, confessor and holy fool, for a military unit. The life and spiritual struggle of the saint were entirely devoted to faith in our Lord Jesus Christ and to preaching love and compassion for others.

It is also deeply disturbing that some clergy of the Russian Church support such an unacceptable use of the Venerable Father’s name.

It appears that the authors of this initiative are poorly acquainted with the life of Saint Gabriel. Against this background, this action appears to be a biased attempt to exploit the name of the Church.

The Georgian Orthodox Church distances itself from the use of the name of the Venerable Gabriel the Confessor and Holy Fool to justify or support military action.”

Gabriel Urgebadze unit

World.title: From ‘crown prince’ to prisoner: Irakli Garibashvili’s break with Georgia’s ruling party
World.content:
Irakli Garibashvili vs Georgian Dream

Georgia’s two-time former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili is currently in prison, from where he has openly challenged the authorities he himself represented for many years.

Over the past few weeks, he has published six letters accusing the Georgian government of persecution, blackmail and attempts to destroy his political future.

Garibashvili initially said the pressure against him had been exerted on the orders of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder and honorary chairman of the ruling Georgian Dream party. His criticism, however, later focused primarily on current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze and another influential party figure, Mamuka Mdinaradze.

The confrontation is particularly unusual for a party that for many years appeared from the outside to be an entirely monolithic political organisation.

Irakli Garibashvili is far from an ordinary former official. For almost two decades, he was one of Bidzina Ivanishvili‘s closest and most trusted associates. When Ivanishvili stepped down as prime minister in 2013, he effectively installed the then 31-year-old Garibashvili as his successor.

Now Ivanishvili’s former chosen successor is writing from prison that the very system he once served has “stabbed him in the back”.

Garibashvili’s case is therefore no longer simply a criminal case involving a former prime minister. It has exposed a conflict within Georgian Dream and raised a broader question: is a new redistribution of power beginning within the ruling party?

From prime minister’s office to prison cell

Irakli Garibashvili’s career under Bidzina Ivanishvili’s wing began long before Georgian Dream came to power in 2012.

As early as 2011, Ivanishvili referred to Garibashvili as one of his closest advisers and aides.

Following Georgian Dream’s victory in the 2012 parliamentary election, Garibashvili became interior minister. A year later, Ivanishvili stepped down as prime minister and named Garibashvili as his successor.

Garibashvili consequently served his first term as Georgia’s prime minister from 2013 to 2015. He unexpectedly left government at the end of 2015, but returned in 2019 as defence minister. In 2021, he became prime minister for a second time.

During his second premiership, Garibashvili was one of Georgian Dream’s most hardline figures. He frequently clashed with the opposition, civil society and Western critics. Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Garibashvili repeatedly echoed the government’s narrative about the threat of a “second front” being opened in Georgia and accused some Western figures of supporting the opposition.

In January 2024, he again stepped down as prime minister and was replaced by Irakli Kobakhidze. Garibashvili, meanwhile, became chairman of Georgian Dream. At the time, the party presented the change as a routine internal reshuffle.

In April 2025, Garibashvili announced that he was leaving politics altogether.

Several months later, a criminal investigation was launched against him.

How former prime minister ended up in prison

In October 2025, prosecutors charged Irakli Garibashvili with laundering a particularly large amount of illicit income.

According to investigators, the former prime minister provided false information in his asset declarations in an attempt to make illegally obtained income appear legitimate.

At the time, Garibashvili chose to remain silent and did not contest the case. On 12 January 2026, he pleaded guilty and reached a plea agreement with prosecutors. Under the deal, he was sentenced to five years in prison and fined 1m lari ($360,000). Two of his cars and $6.5m seized during a search of his home were also forfeited to the state.

After being taken into custody in the courtroom, Garibashvili was transferred directly to Penitentiary Establishment No 12 in the city of Rustavi.

Garibashvili later gave an almost sacred significance to his decision to remain silent. He now says that, at the time, he had consciously chosen not to confront the authorities.

Garibashvili and Ivanishvili: relationship spanning almost 20 years

Garibashvili worked in Ivanishvili’s circle even before Georgian Dream was founded. When Ivanishvili entered politics in 2011, Garibashvili was one of his closest associates. And, as noted above, in 2013 Ivanishvili handed him the leadership of the Georgian government.

Ivanishvili himself has often spoken about the early years of their personal relationship. In 2013, he recalled that Garibashvili had worked in the commercial department of one of his companies when Ivanishvili was buying a French-made helicopter. According to Ivanishvili, the young Garibashvili handled the negotiations with the French side so successfully that the sellers wanted to meet him in person.

In Georgian political circles, their relationship was widely seen as one between a patron and his political successor. Government opponents even described Garibashvili as Ivanishvili’s “obedient servant”, while Georgian media frequently portrayed him as a politician “groomed” by Ivanishvili and as being as close to him “as a son”.

Another episode also illustrates the hierarchical nature of their relationship.

In 2021, when Garibashvili was serving his second term as Georgia’s prime minister, a video recording of Bidzina Ivanishvili giving evidence in a Bermuda court was made public. The case concerned Ivanishvili’s legal dispute with Swiss bank Credit Suisse.

In court, Ivanishvili was asked what role Garibashvili had played in his financial affairs years earlier. Ivanishvili explained that Garibashvili had not been a financier and had mainly performed organisational tasks, such as arranging meetings, making phone calls and handling similar matters.

Asked, “So was he something like your secretary?”, Ivanishvili laughed and replied: “Call him whatever you like. Use whichever description you prefer.”

Following the release of the recording, political commentators highlighted the fact that Ivanishvili had twice appointed as the country’s prime minister a former subordinate whose earlier duties he had described in court in dismissive terms.

Ivanishvili mentioned in Garibashvili’s letter from prison

Against this backdrop, Garibashvili’s first public reference to Ivanishvili in a letter from prison, published on 17 August 2026, was particularly significant.

Garibashvili wrote that he had received an offer made on Ivanishvili’s instructions: to confess to another offence, this time a serious corruption crime. In return, he said he had been promised that the new charge would not add to his existing five-year prison sentence.

According to the former prime minister, the deal came with another condition: after his release from prison, he would not be allowed to return to politics.

Garibashvili said the authorities were seeking to ensure that he could not make a political comeback. In the same statement, he held Ivanishvili and the Georgian Dream leadership personally responsible for his own safety and that of his family.

In his next letter, Garibashvili again referred to Ivanishvili, but this time in a markedly different tone.

He wrote that he had endured the authorities’ actions for many months because of his “20-year relationship with Bidzina Ivanishvili, immense love and respect for him, boundless gratitude and absolute loyalty to him“.

In subsequent letters, Garibashvili has sought gradually to shift the focus of the conflict away from Ivanishvili and towards the Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze tandem.

Some analysts believe Garibashvili is trying to avoid burning his remaining bridges with Ivanishvili and to persuade him that the real problem lies with the current prime minister and his circle.

Garibashvili, his wife Nunuka Tamazashvili and Bidzina Ivanishvili

Irakli Kobakhidze and Irakli Garibashvili

What changed after Garibashvili‘s letters

After 17 August, Garibashvili definitively broke his silence.

Several key allegations gradually emerged from his letters. He claims that the authorities deceived him, put pressure on members of his family, demanded that he confess to another corruption offence, and ultimately sought to eliminate any possibility of his return to politics.

Garibashvili also said that he had been given indications that his 75-year-old father could also be arrested.

Mamuka Mdinaradze rejected these allegations.

However, subsequent developments lent additional weight to Garibashvili’s claims.

On 24 August, prosecutors brought new charges against him.

This time, the case concerns the alleged receipt of a particularly large bribe, an offence punishable by between 11 and 15 years in prison if he is convicted.

According to prosecutors, Garibashvili received 750,000 lari ($275,735) through a scheme involving classified procurement contracts at the Defence Ministry. The investigation relies primarily on testimony from former Defence Minister Juansher Burchuladze and his alleged accomplice, Vasil Mkheidze.

Garibashvili has pleaded not guilty to the new charge.

The former prime minister says the proceedings are being used as a tool to exert political pressure on him.

Mdinaradze’s sudden departure

Meanwhile, against the backdrop of Garibashvili’s letters and his allegations against Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze, another significant development took place:

Mamuka Mdinaradze and Irakli Kobakhidze

Mamuka Mdinaradze, who for many years was one of Georgian Dream’s most influential figures and one of Kobakhidze’s closest political allies, announced that he was leaving the government and withdrawing from politics altogether.

In 2025, Mdinaradze was appointed head of the State Security Service, but remained in the post for only a short time. In July 2026, Irakli Kobakhidze announced that Mdinaradze would become regional development minister in September and was expected to play a key role in overseeing regional policy.

However, on 27 August, Mdinaradze unexpectedly announced that he was not only stepping down from his ministerial post but leaving politics altogether.

Garibashvili linked the move to his letters.

“Mamuka Mdinaradze made such serious and grave mistakes in this case that they resulted not only in his removal from office, but also in his departure from politics,” the disgraced former prime minister wrote on 2 September in his fifth letter.

Mdinaradze himself presented his departure as a personal decision.

Why Garibashvili has become a problem for Kobakhidze

Garibashvili’s letters have raised questions about how much political influence the former prime minister retains while in prison. Some analysts believe Garibashvili still has supporters within Georgian Dream and that the authorities’ sharp response to his letters is evidence of his continuing political significance.

Conflict analyst Paata Zakareishvili says Garibashvili realised that he enjoyed greater sympathy within Georgian Dream than Kobakhidze did, and that this encouraged him to continue resisting.

Kobakhidze, Zakareishvili argues, in turn discovered that “even Garibashvili sitting in prison is stronger than he is”.

One possible explanation for this assessment lies in the two men’s very different political backgrounds.

Garibashvili belongs to the first generation of the ruling party and has been part of Georgian Dream since its foundation. He was a member of Ivanishvili’s inner circle and built up strong political connections over the years, particularly in the regions.

Kobakhidze’s power, by contrast, is much more closely tied to the party apparatus and Ivanishvili’s direct backing.

Analyst Irakli Melashvili describes Garibashvili as a “symbolic figure” for supporters of the “old Georgian Dream”. In his assessment, the former prime minister was particularly close to the party’s conservative and pro-Russian electorate.

At the same time, Melashvili points to a fundamental contradiction: Garibashvili has now himself become a target of the system of which he was one of the principal architects and leaders for many years.

For that reason, his resistance cannot automatically be seen as a struggle for a democratic system.

“This is a struggle for his own survival, not for the public good,” Melashvili says.

Lazare Jorbenadze case and a new phase of confrontation

On 1 September, Garibashvili went a step further.

In another letter from prison, he demanded that the authorities provide answers about the circumstances surrounding the death of human rights activist Lazare Jorbenadze, who had publicly criticised Kobakhidze.

Garibashvili also wrote that questions remained unanswered about other cases of suicide which, he said, were linked to the period when the Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze group was in power.

Prosecutors subsequently questioned Garibashvili himself, as well as several other politicians and public figures. A prosecution service representative said Garibashvili had provided no information to substantiate claims that Jorbenadze may have been murdered.

Sixth letter: open confrontation with authorities

On 8 September, Garibashvili published his sixth letter.

He described the authorities’ response as a “ridiculous, repulsive and tragic masquerade” and said the questioning over the Jorbenadze case was an attempt to link him to the opposition United National Movement party.

Garibashvili also responded sarcastically to allegations in pro-government media that he had been acting in the interests of the “deep state” or France.

“I am lucky that I don’t know any other foreign languages, otherwise I would probably have been declared an agent of other countries as well,” he wrote.

He then addressed the authorities directly: “Stop these dirty political games against me!”

Garibashvili said he served neither the West nor the East, neither the North nor the South, and that his sole aim had been to serve Georgia.

He addressed parliament speaker Shalva Papuashvili separately: “Shalva, this is not a legal process — this is ruthless political persecution!“

The letter ends with a message the former prime minister has repeatedly made in recent weeks:

“I am not fighting anyone — you yourselves stabbed me in the back… Now I am forced to defend myself and my family against this injustice and cruelty.”

‘Criminal’, ‘traitor’, ‘agent’: how party responded to former PM

Following Garibashvili’s fifth letter, Georgian Dream’s response became particularly harsh.

A man who twice served as prime minister for the party is now being described by his former allies as a “criminal” and a “traitor”.

A politician who for years himself used harsh rhetoric against government opponents has now become a target of the same system. The language being used against him will be familiar to the government’s critics: allegations of corruption, betrayal, serving the radical opposition and acting in the interests of foreign states.

Georgian Dream representatives say Garibashvili’s narrative has become indistinguishable from that of the “radical opposition”.

MP Gia Volski suggested that the former prime minister may have been led to believe that his struggle could help advance a “revolutionary process” in the country and that he could subsequently benefit from it politically.

Another MP, Dimitri Samkharadze, described Garibashvili as a “self-confessed criminal” and a traitor.

Meanwhile, pro-government television channels, citing Azerbaijani media, circulated allegations that Garibashvili had been acting in France’s interests in Georgia.

Current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze also responded in exceptionally harsh terms.

He described his predecessor’s letters as “ridiculous and tragic”, saying Garibashvili had “sunk to the level of a blogger for some shady little newspaper”.

Georgian Dream secretary-general and Tbilisi mayor Kakha Kaladze, meanwhile, said it was regrettable to see his former ally in such a position, but publicly expressed his full support for Kobakhidze.

Ivanishvili remains silent

The key figure in the entire confrontation has so far remained largely out of public view.

Bidzina Ivanishvili has remained silent.

This is particularly notable because both sides in the conflict ultimately derived their political weight from his backing.

Political analyst Gia Khukhashvili sees one possible scenario in which Ivanishvili himself is managing the current process, with the ultimate aim of weakening Kobakhidze’s team.

Other analysts offer a more cautious interpretation: Ivanishvili is watching the confrontation unfold and will make a decision only when it becomes clear which figure is more useful for preserving his system.

David Zurabishvili, who supports this interpretation, says Ivanishvili has no permanent allies, only permanent interests. Accordingly, neither Garibashvili nor Kobakhidze is indispensable to him.

This explanation is also consistent with Georgian Dream’s history: prime ministers have changed repeatedly during the party’s time in power, while the centre of power has consistently remained with Ivanishvili.

Kobakhidze has no intention of stepping down

Against this backdrop, speculation is already mounting in Georgia over the possible resignation of Irakli Kobakhidze himself.

He has, however, dismissed the rumours.

Kobakhidze said journalists ask him “every three months” whether he is planning to step down as prime minister, adding that he expects to be asked the same question again in another three months.

More significant, however, was his explanation of what had happened within the government after he took office.

According to Kobakhidze, he and his team needed a year and five months to address what he described as “fundamental problems” that had accumulated within the system of government, acting on Bidzina Ivanishvili’s instructions.

Kobakhidze did not directly name Garibashvili in his remarks. The chronology, however, is clear: he was referring to problems that had accumulated in the system during his namesake’s tenure as prime minister.

Is Georgian Dream’s monolith beginning to crack?

Georgian Dream formally retains almost complete control over Georgia’s political system.

It dominates parliament, is seeking to ban several opposition groups, and many opposition leaders are in prison.

Yet it is under these circumstances that a conflict has erupted not between the government and the opposition, but between current and former leaders of the ruling establishment itself.

Giorgi Melashvili, head of the Europe-Georgia Institute, describes the situation as two parallel processes: on the one hand, the circle of decision-makers is narrowing and the system is becoming increasingly centralised; on the other, the Garibashvili case has exposed cracks in Georgian Dream’s internal monolith.

In his assessment, neither the opposition nor other former Georgian Dream figures have dealt the party a blow comparable to that inflicted by Garibashvili’s letters.

Gia Khukhashvili, meanwhile, describes the developments as a confrontation between two factions “at the royal court”. In his view, Ivanishvili remains the only person with the final say.

Much about these scenarios remains speculative, but the facts themselves already present a highly unusual picture:

Former PM behind bars: A two-time former prime minister is in prison, accusing the authorities of political persecution and his former allies of trying to destroy him and his family.

A two-time former prime minister is in prison, accusing the authorities of political persecution and his former allies of trying to destroy him and his family. New criminal case: Following his first letters, he was hit with a new and significantly more serious criminal charge.

Following his first letters, he was hit with a new and significantly more serious criminal charge. Mdinaradze’s sudden departure: One of his main opponents within the ruling team, Mamuka Mdinaradze, unexpectedly left politics altogether.

One of his main opponents within the ruling team, Mamuka Mdinaradze, unexpectedly left politics altogether. Question of succession: Current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze is already having to publicly answer questions about whether he could become the “next former” prime minister.

And Bidzina Ivanishvili, who stands at the centre of all these developments, continues to remain silent.

World.title: ‘Major cause for concern’: expert view on Armenian school students’ low level of knowledge
World.content:
Low knowledge levels among Armenian school students

School students in Armenia lag behind their peers in Georgia, Azerbaijan and Turkey in terms of their level of knowledge. The comparison focuses in particular on 15-year-old students.

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) conducted its annual study as part of the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). Experts assessed students’ knowledge of mathematics and science, as well as their ability to analyse what they read.

The study included 760,000 15-year-old students from 91 countries. The results showed that the overall state of education around the world leaves much to be desired. However, experts in Armenia are particularly concerned about the situation in their own country. The education problems have also alarmed people far beyond the field’s specialist community.

Economist Tigran Jrbashyan sees the study’s results as a major cause for concern.

“This is no longer a problem for the education ministry. It is a question of Armenia’s economic security and long-term competitiveness,” he stressed.

Jrbashyan published several posts on his Facebook page, calling on the government to take immediate action. He proposes introducing a special regime in the education sector over the coming years.

Подробнее о результатах исследования, а также комментарий экономиста Тиграна Джрбашяна.

Results for students in Armenia and leading countries

According to the study, some cities in China lead the rankings for educational achievement, followed by Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan. The UK and Estonia also rank among the top 10.

Armenia’s results lag behind those of every other country in the region. Armenian school students scored below the OECD average in all areas covered by the study.

The average share of Armenian school students reaching the benchmark was

28% in science (OECD average — 74%),

28% in mathematics (OECD average — 65%),

19% in reading and the ability to analyse written text (OECD average — 67%).

Less than 1% of Armenian students achieved the highest level in mathematics, while the figure was even lower in science.

“And virtually none of the students demonstrated reading skills that would indicate an ability to understand lengthy texts, work with abstract or contradictory concepts, and distinguish facts from opinions,” Radio Azatutyun reports.

Comment

According to Tigran Jrbashyan, an economist and head of Ameriabank’s management consulting service, the PISA study assesses not so much what 15-year-olds know as their ability to apply their knowledge in practice: understanding texts, analysing information and solving problems.

“Among our 15-year-olds, 28% reach at least the minimum, Level 2 proficiency in mathematics. The figure is also 28% in science. In reading, however, only 19% reach this level. In other words, four out of five of our 15-year-olds do not even reach the basic level of functional reading literacy,” he said.

Meanwhile, according to the PISA study, 39% of teenagers in Georgia reach the basic level of reading literacy, compared with 36% in Kazakhstan and 35% in Azerbaijan.

The economist argues that no matter how much Armenia talks about its achievements in artificial intelligence and high technology, all its planned initiatives will remain unrealised projects without human capital.

“If Armenia ranks third from the bottom in problem-solving skills among 15-year-olds, our ambitions in AI and high technology cannot be limited to investment, equipment and infrastructure alone,” he explained.

Jrbashyan notes that Armenia has built, renovated and modernised schools in recent years. He considers this an unquestionable investment in the quality of education. At the same time, he says the country needs to change how it assesses the effectiveness of education policy.

In particular, he proposes assessing

how students’ reading skills and their mathematical and scientific knowledge have changed as a result of these investments;

whether the share of students who fail to reach the basic level has decreased;

whether the share of high-performing students has increased.

The analyst insists that, given the current situation, the government needs to

take immediate action to determine at which stage of the education system, and for what reasons, students lose ground;

set measurable targets for 2028 and 2031 and consistently work towards achieving them.

“The cost of inaction in the context of PISA is not simply a low ranking. It means lost economic growth and the loss of Armenia’s competitiveness for decades to come,” he stressed.

The expert believes the PISA 2025 results show that the scale of Armenia’s education problem has outgrown the pace of the government’s response. As a result, reforms carried out at the usual pace are no longer enough:

“I would propose declaring education an emergency national priority and introducing a special management regime for three to five years.”

Jrbashyan stresses that an emergency regime should mean not only faster decision-making and more resources, but also much greater accountability for results.

Moreover, he sees a need for national mobilisation on the issue. He believes education policy should not measure its success only through the next PISA study:

“We need to create a national system of regular assessment that will allow us to see every year where we are making progress and where we are not, and adjust policy accordingly.”

World.title: The transaction between ABB Bank and Davr Bank has been completed!
World.content:
The process of completing the transaction between ABB Financial Group and Davr Bank, a commercial bank operating in Uzbekistan, has been successfully finalized. The transaction was registered on 10 September 2026 at the Tashkent Stock Exchange.

The total value of the transaction amounts to 1.646 trillion soums (approximately USD 140 million). According to the terms of the agreement, ABB Bank acquired 51 million ordinary shares of Davr Bank, obtaining a 51% stake in the bank’s capital.

In the coming days, the Bank will commence operations in the Uzbekistan market under the “ABB Davr” brand as a universal bank and will provide a wide range of banking services to individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as large corporate organizations.

Currently, Davr Bank serves more than 2 million customers, has over 1,800 employees, and operates 43 branches and service centers in the capital and regions. The bank’s total assets exceed 2 billion manats. The Bank maintains an active position, particularly in the area of small and medium-sized business financing.

It should be noted that, within the framework of the state visit of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Mr. Ilham Aliyev to Uzbekistan on 23 August 2026, the official opening ceremony of the “ABB Davr Bank” project was held with the participation of the Presidents of Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

ABB Financial Group’s strategic vision regarding its operations in the Uzbekistan market can be found in an interview with ABB Bank’s Chairman of the Management Board Abbas Ibrahimov.

Information about ABB Bank’s modern, useful, and universal products and services is available at the Bank’s branches and offices, on the official website https://abb-bank.az/, through the Information Center at 937, as well as on the Bank’s official corporate social media pages.

World.title: Azerbaijan, Türkiye seek to connect Eurasia through electricity links
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 11. Azerbaijan and Türkiye are seeking to connect a large region, including Eurasia, through electricity interconnections, Azerbaijan’s Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov said at a briefing following the signing ceremony of the 5th Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

“We are discussing not only electricity generation but also electricity interconnections. We want to connect a large region, Eurasia, through Azerbaijan and Türkiye,” Shahbazov said.

The minister said he had arrived in Baku with a delegation broadly representing Türkiye’s energy sector and that the 5th Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum had successfully concluded.

“It is generally known that brotherly and partnership relations exist between Azerbaijan and Türkiye. As a result of the political will of President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev and President of the Republic of Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, these relations have developed even more strongly in recent years. With the Shusha Declaration, our ties and relations have taken on the character of a strategic alliance,” Shahbazov said.

According to him, as reflected in the Shusha Declaration, energy cooperation contributes to the development not only of the two countries but also of the broader region, and this process will continue.

The minister noted that major projects implemented between Azerbaijan and Türkiye, including the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan, Baku-Tbilisi-Erzurum, TANAP and STAR projects, contribute not only to the prosperity of the two countries but also to the broader region and participants in the global energy market.

“Our cooperation also makes a major contribution to the energy security of the European Union. It is through Türkiye that our energy resources are delivered to global markets. This cooperation continues in both oil and gas. In recent years, we have already supplied gas to 16 countries, which in itself is a good example of how intensively Azerbaijan-Türkiye relations are developing,” he said.

Shahbazov emphasized that the goal of the Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum is not only to continue existing cooperation but also to identify future prospects and upcoming challenges.

“We want to continue our successful cooperation in oil and gas in the area of electrification as well. With the beginning of the new electricity era, the development of digitalization and artificial intelligence will require large amounts of electricity. We have major plans in this area. We are discussing not only electricity generation but also electricity interconnections. We want to connect a large region, Eurasia, through Azerbaijan and Türkiye,” the minister added.

According to him, discussions are currently underway on the electricity interconnection between Nakhchivan and Türkiye, the Azerbaijan-Georgia-Türkiye-Bulgaria electricity interconnection, as well as new electricity interconnections planned to run across the Black Sea.

“All of these will make it possible to transmit both renewable electricity and electricity in general over long distances and to regions of interest to us. At the same time, Azerbaijan is continuing the same processes with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, that is, with Central Asia. We are discussing all of these issues in an integrated manner within the framework of the Energy Forum,” Shahbazov said.

World.title: Azerbaijan, Türkiye take energy partnership to new strategic stage – minister
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 11. Energy cooperation between Azerbaijan and Türkiye has further strengthened and taken on new strategic significance under the leadership of President Ilham Aliyev and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Azerbaijan’s Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov said while speaking at the 5th Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum in Baku, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

The minister noted that this stage is characterized by efforts to strengthen national and regional energy security, diversify energy flows, establish interconnections in line with the requirements of the new era of electricity, integrate energy systems and advance a shared vision for the Turkic world.

“The Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum, through its regular meetings and the work of its working groups, contributes to implementing this strategic agenda and continues to make a sustained contribution to deepening our cooperation in hydrocarbons, renewable energy, energy efficiency, electricity, regulation and mining,” Shahbazov said.

According to him, joint efforts during this period have produced significant results in the energy partnership.

“The commissioning of the Igdir-Nakhchivan gas pipeline, made possible by the strong political will of our countries; the entry of Turkish Petroleum into the Shah Deniz project; the agreement to export part of the gas to be produced during the full-scale development of the Absheron field to Türkiye; as well as the transportation of Azerbaijani gas through Türkiye to new European markets beyond the coverage of the Southern Gas Corridor and to Syria demonstrate the expanding scale and geography of our energy partnership,” the minister emphasized.

The 5th Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum is being held in Baku with the participation of Azerbaijan’s Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov and Türkiye’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar.

The forum features discussions on hydrocarbons and petrochemicals, energy efficiency, the electricity market, renewable energy, regulation, mining and other areas. The forum protocol is expected to be signed at the end of the event, followed by a media briefing.

The Azerbaijan-Türkiye Energy Forum was established under the framework of the Joint Commission on Economic Cooperation between the two countries to further strengthen strategic energy cooperation.

World.title: Uzbekistan, South Korea build stronger investment partnerships
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 11. Tashkent region is seeking to expand investment and industrial cooperation with South Korean regions and companies.

This was reflected in the statement by the Tashkent regional administration, following a visit of a delegation from Tashkent region led by Governor Zoyir Mirzayev to South Korea to develop practical and mutually beneficial cooperation, with the first day of the visit focused on the First Uzbekistan-Korea Interregional Cooperation Forum in Seoul.

The forum brought together representatives of the two countries’ governments and state institutions, ministries and agencies, regional authorities, international organizations and business communities.

Participants discussed the current state of interregional cooperation between Uzbekistan and South Korea and ways to give the partnership new practical content. Key areas included human capital development, social and cultural ties, industrial cooperation, investment partnerships and the digital economy.

Uzbekistan’s Deputy Prime Minister Jamshid Khodjayev said the strategic partnership and alliance between Uzbekistan and South Korea have reached a qualitatively new stage in recent years, supported by the long-term and pragmatic policies of the two countries’ leaders.

“Uzbekistan and South Korea are not only close political partners, but are also consistently developing cooperation in economic integration, industrial cooperation, transport and logistics, innovation, education and humanitarian affairs,” Khodjayev said.

Mirzayev also addressed the forum, highlighting the strengthening of ties between Tashkent region and South Korean provinces. He noted established cooperation with Jeollanam-do, Gyeongsangbuk-do and Gyeongsangnam-do provinces, as well as twinning arrangements between cities and districts.

The governor presented Tashkent region’s investment potential and opportunities for foreign partners in industry, agriculture, innovation and other priority sectors.

“Tashkent region is interested in expanding direct cooperation with South Korean regions and companies and turning established interregional ties into concrete investment and industrial projects,” the regional administration said.

The forum also featured the opening ceremony of the Korea-Uzbekistan Economic Association, which is expected to serve as a platform for direct business contacts, new investment initiatives and business partnerships between companies from the two countries.

A number of bilateral documents were also exchanged during the event.

As part of the forum, the Tashkent region delegation held B2B and G2B meetings with representatives of major South Korean companies and businesses. The discussions focused on investment projects, industrial cooperation, the introduction of advanced technologies and the development of new joint initiatives.

The delegation’s visit will continue with meetings and negotiations aimed at expanding cooperation between Tashkent region and South Korean regions and companies, according to the regional administration.

World.title: 'Landmark' NT novel wins best fiction at Prime Minister's Literary Awards
World.content:
A novel based on the oral history of Yolŋu people from north-east Arnhem Land has been named as this year's fiction pick at the Prime Minister's Literary Awards.

Darwin-born author Leonie Norrington and co-authors Djawundil Maymuru, Merrikiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs and Djawa Burarrwanga have won the $80,000 fiction prize for their book A Piece of Red Cloth.

Told from the perspective of Yolŋu people, the book tells the story of a grandmother's quest to protect her granddaughter from Macassan trepang fishermen during the 1600s, while they learn to interact with foreigners.

Leonie Norrington says winning the award is a "recognition of history". (ABC News)

The Prime Minister's Literary Awards judges labelled the novel as a "landmark achievement in fiction", writing it "is also an urgent example of intercultural work, setting a high benchmark for collaboration between Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal writers".

"It is a profound work of remembrance and re-imagination, fusing oral history, novelistic technique and deep cultural knowledge," the judges said.

Having grown up in the Barunga community, Dr Norrington said her Aboriginal mother Clare Bush inspired her to write A Piece of Red Cloth before she died.

Dr Norrington said her Aboriginal mother wanted the Yolŋu people's story told to help people in other parts of the country to understand the country was "alive" and we are "one with the earth".

"If we only have what she called 'Captain Cook history', then we're always going to have a frontier mentality about our country," she said.

"We can exploit the country because we're not from the country.

Prime Minister's Literary Awards announced Kate Wild's book about the fatal shooting of Kumanjayi Walker and the ensuing murder trial, The Red House, is one of six PMLA winners.

"We could belong to the country and then have more respect for the country and for the first peoples of the country, not just as the first people who lived here, but the people who emerged at the same time as the country."

Speaking to Radio National in 2025, local custodian Merrikiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs said the book explores cultural traditions that are still apparent in modern communities while re-telling the story of how Yolŋu people had been trading with countries overseas for centuries.

Merrkiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs accepted the award in Canberra on Thursday. (ABC News: Billy Cooper)

"All I can is that we still live like this, like what's happening in the book today," she told the program.

"Even if we are modern people, we still go out bush, we till dig for that yams, for those roots get it up oysters, still live it, still eat it."

Dr Norrington said winning the award was a "recognition of history" and hoped her book could be a driving force for action.

"Our history has been read by the Prime Minister of Australia and now things can change," she said.

Leonie Norrington and Merrikiyawuy Ganambarr-Stubbs were part of the group that collaborated to write A Piece of Red Cloth. (Supplied)

"I think if I was going to have a message to the prime minister, I think it would be that Australia is a terribly, terribly dry and very fragile country and we need to look after it.

"The future generations of Australia really rely on us making good decisions about what we do with this very fragile land."

A Piece of Red Cloth wasn't the only NT winner at the prestigious awards — Kate Wild's book The Red House, about the fatal shooting of Kumanjayi Walker in Yuendumu and the murder trial of police officer Zachary Rolfe, won the non-fiction category.

World.title: Putin and Iranian president arrive in India for summit focusing on war
World.content:
Vladimir Putin has arrived in India for talks ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit dominated by economic challenges and conflict in the Middle East and Ukraine, with the leaders of China and Iran set to attend.

War, global trade turbulence and oil are expected on the agenda at the two-day annual summit which opens on Saturday, when Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to arrive.

It will be Mr Xi's first visit to India since 2019, marking the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the rival neighbours.

The visit comes six years after a deadly military clash between China and India along their disputed Himalayan border.

Xi Jinping is making his first visit to India since 2019. (Reuters: Maxim Shemetov)

Ties between both nuclear-armed China and India have warmed in recent months, with flights, visas and high-level contacts gradually being restored.

But deep mistrust remains within their contested frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry still complicating the relationship.

"One should engage in debate and friendship only with the virtuous, and nothing whatsoever with the unvirtuous," Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in a post on social media on Friday, welcome arriving leaders.

Modi calls for end to Ukraine war India's PM Narendra Modi tells Putin the war in Ukraine needs to end.

Mr Modi is due to hold talks later on Friday with Mr Putin, who last visited India in December 2025. Moscow is one of New Delhi's most important strategic partners.

India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the Iran war in part by turning to Russia, one of its most important relationships and most controversial fuel supplier in recent years, as the war in Ukraine drags on.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is also expected on Friday, and is also set to hold talks with Mr Modi.

Posters of leaders in attendance of the BRICS summit line the streets of New Delhi. (Reuters: Francis Mascarenhas)

Gulf conflict is the 'fault line'

The BRICS summit was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions typically dominated by Western powers.

It has since expanded to include Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, three countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the BRICS summit," said Harsh V Pant, a professor of international relations and vice president of India's Observer Research Foundation.

" What was seen until last year as an achievement, the expansion of BRICS, today looks like a big constraint on BRICS. "

It will be Mr Pezeshkian's first visit to India as Iranian president, and will put the Middle East conflict firmly in conversations.

Econimist Shilan Shah said the war in Iran would provide a stern test of the expanded group's cohesion.

Mr Shah noted the failure of the BRICS foreign ministers to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May.

United Arab Emirates President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan, and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi are all expected to be in attendance.

India maintains cordial relations with Iran and Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington.

Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited Kyiv this month when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was "grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war".

World.title: Live: Dockers and Cats put season on the line in semifinal showdown
World.content:
It was a chastening Thursday night for Fremantle last week. Riding into the finals series with boundless confidence after a dominant home and away season and minor premiership, the Dockers were taught a lesson by the relentless Hawks.

(Getty Images)

Too many went missing, too many failed to step up on the big stage, and overall the Hawks looked a more powerful and finals-ready unit than their rivals from the west. Freo were well beaten, never in the contest, and copped a pasting in the media for their efforts.

Geelong was challenged early by Carlton and looked in strife during periods of the first half, but after the long break flicked a switch and rather cruised to victory in their elimination final.

The best word to sum up the Cats' performance was professional. It was a "been there, done that" finals win from a side packed with experience and premiership players. They didn't panic when things weren't going well, and they didn't let up when the worm turned.

(Getty Images)

So tonight then. The Dockers will be breathing fire, certain they can't put in two stinkers in a row. This will be their last chance to play in front of their home crowd, and those fans will be just as ferocious the players.

But the Cats will look at Hawthorn last week and see a blueprint. Geelong is as well position as any of the remaining contenders to take a scalp like Freo's on the road, and might sense they are there to be taken.

World.title: Being a renter, Jenny missed out on solar boon but that is about to change
World.content:
Australia could soon follow in the footsteps of Germany and the United Kingdom as it prepares to lift a ban on plug-in solar and batteries, unlocking access to the technology for millions of apartment dwellers and renters for the first time.

The move was discussed during a meeting of the country's energy ministers, where they agreed to explore pathways to support the "safe deployment" of plug-in solar across the country.

'Crazy' battery charging fires gas power Australia is leading the world in the adoption of batteries. But in one state, storage is fuelling some perverse and pricey outcomes.

The systems, which are also commonly referred to as 'balcony solar', were legalised in the United Kingdom last month and New Zealand has flagged plans to do the same within 12 months.

Germany is a world-leader in plug-in solar, with an estimated one in 10 households having a system installed.

It can technically be sold in Australia but not legally plugged in and used.

Energy Minister Chris Bowen said a third of Australians have solar on their roof, making the technology "more popular than the backyard pool".

"Now we're taking the next step, by looking at how even more Australians can take advantage of free, abundant sunshine to cut their energy bills — even if they don't have a roof.

"All state and territory ministers are on board and will work with the Commonwealth to look at how plug-in solar and batteries can work in Australia to give apartment dwellers more control over their energy bills."

Chris Bowen says a third of Australians have solar on their roof. (ABC News: Matt Roberts)

Heidi Lee Douglas is the CEO of Solar Citizens, a community organisation that's been campaigning for plug-in solar to be legalised, and welcomed that Australia was now a step closer to that reality.

"This commitment to make plug-in solar and plug-in batteries legal in Australia is great news for more than a third of Australians who rent or live in apartments, and also for low-income households so they can access some of the bill-busting benefits that cheap clean solar home owners enjoy," she said.

"We want to see a firm timeline and deadline by December at the next energy ministers meeting for when plug-in solar and batteries will be available for use in every state and territory.

" Australians are looking for every opportunity to bring down their power bills. "

Heidi Lee Douglas is the CEO of Solar Citizens and says plug-in systems would finally bring more social equity for the technology. (Supplied: Solar Citizens)

What are plug-in solar and batteries?

Plug-in solar systems and batteries can be plugged into regular power points and do not require installation by an electrician.

The power generated by the panels is fed into the home network via an inverter and a standard plug and helps offset electricity used by appliances.

Overseas, they are commonly attached to apartment balconies or installed in backyards and produce between 600-800 watts of power, typically at a cost of up to $1,300.

They are a popular choice for people who live in an apartment and cannot mount rooftop solar as well as renters, many of whom have never considered the possibility of accessing renewable energy.

More than 30 per cent of Australians are renting, which equates to almost 3 million households.

Maiya Irving-Mackinnon is a renter from the Sydney suburb of Marrickville who estimates her electricity bills have increased by about 15 per cent, or $200, over the past 12 months.

Maiya Irving-Mackinnon, a renter from the Sydney suburb of Marrickville, is keen to reduce her power bills by having a plug-in solar panel. (ABC News: Patrick Thomas)

"Solar has never really been something that we can consider as a renter because we can't install anything on the roof or on a ground floor apartment," she said.

"I would really like to have the option to install solar panels and for that to be subsidised but it's not really something that's been available for a renter before.

" During the day, if we were able to run our electronics at a reduced cost, if not for free, then I think that would make a really big difference to our energy bill. "

Experts have suggested the payback period for plug-in solar systems ranges from four to ten years.

Ms Lee Douglas expects some households will save up to $1,000 a year on electricity bills.

"The average plug-in solar panel will allow you to save about $300-$400 a year, and plug-in batteries will easily double that," she said.

Importantly, renters would be able to take the panels and batteries with them when they moved.

Barriers to overcome

Plug-in solar systems don't need installation; they are as easy to plug in as a kettle or toaster. (Supplied: Holger's Pictures)

The federal government will now work with the states and territories to "identify measures that enable the safe use" of plug-in solar and report back on next steps by the end of the year.

The federal government is yet to indicate whether it is considering offering subsidies or rebates for the technology.

Solar Citizens is calling on plug-in solar and batteries to become legal in Australia by July next year.

But there are still barriers to overcome ahead of then, including ensuring safety standards are up to scratch for when products begin to enter the market.

Executive director of the German Plug-In Solar Association Craig Morris said Australia could look to the safety standards that Germany has developed as a starting point.

"The risk of too many companies coming in and some of them not being serious has gone down," he said.

"If you go back just five years, I think we had a number of companies that you didn't really know too much about them and maybe they were just trying a quick buck.

" But I think in the meantime, the big boys have taken over and pushed out some of the smaller firms. "

Benchmark power price drops Surging levels of renewable energy and better reliability from coal-fired generators are set to give consumers a break, with benchmark power prices to fall up to 10 per cent for consumers and more for small businesses.

Bringing landlords and body corporates on board to allow plug-in solar to be hung on balconies or stationed in backyards is another challenge that would need to be addressed in Australia before the technology is legalised and rolled out.

In Germany, tenants need to get permission to install plug-in solar but landlords need a good reason, such as planned facade renovations, to reject the request.

Mr Morris said ultimately, adoption of plug-in batteries would be crucial in allowing the full benefits of plug-in solar to be fully realised.

"What we're ultimately offering, which is plug-in solar with batteries, or maybe even plug-in batteries without solar, offering flexibility from households," he said.

"The batteries would charge and discharge not in order to optimise our consumption of the solar power we generate, but to optimise operation of the local grid.

"And this can save money across the board, across the country for everyone, even if you don't have a system, because we're going to optimise the usage of these public power lines."

World.title: Former Liberal candidate cautioned over LGBTQIA+ comments
World.content:
An Albany councillor and former Liberal candidate has been cautioned by the State Administrative Tribunal over his comments falsely linking the LGBTQIA+ community with paedophiles.

Thomas Brough, who is an emergency doctor at the Albany Health Campus, was referred to the SAT last year by the Medical Board of Australia after complaints to the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency.

In a settlement proceeding on Thursday, both parties agreed Dr Brough's comments constituted unprofessional conduct.

It comes two months after the tribunal dropped an order from the Local Government Standards Panel for Dr Brough to complete inclusivity training, finding the required course did not exist.

Thomas Brough is an emergency department doctor at the Albany Health Campus. (ABC Great Southern: Kyle Pauletto)

Unprofessional conduct

The decisions put an end to a long-running saga that began with a discussion of the city's pride festival at a council meeting in 2024.

"Within the coalition of the LGBTQIA+, I just want to hone in on the plus," Dr Brough said.

"That includes a group of people who identify as minor attracted persons."

He later doubled down on his comments while speaking to local media, sparking outrage from Albany Pride organisers, who made official complaints.

During his campaign for the WA state election a few months later, he issued a statement apologising for "any hurt that has been caused".

Albany Pride is a major LGBTQIA+ organisation in the Great Southern region. (ABC Great Southern: Jamie Thannoo)

Inclusivity training

The City of Albany engaged an independent assessor in response to complaints around the matter, who found Dr Brough's comments to be in breach of the local government code of conduct.

Under a directive from the Local Government Standards Panel, Dr Brough was asked to apologise and undertake inclusivity training provided by the Australian Human Rights Commission.

Thomas Brough has been a city councillor since 2021. (ABC Great Southern: Andrew Chounding)

Dr Brough successfully appealed that decision on the basis the required training did not exist, with SAT member Naomi Eeagling setting aside that part of the order on July 31.

Controversial figure

In 2025, WA Liberal leader Libby Mettam distanced herself from Dr Brough after he made anti-abortion comments during a press conference on hospital funding.

When asked if WA's abortion laws should be reviewed, Dr Brough replied "yes" before saying: "Babies born alive should not be left to die."

Thomas Brough ran as the Liberal candidate for Albany at the 2025 state election. (ABC News: Samantha Goerling)

In a statement sent to media after the press conference, Ms Mettam said a review of the state's abortion laws was not on the party's agenda.

Dr Brough's comments sparked robust debate in parliament, with Premier Roger Cook declaring there was "something sinister and rotten going on" in the Liberal Party.

Dr Brough ran for the Liberal Party for the seat of Albany at the 2025 state election, but lost to the Nationals' Scott Leary, trailing narrowly on first preferences.

Dr Brough declined to comment.

The ABC understands a link to the State Administrative Tribunal's decision will appear on Dr Brough's entry in the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency's register of practitioners.

World.title: Police use of force under review after 63yo woman pushed to ground
World.content:
Police in Western Australia are reviewing whether use of force was justified after a video appeared to show an officer push an older Indigenous woman to the ground in the state's north.

The altercation happened outside a block of units in Karratha on Tuesday morning, and led to four people being charged, including the woman herself.

The video does not show what led up to Beverley Hubert, 63, being pushed to the ground by one of the officers.

However, Ms Hubert said she and other family members intervened after police arrived at the units to arrest her 33-year-old nephew, an arrest she alleged was heavy-handed.

Her nephew is facing a string of charges including criminal damage and reckless driving.

Police in Karratha appear to push a woman to the ground. (Supplied)

"We sort of got up and went towards them, rushing towards them, I was dawdling across because I didn't have a walker, but I managed to walk across slowly," she said.

"That bloke walked up, telling me to back off. [He] pushed me over."

Ms Hubert said she fell on her backside and her head hit the gravel, although the camera pans away from her at that point.

The video also showed people being pepper sprayed, as well as another woman pushing the same police officer as Ms Hubert remains on the ground.

Swearing and verbal abuse directed at police can be heard, as well as a woman identifying herself as the woman's daughter, saying Ms Hubert was a dialysis patient.

Police to review incident

In a statement, WA police said they called an ambulance after a 63-year-old woman fell over, but she declined their assistance.

She has been charged with assaulting a public officer, as well as two other women aged 31 and 56.

Pepper spray was used by police during the incident. (Supplied)

A police spokesperson said officers utilise "a range of less lethal tactical options to support officers in resolving incidents safely while minimising harm"

"Police are trained to apply the minimum force necessary and to continually reassess and de-escalate where possible.

" Any use of force must be justified, proportionate and necessary in the circumstances, and is subject to mandatory reporting and review. "

The 33-year-old man who was arrested was facing four charges and two additional charges were laid after the incident, including obstructing a police officer.

World.title: Text messages and DNA led to arrest of accused murderer, ACT police say
World.content:
Court documents have revealed how text messages, DNA and an undercover police operation led to the arrest of a man accused of killing a woman and setting fire to her flat in Canberra's north.

Warning: This story contains graphic details.

Jack Henry Curtin, 27, was arrested and charged with murder and arson earlier this week over the death of 46-year-old Kylee McHugh.

Ms McHugh's body was found in her burning ground floor unit in Belconnen on May 18.

The police statement of facts says investigators found a string of text messages between Ms McHugh and a phone number allegedly used by Mr Curtin in the days before her death.

"You smoked my weed replace it," one message read.

"Go buy some weed to replace mine or prepare yourself when you come back don't come back not expecting nothing to happen."

Fire crews arrived to find Ms McHugh's ground-floor unit alight. (ABC News: Caitlin Maloney)

Ms McHugh replied "I have not stolen anything from you" and "I don't need to", according to the statement of facts.

People who knew Ms McHugh told officers a couple had been staying at her unit in May, but the pair accused her of stealing their cannabis, and so she had kicked them out.

A woman with Ms McHugh's mobile number later called Triple-Zero seeking help to evict the couple from her apartment.

"If I don't have assistance getting them out, there's going to be a blood bath," the caller said.

Ms McHugh also called ACT Housing about evicting the couple, who told her she would need to call police.

"Once I do that, my life becomes a threat, my life becomes a threat," Ms McHugh said.

CCTV allegedly shows accused near murder scene

Telecommunication service data showed a phone with the number allegedly used by Mr Curtin in the Belconnen area on the night before and morning of the fire, before being turned off.

The phone was later found by members of the public before being seized by police.

Man charged with murder after house fire ACT police are accusing a 27-year-old man of murdering Canberra woman Kylee McHugh before setting her home on fire.

CCTV footage also allegedly showed Mr Curtin in the Belconnen area near Ms McHugh's unit complex on May 17.

Mr Curtin was also allegedly seen near the unit complex at around 3:30am on the morning of the fire, and again an hour later.

Officers spoke to Mr Curtin in the days after the blaze, when he told them he'd recently lost his phone and bought a new one.

"I know more events about Kylee … That chick just died and burn up to a crisp," he allegedly said.

The court documents say DNA obtained from Mr Curtin couldn't be excluded from samples taken from Ms McHugh's remains.

Jack Henry Curtin, 27, was arrested and charged with murder and arson over Kylee McHugh's death. (Supplied: ACT Policing)

The forensic pathologist said believed she died before the fire took hold, finding blunt force injuries to her neck and head with "compression of the larynx likely being the major contributor to death".

Firefighters found five seats of fire, including some with "ignitable liquid pour patterns" around the unit.

In July, police launched an undercover sting during which Mr Curtin allegedly made admissions about the murder and arson.

When he was arrested on Monday, the documents say he made no admissions about his alleged crimes.

On being in the area at the time, he told police he had observed a "glow" at Ms McHugh's flat and returned later to see the unit on fire.

Mr Curtin has not entered any pleas and was remanded in custody.

The case will return to court next month.
