Tech.title: Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Apple Watch Ultra 4: Clash of the Newest Apple Watches
Tech.content:
At its Surprise & Shine event on Sept. 9, Apple revealed its newest devices, including its latest smartwatches. Here’s how the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 compare.

The new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are premium wearables running the company’s WatchOS 27 software, which have plenty of features that interact with paired iPhones and a growing number that work even when apart (handy when out on a run). The Series 12 is the standard model, while the Ultra 4 is the higher-end version with more durability and features.

This year, the Apple Watches got more software upgrades than hardware upgrades, but one important thing that didn’t change with either was the price. Whereas the iPhones all got price bumps (even the older models Apple still sells), the Apple Watch Series 12 still starts at $400 and the Apple Watch Ultra 4 at $800. Both models can be preordered now and ship on Sept. 18.

Note that while the Ultra 4 only has its titanium finish (and can be pricier with fancier bands), the Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $400 for 42mm in aluminum finish, jumps to $699 for titanium and tops out at $899 for its new ceramics case material.

Here’s how Apple’s latest smartwatches compare.

Apple/CNET $399 (Save with trade-in) Apple Watch Series 12 at Best Buy Get it now See at Best Buy Expert Take The latest 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 is available for preorder at Best Buy for $399. If you have an older device, you can trade it in for a new one at a lower price. Every purchase also comes with up to four free months of Apple Fitness and three free months of Apple Music.

Apple/CNET From $799 (Save with freebies) Apple Watch Ultra 4 at Best Buy Get it now See at Best Buy Expert Take The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is available for preorder at Best Buy for $799. The preorder comes with a few freebies, including four free months of Apple Fitness Plus and three free months of Apple Music. You can choose to pick it up in store on the release date or have it shipped to arrive by the release date, so you can start using your new watch as soon as it’s released.

Design and display

The Apple Watch Series 12 looks practically identical to its predecessor, the Apple Watch Series 11 released in 2025, with a rectangular OLED display (up to 2,000 nits brightness) and rounded edges. The 42mm and 46mm sizes return along with aluminum and titanium body versions — as well as a new ceramic material (returning from the Apple Watch 5 in 2019) that adds a hair more size and about 10g of weight. For a comparison, the 42mm aluminum model is 32.2g, the titanium is 36.5g and the pearl white color of ceramic is 41.7g (the night blue hue of ceramic is 42.8g).

The Apple Watch Series 12 comes in a variety of colors depending on the case material. For aluminum, you can pick between dark bronze, light gold, black and space gray. Titanium comes in radiant gold and natural hues, while the ceramic comes in pearl white and night blue.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 in both colors with different watch bands. Vanessa Hand Orellana/CNET

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 likewise looks identical to its predecessor, with a larger, rectangular OLED Retina display that stretches flat to the watch’s edges. It still only comes in the 49mm size and titanium body. The bigger size makes room for a customizable Action button. The Ultra 4 comes in natural and black case colors.

The sensor array on the underside of both watches has been redesigned to increase the surface area for readings, but most folks won’t notice — until they realize the watch can take heart rate readings every 5 seconds, compared to roughly every 5 minutes on older models.

Both watches are rated IP6X for dust resistance, but while the Apple Watch Series 12 is water resistant to 50 meters — “swimproof,” according to Apple — the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is water resistant to 100 meters and rated for recreational scuba diving to 40 meters. It’s also tested to MIL-STD 81H to continue functioning at altitude, in high and low temperatures, frozen and thawed, in ice and freezing rain and through shock and vibration.

Given how similar the models are to their predecessors, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the superior model in display size and durability, surviving more extreme conditions. At literally twice the base price of the Apple Watch Series 12, though, you’ll be paying for this privilege.

The Apple Watch Series 12, in gold titanium (left) and bronze aluminum (right). Vanessa Hand Orellana/CNET

Specs and battery life

Both watches run the S11 chip, the newest Apple wearable silicon that enables features such as the every-5-second heart rate readings. They also have 64GB of onboard storage apiece, which can be used to save music and other media or app data such as hiking trails, though a good portion is reserved for the operating system.

Battery life is another area in which the watches strongly diverge. Apple shares battery life estimates rather than battery capacities. The Apple Watch Series 12 lasts about 24 hours, or 38 hours in Low Power Mode. The Ultra 4 extends its lead over its predecessor, offering up to 50 hours of battery life, compared with 42 hours for the Ultra 3. That can be expanded up to 84 hours on Low Power mode.

While both watches have Low Power modes to last longer in the day, the Ultra 4 has two additional versions specifically tuned for workouts. The Extended Workout mode can track a workout for up to 25 hours by shutting off the always-on display and the running-form metrics while still tracking GPS and heart rate. If somehow 25 hours isn’t enough, there’s a Max Extended Workout mode that lasts up to 48 hours, though the tradeoff is dropping from multiband to single-band GPS and slowing heart rate readings to a 5-minute average instead of sampling live (you also can’t use custom workouts, get alerts or split the exercise).

Similarly, Apple doesn’t share wattage specs for its smartwatch chargers, but when using the company’s proprietary fast charger, the Series 12 can go from 0% to 80% in 30 minutes, while it takes the Ultra 4 around 45 minutes to hit the same percentage.

While both of Apple’s latest watches are almost equally powerful, the Ultra 4 beats the Series 12 by a landslide when it comes to battery life. According to Apple, the premium model can last about two days between charges — roughly twice as long as the Series 12. This is likely due to the Ultra 4’s larger battery.

The Apple Watch Series 12 on either side, with the Apple Watch Ultra 4 in the middle. Screenshot by CNET/Apple

AI and software

Both watches come with WatchOS 27, the latest version of Apple’s operating system at the time of their launch. New features include Siri AI, which CNET principal writer Vanessa Hand-Orellana found to be “miles ahead of traditional Siri.”

New to both watches is Audio Intelligence, a suite of AI-powered features that uses their microphones to continuously analyze surrounding sounds. For instance, Live Rewind allows you to press the digital crown to see a transcription of the last 15 seconds of conversation around you, and in early testing, it was able to pick out voices pretty well. Another feature, Siri Recap, detects conversations throughout the day or at set times to generate summaries or notes — say, for work meetings — which can be triggered manually or scheduled ahead of time. Apple says it’s designed the features so audio isn’t stored on the device and only keeps transcripts the wearer chooses, but it’s already spurred some privacy concerns.

Upgraded sensors on both watches allow them to take readings more often, sampling how your body is doing across various metrics. This is mined and represented in a new Readiness score, which represents how well your body recovers from exercise over the course of the day. The Vitals app also has a new Daytime toggle that allows you to compare your health metrics throughtout the day to compare with the usual overnight measurements.

Both watches also get a redesigned Health app with AI insights and biometrics provied in daily summaries, which replicate findings from other wearables such as the Fitbit Air and Oura. It’s also gotten a more comprehensive health test to measure VO2 max and mobility, which is done in combination with the cameras on a paired iPhone.

While both watches can be connected to cellular service (the Series 12 must be purchased in the 4G LTE version), the Ultra 4 inherits its predecessor’s capability for 5G connectivity as well as linking up to satellites to contact emergency services when outside mobile network range. The premium watch also has fall detection and crash detection.

Those last emergency connectivity features should give the Ultra 4 the edge over the Series 12, but virtually every other software and AI feature is shared between the smartwatches.

Live Rewind on the Apple Watch generates a transcription of what was said during the last 15 seconds around you. Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Which watch should you pick?

Which smartwatch you pick between the Series 12 and the Ultra 4 is an easier decision than it might seem, as the more premium option is twice the price of the most affordable configuration of the Series 12. The two watches share nearly all the same features, so only the most serious athletes need consider the more expensive model.

If you have $800 to spend, the decision becomes tougher. Of the Ultra 4’s handful of advantages over the Series 12, the one you’ll likely appreciate most is its longer battery life. Charging a standard Apple Watch every day can be tedious, and if you forget to top it up at the end of the day, it may not last through the night. That makes it tough for the Series 12 to measure health and sleep metrics while you’re snoozing.

The Ultra 4 is the obvious choice for outdoorsy folks with deep enough pockets, as it’s more rugged, can survive in deeper waters and has satellite connectivity to help when running into trouble off the grid or away from your phone.

That said, both smartwatches improve on their predecessors and are excellent options for anyone seeking a watch that works seamlessly with an iPhone.

Tech.title: You Can Now Buy the Trump Phone for $250 More Than Originally Priced
Tech.content:
After Apple’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, which debuted the long-rumored foldable iPhone Duo with a starting price of $1,999, the conversation at my home has mainly centered on our mobile phone expenses and whether it’s worth upgrading.

Well, good news: There is a flashy phone on the market that is cheaper than the hyped-up foldable. OK, there are many well below that price, but do they operate on an outdated operating system? Are they painted gold?

Ring the alarms and throw the confetti; I am talking about Trump Mobile’s golden T1 Phone.



The gold-colored mobile device was originally priced at an affordable $499. Due to a quiet price hike the provider implemented overnight, as first reported by The Verge, the Trump phone is now marked at $749. That’s a $250 increase, making the T1 a more expensive option over the iPhone 17E. Control your excitement.

A Trump Mobile spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

Trump Mobile didn’t explain the cost increase, but the writing has been on the wall for some time. The company’s execs went on record earlier this year with The Verge that the initial $499 price tag was a temporary introductory price. It’s even possible for the T1 to become more expensive, with a price of up to $999 in the future. So, you know, embrace this price while you can.

That said, the company didn’t provide any firm explanation beyond that, leading us to speculate that this could be due to the ongoing global memory chip shortage driven by the AI boom, known as RAMageddon. Apple recently implemented an array of price hikes due to the RAM shortage, upping the price of its older iPhone lineup, iPads, MacBooks and more.

But the Trump phone isn’t in the same ballpark as an iPhone. In fact, the Trump phone is essentially a reskinned mid-level HTC handset.

This might be the worst possible shade of gold. Corinne Reichert/CNET

After an almost year-long delay, the Android phone, originally advertised as made in the US, began shipping in May to members of the media, which included CNET (you can read the full review here), along with a few customers (who paid a preorder deposit of $100 for the device).

Once CNET’s experts were able to take a closer look at the T1, which is now labeled as being “assembled in the USA,” we confirmed what iFixit learned before us: The Trump phone was likely manufactured in Guangdong, China, and is nearly identical to the Taiwanese HTC U24 Pro. The latter handset was released to market two years ago and can be found for less than $600 at retailers such as Walmart and Amazon.

But are those HTC handsets I mentioned above painted gold? Do they come equipped with Truth Social on an outdated OS, while their casings are decorated with an American flag missing some stripes? I think not.

So, if you’re still in the market for Trump Mobile’s T1 phone, I advise you to get while the getting’s good. Before we know it, the Trump phone could be priced at around $1,000. I’m all for retro tech and nostalgia, but for all the outdated tech this phone is built on, that price tag is pushing it when newer phones on the market, sporting more impressive bells and whistles, are clocking in at a price that’s way lower.

Tech.title: Jell-O and Beer May Hold the Keys to Brewing Houses on Mars
Tech.content:
Establishing life on another planet is a multifaceted process with many problems. Housing is one major challenge, but a new study suggests researchers have found a way to build living quarters on Mars using materials already present on the planet, along with a couple of other clever ingredients.

The study, published on Sept. 10 in the journal Chem Circularity, reports that researchers found a way to turn the sand on Mars into what is functionally low-grade concrete using little more than gelatin, yeast, and the natural Martian environment. Combine the three ingredients, and the dry, cold, low-pressure environment of Mars freeze-dries the mixture, turning it into a porous, foam-like material strong enough to build houses on the red planet.

“My inspiration came from freeze-dried fruits that become harder,” senior author Jishen Qiu of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology said in a statement. “So, I asked myself if we can take advantage of that and make some materials.”

According to Qiu, the concrete produced by this method measures 10 to 12 megapascals (a metric unit of pressure), putting it on par with low-grade concrete here on Earth. This concrete is strong enough to build a one- or two-story house on Earth, and since Earth has three times the gravity of Mars, it’s more than strong enough to build structures on Mars too.

The gelatin is run-of-the-mill porcine gelatin, which means it’s made from pigs, and it’s quite literally the same stuff that Jell-O uses to make its jiggly dessert. For the yeast, Qiu created a specially engineered version covered in the same proteins mussels use to attach themselves to rocks. These two ingredients, along with pounded-up Martian rocks and water, create the material.

Mars’ frigid cold, low-pressure environment effectively freeze-dries the material, causing water to sublimate, which means it turns directly from a solid to a vapor, leaving the Martian concrete behind. Because this process is so fast, items must be 3D-printed in real time to work properly.

The team tested it by 3D printing two small beehive-shaped structures about the size of a wine cork in a simulated Martian environment, but the team believes the process can scale up. Once the structures have reached the end of their usefulness, people on Mars can break them down, mix them in a bioreactor, and brew a new building with the same materials, as long as there’s still yeast alive to reproduce.

An elegant solution to a long-standing problem

Houses on Mars made with this method would resemble beehives, but be made of what is essentially concrete. Nin Liu

Delivering humans to Mars is already a tall order. Elon Musk tried to get it done by 2025 and missed the mark by at least a decade. However, getting people there is only half the battle. Once there, they need a place to live that can withstand the Martian environment, which includes temperature swings of nearly 100 degrees Celsius and virtually no radiation protection from the sun due to the thin Mars atmosphere.

There are many ideas about the subject, ranging from inflatable domiciles to the idea of letting self-propagating fungi grow whole buildings. Some enterprising scientists from the Indian Space Research Organisation even made space bricks from Martian soil, guar gum, urea, nickel chloride and a bacterium called Sporosarcina pasteurii, which converts urea and calcium into calcite. This lets the soil harden into something resembling concrete.

NASA held a habitat challenge from 2015 to 2019 that tasked companies and researchers to 3D-print homes using unique methods and materials. The winners took home over $2 million in prizes. In short, no stone has been left unturned, and people are using all sorts of exotic materials to try to find the best solution for habitats on Mars, including Qiu.

“I always ask myself: Is there any physical law or fundamental mechanism that prevents us from doing this?” Qiu said. “I can’t see any at this point in time. We are confident in scaling it up. It would surprise me if materials for future Martian engineering will not be as diverse as those used in Earth engineering, and biology will certainly contribute.”

Tech.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: The Highest-End Phones Compared
Tech.content:
Apple’s $1,299 iPhone 18 Pro Max now stands tall as the company’s newest nonfolding high-end flagship phone. Announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, it packs big camera and battery upgrades. But with a starting price that’s $100 higher than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, the phone’s 256GB model is now priced closely to Samsung’s $1,300 Galaxy S26 Ultra.

While every iPhone received a $100 price increase that’s likely influenced by the ongoing RAM shortage, Apple’s topline iPhone appears to be a close rival to the S26 Ultra in several key areas, especially when it comes to battery life and cameras.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra design and display

While Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max and Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra are big phones, their design aesthetics are quite different. The 18 Pro Max sports a similar aluminum unibody design to the one that debuted on last year’s 17 Pro Max. It comes in burgundy red, glacier blue, silver and black colors. Its shape gives it a hefty appearance, but one that fits in well when the phone is being used as a professional camera for events like Apple TV’s Major League Baseball broadcasts. And at 249 grams (8.8 ounces), the 18 Pro Max isn’t lightweight by any stretch. The phone has a 6.8-inch OLED display that should be quite expansive for videos, websites and games.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra has a slightly bigger 6.9-inch AMOLED display, but at 214 grams, it’s notably lighter than the iPhone 18 Pro Max. It also comes in six colors: pink gold, silver shadow, cobalt violet, sky blue, white and black. The S26 Ultra is also the thinnest in its line, but its Privacy Display is its most unique feature. The S26 Ultra’s display can make specific apps or notifications difficult to see from off-angle viewing, making it easier to hide content from prying eyes without needing to apply a privacy screen protector. No other company has replicated Samsung’s Privacy Display, which does make the phone stand out.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max in glacier blue. Apple/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra battery capacity

Both phones have big batteries. While Apple doesn’t disclose its battery specs in the US — instead citing that it can play 45 hours of video — its Ireland website claims the physical SIM edition will have a 5,391-mAh capacity. That’s slightly higher than the 5,000-mAh capacity on the S26 Ultra and might be even higher on the eSIM model that will be sold in the US.

Apple hasn’t yet disclosed the charging speed for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but this is an area where Samsung already excels — the S26 Ultra has 60-watt wired charging and won our CNET Lab Test award for fastest wired charging phone by recharging from 0% to 76% in 30 minutes. That said, last year’s iPhone 17 Pro Max had a 40-watt charging speed that was one of our top performers, recharging 0% to 69% in the same 30-minute test. We look forward to testing out the 18 Pro Max to see how it fares.

You can turn on Privacy Display in Quick Settings to prevent others from seeing what’s on your screen. Celso Bulgatti/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra cameras

Both phones also have their respective companies’ highest-end cameras, with Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max now featuring a variable-aperture camera that can physically open or close to take better photos in darker or lighter environments. This feature comes with the Pro Max’s three-camera setup that includes a 49-megapixel wide camera, a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera and a 48-megapixel telephoto camera with a 4x optical zoom. While the S26 Ultra doesn’t include a variable aperture, it has four cameras on the back that include a 200-megapixel main camera, a 50-megapixel ultrawide, a 50-megapixel telephoto with a 5x optical zoom and a 10-megapixel telephoto with a 3x optical zoom.

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra processor, features

Apple’s A20 Pro processor powers the company’s latest AI features, headlined by the new Siri AI assistant that is built with Apple’s collaboration with Google’s Gemini. It can help you look up specific information buried in your emails and texts and turn them into actionable items like new reminders or calendar events. Apple also made a point of showing off the A20 Pro’s gaming abilities and how the phone’s vapor chamber helps keep it running cool while pushing intensive graphics.

But Samsung’s phone includes Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 for Galaxy processor, powering its own slate of Galaxy AI features focused on proactive suggestions, along with photo editing. It’s also quite capable of high-end gaming.

Check out the specs below to compare both phones further.

Tech.title: Over 153 Million Driver’s Licenses Were Stolen by Hackers. Here’s What to Know
Tech.content:
If you’ve used your driver’s license to verify your information either in the real world or online, there’s a chance that some of your driver’s license information was stolen by hackers in a security breach against the ID verification giant IDScan that was reportedly active for a year.

“On or around Sept. 1, 2026, IDScan.net received information indicating that certain data may have been accessed without authorization,” IDScan said in a statement on Sept. 4. “Upon this discovery, we took immediate steps to secure our systems and engaged a team of third-party specialists to help determine the full nature and scope of the incident.”

The hack is discussed in more detail by Brian Krebs, a security researcher who runs the website Krebs on Security. He says he was first made aware of the breach after a source alerted him to a post on a Russian cybercrime forum from a hacker offering digital scans of identity documents for more than 170 million people from a service called Nexus.

Krebs was able to access Nexus and verify that it did indeed have the documents it said it had, including a scan of his own driver’s license.

The data includes 153 million driver’s licenses, 10 million ID cards, 3 million travel documents like passports and, according to Krebs, “at least 579,000” medical cards. Most of these records are for US residents, but about 1.1 million Canadian driver’s licenses were also found.

Per IDScan, hackers weren’t able to get every piece of information from those documents, but most likely obtained full names, driver’s license numbers and government-issued ID numbers.

The hackers who ran Nexus boasted that they had obtained the information by “continuously exfiltrating new data for over a year” into a private database from “a major identity verification company.”

The data collected likely came from a range of sources. Krebs says the leak of his information could have resulted from renting a car from Hertz, which uses IDScan to verify driver’s licenses. Other companies that use IDScan include FedEx, Target, GameStop and over 1,000 cannabis dispensaries, car rental agencies and gun shops across 19 states. IDScan reported that it scanned 150 million IDs in 2024 alone.

The New Orleans field office of the FBI is investigating the matter. The FBI has not responded to a request for comment.

Here’s what you can do

IDScan says it will notify everyone who was affected by the breach and “provide access to free credit monitoring and identity protection services” for those people. If you end up being one of them, IDScan says to contact it at 1-833-516-2980 (Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET) to enroll in those services.

Those concerned they may have been affected have a few options. The easiest and quickest is a credit freeze, which makes it much more difficult for cybercriminals to open new accounts in your name. CNET has a guide for that if you need help. Freezing your credit is free, but it requires you to set up individual accounts with the three major credit bureaus.

Since cybercrime can strike anywhere and at any time, it’s also good to follow some tips to keep yourself safe, including using strong passwords, familiarizing yourself with the latest AI-powered phishing scams and considering using a VPN to help obfuscate your online presence so you can’t be tracked.

The unfortunate reality is that cybersecurity breaches are getting bigger, and companies are telling consumers less about what’s happening, so it’s worth staying vigilant, even if your driver’s license wasn’t stolen.

Tech.title: Ninja Takes on Caraway With Cheaper, ‘More Durable’ Ceramic Cookware
Tech.content:
One thing about Ninja, the company is going to keep its customer base happy with new release after new release. On the heels of launching its first water filter, the HydraSense, Ninja’s first-ever ceramic-coated cookware is now available, too.

The cookware is dishwasher-safe and oven-safe up to 550 degrees Fahrenheit. The pieces are stackable for easy storage, and the handles on the lids can be pushed down to save even more space. Ninja says the ceramic cookware is twice as durable as competitor Caraway, but the company didn’t share what type of testing, if any, was conducted to support that claim. We also haven’t gotten our hands on the Ninja NeverQuit lineup yet to independently test its durability or do a side-by-side comparison with Caraway or other ceramic cookware.

However, Ninja’s new cookware is more affordable than Caraway. The NeverQuit three-piece frying pan set is $250 while Caraway’s three frying pans with lids set is currently available for $395.

Ceramic-coated cookware is often favored because it’s nonstick, easy to clean and can be made without chemicals typically used in non-stick cookware, such as PTFE (Teflon). Ninja says the NeverQuit coating is “designed without lead, cadmium, PFAS, PFOA, PTFE or hard anodization.”

It is available in a three-, six- or 12-piece set. The 12-piece set includes 8-inch and 10.25-inch frying pans, a 4-quart pan with lid, a steamer basket, a spatula, a pasta ladle, a 6-quart stock pot with lid, a 6-quart metal strainer basket and a spoon rest.

Ninja also teased an upcoming stainless-steel cookware line named “Ninja Eversear,” but hasn’t announced a launch date just yet.
